title.zh: 卷二十七 志第十七 符瑞上
title.raw: 卷二十七 志第十七 符瑞上 Volume 27 Treatises 17: Auspicious Signs 1

meta.sourceNote: ChineseNotes scrape had source glyph artifacts; chapter body imported from Wikisource after ChineseNotes glossary scrape.

sentences.zh: 夫體睿窮幾，含靈獨秀，謂之聖人，所以能君四海而役萬物，使動植之類，莫不各得其所。

translations.literal: Those who embody sagacity and fathom the subtlest patterns, bearing the spirit in unique excellence — these are called sages; thereby they can rule the four seas and employ the ten thousand things, so that moving and rooted kinds alike each attain their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: One who unites profound wisdom with insight into hidden causes, and stands alone in spiritual excellence, is called a sage. Such a person can govern all within the seas and put the myriad creatures to use, so that both animals and plants each find their rightful place.

sentences.zh: 百姓仰之，歡若親戚，芬若椒蘭，故為旗章輿服以崇之，玉璽黃屋以尊之，以神器之重，推之於兆民之上，自中智以降，則萬物之為役者也。

translations.literal: The common people look up to them, rejoicing as toward kin, fragrant as pepper or orchid; therefore banners, emblems, and chariot-robes are fashioned to honor them, jade seals and yellow canopies to exalt them; by the weight of the sacred vessel they are raised above the myriad people — from middling intelligence downward, these are those employed by the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: The people look up to them with the joy one feels for close kin, drawn as by the scent of pepper and orchid. Hence flags, insignia, and ceremonial dress are made to honor them, jade seals and the imperial yellow canopy to magnify them. By the weight of the sacred regalia they are set above the myriad masses; from ordinary intelligence downward, they are the ones who serve the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 性識殊品，蓋有愚暴之理存焉。

translations.literal: Nature and knowledge differ in grade; presumably the principle of folly and violence exists therein.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature and understanding vary in degree; within this difference lies the root of foolishness and brutality.

sentences.zh: 見聖人利天下，謂天下可以為利，見萬物之歸聖人，謂之利萬物。

translations.literal: Seeing that sages benefit the world, they suppose the world may be turned to profit; seeing that the ten thousand things submit to the sage, they call it profiting the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: When they see that the sage benefits the realm, they imagine the realm itself can be mined for profit; when they see the myriad things yield to the sage, they call it benefiting the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 力爭之徒，至以逐鹿方之，亂臣賊子，所以多於世也。

translations.literal: Those who strive by force even liken it to the contest for the deer; rebellious ministers and wicked sons — hence they abound in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Men who fight for power even compare their struggle to the race for the central plain; treacherous ministers and wicked heirs are therefore so numerous in the world.

sentences.zh: 夫龍飛九五，配天光宅，有受命之符，天人之應。

translations.literal: Now when the dragon flies to the fifth and ninth lines, matching Heaven and illuminating the dwelling, there are tokens of received mandate — the response of Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: When the dragon ascends to sovereignty, aligning with Heaven and bringing light to the realm, there appear signs of a received mandate — the mutual response of Heaven and humanity.

sentences.zh: 易曰：「河出圖，洛出書，而聖人則之。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "The River brings forth the Chart, the Luo brings forth the Writ, and the sage takes them as his model.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "When the Yellow River yields the Chart and the Luo River yields the Writ, the sage models himself upon them.

sentences.zh: 」符瑞之義大矣。

translations.literal: " The meaning of auspicious tokens is indeed great.
translations.idiomatic: " The significance of portents and felicitous signs is profound indeed.

sentences.zh: 上古

translations.literal: High Antiquity
translations.idiomatic: High Antiquity

sentences.zh: 赫胥、燧人之前，無聞焉。

translations.literal: Before [the eras of] He-Xu and Suiren, nothing is heard.
translations.idiomatic: Before the times of He-Xu and Suiren, nothing is recorded.

sentences.zh: 太昊帝宓犧氏，母曰華胥。

translations.literal: The Great August Emperor Fu Xi, his mother was called Hua Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The Great August Emperor Fu Xi — his mother was named Hua Xu.

sentences.zh: 燧人之世，有大迹出雷澤，華胥履之，而生伏犧於成紀。

translations.literal: In the age of Suiren, a great footprint appeared at Lei Marsh; Hua Xu trod upon it and bore Fu Xi at Chengji.
translations.idiomatic: During the age of Suiren, a great footprint emerged at Lei Marsh. Hua Xu stepped upon it and gave birth to Fu Xi at Chengji.

sentences.zh: 蛇身人首，有聖德。

translations.literal: Serpent body, human head — he possessed sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His body was that of a serpent, his head that of a man, and he possessed sage virtue.

sentences.zh: 燧人氏沒，宓犧代之，受龍圖，畫八卦，所謂「河出圖」者也。

translations.literal: When Suiren perished, Fu Xi replaced him, received the Dragon Chart, drew the Eight Trigrams — this is what is called "the River brings forth the Chart."
translations.idiomatic: After Suiren passed away, Fu Xi succeeded him, received the Dragon Chart, and drew the Eight Trigrams — the event known as "the River brings forth the Chart."

sentences.zh: 有景龍之瑞。

translations.literal: There was the auspicious sign of the Luminous Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: The portent of the Luminous Dragon appeared.

sentences.zh: 炎帝神農氏，母曰女登，遊於華陽，有神龍首感女登於常羊山，生炎帝。

translations.literal: The Flame Emperor Shen Nong, his mother was called Nü Deng; traveling at Huayang, a divine dragon's head moved Nü Deng at Mount Changyang, and she bore the Flame Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Flame Emperor Shen Nong — his mother was Nü Deng. While traveling at Huayang, a divine dragon's head touched her on Mount Changyang, and she gave birth to the Flame Emperor.

sentences.zh: 人身牛首，有聖德，致大火之瑞。

translations.literal: Human body, ox head — he possessed sagely virtue and brought forth the auspicious sign of the Great Fire.
translations.idiomatic: His body was human, his head that of an ox. He possessed sage virtue and brought about the portent of the Great Fire.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾生，醴泉出。

translations.literal: Fine grain grew; sweet spring water issued forth.
translations.idiomatic: Excellent grain appeared, and sweet spring water welled up.

sentences.zh: 黃帝軒轅氏，母曰附寶，見大電光繞北斗樞星，照郊野，感而孕。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor Xuan Yuan, his mother was called Fu Bao; she saw great lightning encircle the Pivot Star of the Northern Dipper, illuminating the outskirts, and conceived through this influence.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor Xuan Yuan — his mother was Fu Bao. She beheld great lightning coil around the Pivot Star of the Northern Dipper, lighting the countryside, and conceived through this encounter.

sentences.zh: 二十五月而生黃帝於壽丘。

translations.literal: After twenty-five months she bore the Yellow Emperor at Shouqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five months later she gave birth to the Yellow Emperor at Shouqiu.

sentences.zh: 弱而能言，龍顏，有聖德，劾百神朝而使之。

translations.literal: While still young he could speak; dragon countenance — he possessed sagely virtue and compelled the hundred spirits to attend court and serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Even in infancy he could speak. His face was like a dragon's, and he possessed sage virtue, commanding the hundred spirits to attend him and do his bidding.

sentences.zh: 應龍攻蚩尤，戰虎、豹、熊、羆四獸之力。

translations.literal: The Responsive Dragon attacked Chiyou, fighting with the strength of the four beasts — tiger, leopard, bear, and brown bear.
translations.idiomatic: The Responsive Dragon assailed Chiyou, wielding the power of the four beasts — tiger, leopard, bear, and grizzly.

sentences.zh: 以女魃止淫雨。

translations.literal: By means of Nü Ba he halted the excessive rain.
translations.idiomatic: He deployed Nü Ba to stop the torrential rains.

sentences.zh: 天下既定，聖德光被，羣瑞畢臻。

translations.literal: When the world was settled, sagely virtue spread its radiance, and all auspicious signs arrived in full.
translations.idiomatic: Once the realm was pacified, his sage virtue shone across the land, and every felicitous portent appeared.

sentences.zh: 有屈軼之草生於庭，佞人入朝，則草指之，是以佞人不敢進。

translations.literal: There was the Qu-Yi grass growing in the courtyard; when flatterers entered court, the grass pointed at them — thus flatterers dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Qu-Yi grass grew in the courtyard. Whenever a sycophant entered court, the grass pointed at him, so that flatterers dared not come forward.

sentences.zh: 有景雲之瑞，有赤方氣與青方氣相連，赤方中有兩星，青方中有一星，凡三星，皆黃色，以天清明時見於攝提，名曰景星。

translations.literal: There was the auspicious sign of the Luminous Cloud: red vapor and green vapor joined; within the red were two stars, within the green one star — three stars in all, all yellow, visible at Sheti when the sky was clear — called the Luminous Star.
translations.idiomatic: The portent of the Luminous Cloud appeared: red qi and green qi connected. Within the red region were two stars, within the green one star — three stars in all, all yellow, visible near Sheti when the sky was clear. This was called the Luminous Star.

sentences.zh: 黃帝黃服齋于中宮，坐于玄扈洛水之上，有鳳皇集，不食生蟲，不履生草，或止帝之東園，或巢于阿閣，或鳴於庭，其雄自歌，其雌自舞。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor, in yellow robes, fasted in the central palace and sat upon the dark ford of the Luo River; phoenixes gathered, not eating living insects, not treading living grass; some rested in the emperor's eastern garden, some nested in the lofty pavilion, some called in the courtyard — the males sang of themselves, the females danced of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor, clad in yellow and fasting in the central palace, sat by the dark ford of the Luo River. Phoenixes gathered, refusing living insects for food and living grass underfoot. Some alighted in the emperor's eastern garden, some nested in the lofty pavilion, some sang in the courtyard — the males sang on their own, the females danced on their own.

sentences.zh: 麒麟在囿，神鳥來儀。

translations.literal: The qilin was in the park; divine birds came to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: The qilin appeared in the royal park, and divine birds came to present their homage.

sentences.zh: 有大螻如羊，大螾如虹。

translations.literal: There were great ants like sheep, great earthworms like rainbows.
translations.idiomatic: Great ants appeared as large as sheep, and great earthworms as vast as rainbows.

sentences.zh: 黃帝以土氣勝，遂以土德王。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor, because earth qi prevailed, thereupon took the Earth Virtue and became king.
translations.idiomatic: Because the power of earth qi prevailed, the Yellow Emperor adopted the virtue of Earth and ascended as king.

sentences.zh: 五十年秋七月庚申，天霧三日三夜，晝昏。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, autumn, seventh month, day gengshen — heaven fog for three days and three nights, day dim.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year, on the gengshen day of the seventh month in autumn, fog shrouded the sky for three days and three nights, and daylight turned dim.

sentences.zh: 黃帝以間天老、力牧、容成曰：「於公何如？

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor questioned Tian Lao, Li Mu, and Rong Cheng, saying: "What of this, gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor asked Tian Lao, Li Mu, and Rong Cheng: "What do you make of this, gentlemen?

sentences.zh: 」天老曰：「臣聞之，國安，其主好文，則鳳皇居之。

translations.literal: " Tian Lao said: "Your servant has heard that when the state is at peace and its ruler loves culture, the phoenix dwells there.
translations.idiomatic: " Tian Lao replied: "I have heard that when the state is secure and its ruler favors culture, the phoenix will dwell there.

sentences.zh: 國亂，其主好武，則鳳皇去之。

translations.literal: When the state is in turmoil and its ruler loves warfare, the phoenix departs.
translations.idiomatic: When the state falls into chaos and its ruler favors warfare, the phoenix departs.

sentences.zh: 今鳳皇翔於東郊而樂之，其鳴音中夷則，與天相副。

translations.literal: Now the phoenix soars at the eastern suburbs and delights in it; its cry strikes the Yize pitch — it matches Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Now the phoenix soars at the eastern suburbs in evident joy; its cry strikes the Yize pitch, harmonizing with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 以是觀之，天有嚴教以賜帝，帝勿犯也。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, Heaven has stern instruction to bestow upon the emperor — the emperor must not transgress it.
translations.idiomatic: From this we may see that Heaven has sent a solemn teaching to the emperor; Your Majesty must not violate it.

sentences.zh: 」乃召史卜之，龜燋。

translations.literal: " He then summoned the scribe to divine by tortoise — the shell burned.
translations.idiomatic: " He then summoned the scribe to perform a tortoise divination, and the shell burned up.

sentences.zh: 史曰：「臣不能占也。

translations.literal: The scribe said: "Your servant cannot divine this.
translations.idiomatic: The scribe said: "I cannot divine this matter.

sentences.zh: 其問之聖人。

translations.literal: Ask the sage about it.
translations.idiomatic: You must consult the sage.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「已問天老、力牧、容成矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I have already asked Tian Lao, Li Mu, and Rong Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "I have already asked Tian Lao, Li Mu, and Rong Cheng.

sentences.zh: 」史北面再拜曰：「龜不違聖智，故燋。

translations.literal: " The scribe, facing north, bowed twice and said: "The tortoise does not oppose sagely wisdom — therefore it burned.
translations.idiomatic: " The scribe bowed twice toward the north and said: "The tortoise would not contradict sage wisdom — that is why it burned.

sentences.zh: 」霧除，遊于洛水之上，見大魚，殺五牲以醮之，天乃甚雨，七日七夜，魚流於海，得圖、書焉。

translations.literal: " When the fog cleared, he traveled upon the Luo River and saw a great fish; he slaughtered the five sacrificial animals to offer libation to it. Heaven then sent heavy rain for seven days and seven nights; the fish flowed to the sea, and he obtained the Chart and the Writ.
translations.idiomatic: " When the fog lifted, he went to the Luo River and saw a great fish. He sacrificed the five animals to offer libation, whereupon Heaven sent torrential rain for seven days and seven nights. The fish drifted out to sea, and he obtained the Chart and the Writ.

sentences.zh: 龍圖出河，龜書出洛，赤文篆字，以授軒轅。

translations.literal: The Dragon Chart came forth from the River, the Tortoise Writ from the Luo — red characters in seal script — and were bestowed upon Xuan Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Dragon Chart emerged from the River and the Tortoise Writ from the Luo, inscribed in red seal characters, and were bestowed upon Xuan Yuan.

sentences.zh: 軒轅接萬神於明庭，今寒門谷口是也。

translations.literal: Xuan Yuan received the myriad spirits at the Bright Court — present-day Hanmen Valley Mouth is the place.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Yuan received the myriad spirits at the Bright Court — the site of present-day Hanmen Valley Mouth.

sentences.zh: 帝摯少昊氏，母曰女節，見星如虹，下流華渚，既而夢接意感，生少昊。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhi, the Lesser August Shao Hao clan — his mother was called Nü Jie; she saw a star like a rainbow descend to flow upon Hua Zhu, then dreamed of union and conceived through spiritual influence, bearing Shao Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhi of the Lesser August Shao Hao clan — his mother was Nü Jie. She saw a star like a rainbow descend upon Hua Zhu, then dreamed of union and conceived through divine influence, giving birth to Shao Hao.

sentences.zh: 登帝位，有鳳皇之瑞。

translations.literal: When he ascended the imperial throne, there was the auspicious sign of the phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Upon ascending the throne, the portent of the phoenix appeared.

sentences.zh: 帝顓頊高陽氏，母曰女樞，見瑤光之星，貫月如虹，感己於幽房之宮，生顓頊於若水。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanxu of the Gaoyang clan — his mother was called Nü Shu; she saw the Yaoguang star pierce the moon like a rainbow, was moved within the palace of the secluded chamber, and bore Zhuanxu at Ruoshui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuanxu of the Gaoyang clan — his mother was Nü Shu. She saw the Yaoguang star pierce the moon like a rainbow, conceived in the palace of the secluded chamber, and gave birth to Zhuanxu at Ruoshui.

sentences.zh: 首戴干戈，有聖德。

translations.literal: He wore helm and weapon upon his head — he possessed sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He bore helm and weapon upon his head and possessed sage virtue.

sentences.zh: 生十年而佐少昊氏，二十而登帝位。

translations.literal: At ten years of age he assisted the Shao Hao clan; at twenty he ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of ten he assisted the Shao Hao clan; at twenty he ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝嚳高辛氏，生而駢齒，有聖德，代高陽氏王天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Ku of the Gaoxin clan — born with double teeth, possessing sagely virtue — he replaced the Gaoyang clan and ruled all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ku of the Gaoxin clan was born with double teeth and possessed sage virtue. He succeeded the Gaoyang clan and ruled all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 使鼓人拊鞞鼓，擊鍾磬，鳳皇鼓翼而舞。

translations.literal: He had the drummer strike the hand-drum and beat bells and chimes — the phoenix beat its wings and danced.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the drummer to beat the hand-drum and strike the bells and chimes, and the phoenix flapped its wings and danced.

sentences.zh: 帝堯之母曰慶都，生於斗維之野，常有黃雲覆護其上。

translations.literal: Emperor Yao's mother was called Qingdu; born in the wilds of Douwei, yellow clouds constantly covered and sheltered her above.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao's mother was Qingdu. Born in the wilds of Douwei, she was constantly sheltered beneath yellow clouds.

sentences.zh: 及長，觀于三河，常有龍隨之。

translations.literal: When she grew up, observing at the Three Rivers, a dragon constantly followed her.
translations.idiomatic: When she grew to maturity and visited the Three Rivers, a dragon constantly followed her.

sentences.zh: 一旦龍負圖而至，其文要曰：「亦受天祐。

translations.literal: One day a dragon came bearing a chart upon its back; its text in essence read: "You too shall receive Heaven's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: One day a dragon arrived bearing a chart on its back. Its essential text read: "You too shall receive Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: 」眉八彩，鬢髮長七尺二寸，面銳上豐下，足履翼宿。

translations.literal: " Eyebrows of eight colors, temples and hair seven feet two inches long, face sharp above and full below, feet treading upon Wings Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: " Her eyebrows were eight-colored, her temples and hair seven feet two inches long, her face tapering above and full below, her feet resting upon the Wings Lodge constellation.

sentences.zh: 既而陰風四合，赤龍感之。

translations.literal: Presently yin winds joined from the four quarters; the red dragon moved her through spiritual influence.
translations.idiomatic: Then yin winds gathered from all four quarters, and the red dragon touched her through divine influence.

sentences.zh: 孕十四月而生堯於丹陵，其狀如圖。

translations.literal: She was pregnant fourteen months and bore Yao at Danling — his form matched the chart.
translations.idiomatic: After fourteen months of pregnancy she gave birth to Yao at Danling, and his appearance matched the chart.

sentences.zh: 及長，身長十尺，有聖德，封於唐。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his body was ten feet tall, possessing sagely virtue; he was enfeoffed at Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew to manhood, he stood ten feet tall, possessed sage virtue, and was enfeoffed at Tang.

sentences.zh: 夢攀天而上。

translations.literal: He dreamed of climbing Heaven and ascending.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of climbing up to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 高辛氏衰，天下歸之。

translations.literal: The Gaoxin clan declined; all under Heaven submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: As the Gaoxin clan waned, the realm submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 在帝位七十年，景星出翼，鳳皇在庭，朱草生，嘉禾秀，甘露潤，醴泉出，日月如合璧，五星如連珠。

translations.literal: On the imperial throne for seventy years — the Luminous Star appeared at Wings, the phoenix was in the courtyard, cinnabar grass grew, fine grain flourished, sweet dew moistened, sweet spring water issued forth, sun and moon like joined jades, the five stars like strung pearls.
translations.idiomatic: During his seventy years on the throne, the Luminous Star appeared at Wings, the phoenix nested in the courtyard, cinnabar grass sprang up, excellent grain flourished, sweet dew fell, sweet spring water welled forth, the sun and moon shone like joined jades, and the five planets aligned like pearls on a string.

sentences.zh: 厨中自生肉，其薄如箑，搖動則風生，食物寒而不臭，名曰「箑脯」。

translations.literal: In the kitchen meat grew of itself, thin as a fan; when shaken wind arose; food was cold yet not foul — called "Fan-Dried Meat."
translations.idiomatic: In the kitchen, meat grew of its own accord, thin as a fan. When shaken it produced a breeze; the food was cool yet never spoiled. It was called "Fan-Dried Meat."

sentences.zh: 又有草夾階而生，月朔始生一莢，月半而生十五莢，十六日以後，日落一莢，及晦而盡，月小則一莢焦而不落，名曰「蓂莢」，一曰「曆莢」。

translations.literal: There was also grass growing beside the steps: on the first of the month one pod appeared; at mid-month fifteen pods; after the sixteenth, one pod fell each day until at month's end all were gone; in a short month one pod withered but did not fall — called "Ming Pod," also called "Calendar Pod."
translations.idiomatic: Another grass grew along the steps. On the first day of the month one pod appeared; by mid-month there were fifteen pods. After the sixteenth, one pod fell each day until the month ended. In a short month one pod withered but did not fall. It was called the "Ming Pod," also known as the "Calendar Pod."

sentences.zh: 歸功於舜，將以天下禪之，乃潔齋修壇塲於河、雒，擇良日，率舜等升首山，遵河渚。

translations.literal: He attributed merit to Shun and was about to yield the realm to him in abdication; he purified himself, fasted, and prepared the altar-ground at the He and Luo, chose an auspicious day, led Shun and others to ascend Mount Shou, and followed the river's islets.
translations.idiomatic: Attributing his achievements to Shun, he prepared to abdicate the realm to him. He purified himself, fasted, and built an altar at the He and Luo rivers, chose an auspicious day, led Shun and his party up Mount Shou, and followed the river's islets.

sentences.zh: 有五老游焉，蓋五星之精也。

translations.literal: Five elders wandered there — presumably the essences of the Five Stars.
translations.idiomatic: Five elders appeared there — presumably the essences of the Five Stars.

sentences.zh: 相謂曰：「河圖將來告帝以期，知我者重瞳黃姚。

translations.literal: They said to one another: "The River Chart is about to come and inform the emperor of the appointed time; he who knows us is Double-Pupil Yellow Yao."
translations.idiomatic: They said to one another: "The River Chart is about to arrive and tell the emperor of the appointed time. He who knows us is Double-Pupil of Yellow Yao."

sentences.zh: 」五老因飛為流星，上入昴。

translations.literal: " The five elders thereupon flew away as shooting stars, ascending into Mao.
translations.idiomatic: " The five elders then flew away as shooting stars, ascending into the Mao constellation.

sentences.zh: 二月辛丑昧明，禮備，至於日昃，榮光出河，休氣四塞，白雲起，回風搖，乃有龍馬銜甲，赤文綠色，臨壇而止，吐甲圖而去。

translations.literal: Second month, day xinchou, at dawn the rites were complete; by the time the sun declined, glorious light came forth from the river, auspicious qi filled the four quarters, white clouds rose, whirlwinds swayed — then a dragon-horse came bearing armor, red text on green ground, halted at the altar and stopped, spat out the armored chart and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the second month at dawn, the rites were complete. By sunset glorious light emerged from the river, auspicious qi filled the four quarters, white clouds rose, and whirlwinds stirred. Then a dragon-horse appeared bearing armor inscribed in red on green ground. It halted at the altar, spat out the armored chart, and departed.

sentences.zh: 甲似龜，背廣九尺，其圖以白玉為檢，赤玉為字，泥以黃金，約以青繩。

translations.literal: The armor resembled a tortoise, its back nine feet wide; the chart used white jade as its case, red jade for its characters, sealed with yellow gold, bound with green cord.
translations.idiomatic: The armor resembled a tortoise shell, nine feet wide on its back. The chart used white jade for its case and red jade for its characters, sealed with yellow gold and bound with green cord.

sentences.zh: 檢文曰：「闓色授帝舜。

translations.literal: The case text read: "The opening color bestows the emperor upon Shun.
translations.idiomatic: The text on the case read: "The opening color bestows the imperial mandate upon Shun.

sentences.zh: 」言虞、夏、殷、周、秦、漢當授天命。

translations.literal: " It stated that Yu, Xia, Yin, Zhou, Qin, and Han would each receive the Mandate of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " It declared that Yu, Xia, Yin, Zhou, Qin, and Han would each receive the Mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 帝乃寫其言，藏于東序。

translations.literal: The emperor then copied its words and stored them in the eastern wing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor copied its text and stored it in the eastern wing.

sentences.zh: 後二年二月仲辛，率羣臣沈璧于洛。

translations.literal: Two years later, second month, mid-xin, he led the host of ministers to sink a jade disk in the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, on the mid-xin day of the second month, he led his ministers to sink a jade disk in the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，退俟，至于下昃，赤光起，玄龜負書而出，背甲赤文成字，止于壇。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, he withdrew to wait; by late afternoon red light arose, a dark tortoise came bearing a writ upon its back — red characters formed on its shell — and halted at the altar.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, he withdrew to wait. By late afternoon red light appeared, and a dark tortoise emerged bearing a writ on its back, red characters inscribed on its shell. It halted at the altar.

sentences.zh: 其書言當禪舜。

translations.literal: The writ stated that he should abdicate to Shun.
translations.idiomatic: The writ declared that he should abdicate to Shun.

sentences.zh: 遂讓舜。

translations.literal: He thereupon yielded to Shun.
translations.idiomatic: He then abdicated in favor of Shun.

sentences.zh: 帝舜有虞氏，母曰握登，見大虹意感，而生舜於姚墟。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun of the Youyu clan — his mother was called Wodeng; she saw a great rainbow and conceived through spiritual influence, bearing Shun at Yaoxu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun of the Youyu clan — his mother was Wodeng. She saw a great rainbow, conceived through divine influence, and gave birth to Shun at Yaoxu.

sentences.zh: 目重瞳子，故名重華。

translations.literal: His eyes had double pupils — hence he was named Double Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: His eyes had double pupils, hence his name Double Splendor.

sentences.zh: 龍顏大口，黑色，身長六尺一寸。

translations.literal: Dragon countenance, large mouth, black in color, body six feet one inch in height.
translations.idiomatic: His face was like a dragon's, his mouth large, his complexion dark, and he stood six feet one inch tall.

sentences.zh: 舜父母憎舜，使其塗廩，自下焚之，舜服鳥工衣服飛去。

translations.literal: Shun's father and mother hated Shun; they made him plaster the granary and set fire to it from below — Shun, wearing bird-craft garments, flew away.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's parents despised him. They made him repair the granary and then set fire to it from below. Shun, clad in bird-craft garments, flew away.

sentences.zh: 又使浚井，自上填之以石，舜服龍工衣自傍而出。

translations.literal: They also made him dig a well and filled it with stones from above — Shun, wearing dragon-craft garments, emerged from the side.
translations.idiomatic: They also made him dig a well and filled it with stones from above. Shun, clad in dragon-craft garments, emerged from the side.

sentences.zh: 耕於歷山，夢眉長與髮等。

translations.literal: While plowing at Mount Li, he dreamed his eyebrows were as long as his hair.
translations.idiomatic: While farming at Mount Li, he dreamed that his eyebrows were as long as his hair.

sentences.zh: 及即帝位，蓂莢生於階，鳳皇巢於庭，擊石拊石，百獸率舞，景星出房，地出乘黃之馬，西王母獻白環、玉玦。

translations.literal: When he ascended the imperial throne, Ming pods grew on the steps, the phoenix nested in the courtyard; striking stones and clapping stones, the hundred beasts led the dance; the Luminous Star appeared at Chamber, the earth produced the horse Cheng Huang; the Queen Mother of the West presented a white ring and jade tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Upon ascending the throne, Ming pods grew on the steps and the phoenix nested in the courtyard. When stones were struck, the hundred beasts led the dance. The Luminous Star appeared at Chamber, the earth produced the horse Cheng Huang, and the Queen Mother of the West presented a white ring and jade tablet.

sentences.zh: 舜在位十有四年，奏鍾石笙筦未罷，而天大雷雨，疾風發屋拔木，桴鼓播地，鍾磬亂行，舞人頓伏，樂正狂走。

translations.literal: Shun had been on the throne fourteen years; bells, stones, pipes, and flutes had not yet ceased when Heaven sent great thunder and rain, fierce winds tore off roofs and uprooted trees, drumsticks and drums were scattered upon the ground, bells and chimes ran in disorder, dancers fell prostrate, the music master ran about in frenzy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Shun's reign, while bells, stones, pipes, and flutes were still sounding, Heaven sent a great thunderstorm. Fierce winds tore off roofs and uprooted trees. Drumsticks and drums were scattered across the ground, bells and chimes fell into disarray, dancers collapsed prostrate, and the music master fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 舜乃擁璿持衡而笑曰：「明哉！

translations.literal: Shun then embraced the scepter and held the balance and laughed, saying: "How clear!
translations.idiomatic: Shun then embraced the scepter, held the balance, and laughed, saying: "How clear!

sentences.zh: 夫天下非一人之天下也，亦乃見于鍾石笙筦乎。

translations.literal: The realm is not the realm of a single man — has this not also been shown in bells, stones, pipes, and flutes?
translations.idiomatic: The realm does not belong to one man alone — has this not been revealed even in the sounding of bells, stones, pipes, and flutes?

sentences.zh: 」乃薦禹於天，使行天子事。

translations.literal: " He then recommended Yu to Heaven and had him perform the Son of Heaven's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He then recommended Yu to Heaven and had him perform the duties of the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 于時和氣普應，慶雲興焉，若煙非煙，若雲非雲，郁郁紛紛，蕭索輪囷，百工相和而歌慶雲。

translations.literal: At that time harmonious qi responded everywhere; celebratory clouds arose — like smoke yet not smoke, like clouds yet not clouds, lush and profuse, swirling in coils — the hundred craftsmen joined in harmony and sang the Celebratory Cloud.
translations.idiomatic: At that time harmonious qi responded throughout the land, and celebratory clouds arose — like smoke yet not smoke, like clouds yet not clouds, lush and swirling. The hundred craftsmen joined in harmony and sang the Celebratory Cloud.

sentences.zh: 帝乃倡之曰：「慶雲爛兮，糾縵縵兮。

translations.literal: The emperor then led the song, saying: "Celebratory clouds blaze; tangled and billowing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then led the song: "Celebratory clouds blaze bright, tangled and billowing.

sentences.zh: 日月光華，旦復旦兮。

translations.literal: Sun and moon shed their radiance — dawn upon dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon shed their radiance — dawn upon dawn.

sentences.zh: 」羣臣咸進，稽首曰：「明明上天，爛然星陳。

translations.literal: " The host of ministers all advanced, bowing their heads and saying: "Brilliant is High Heaven, blazing with stars arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: " All the ministers advanced, bowed their heads, and said: "Brilliant is High Heaven, blazing with stars arrayed.

sentences.zh: 日月光華，弘予一人。

translations.literal: Sun and moon shed their radiance — enlarge me, the solitary one.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon shed their radiance — enlarge me, the solitary one.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃再歌曰：「日月有常，星辰有行。

translations.literal: " The emperor then sang again: "Sun and moon have their constancy, stars and planets have their courses.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sang again: "Sun and moon have their constancy, stars and planets have their courses.

sentences.zh: 四時從經，萬姓允誠。

translations.literal: The four seasons follow the canon; the myriad people are truly sincere.
translations.idiomatic: The four seasons follow their proper order; the myriad people are truly sincere.

sentences.zh: 於予論樂，配天之靈。

translations.literal: In my discourse on music, I match the spirit of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In my discourse on music, I harmonize with the spirit of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 遷于聖賢，莫不咸聽。

translations.literal: Turning to the sage and worthy — none do not all heed.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to the sage and worthy — all heed without exception.

sentences.zh: 鼚乎鼓之，軒乎舞之。

translations.literal: Thunderously drum it; loftily dance it.
translations.idiomatic: Thunderously beat the drums; loftily perform the dance.

sentences.zh: 精華以竭，褰裳去之。

translations.literal: Essence and splendor are exhausted — lift the robe and depart.
translations.idiomatic: Essence and splendor are spent — lift the robe and depart.

sentences.zh: 」於是八風修通，慶雲叢聚，蟠龍奮迅於其藏，蛟魚踊躍於其淵，龜鼈咸出其穴，遷虞而事夏。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the eight winds were harmoniously open, celebratory clouds gathered in clusters; coiled dragons exerted themselves swiftly in their lairs, flood-dragons and fish leaped in their depths, tortoises and turtles all emerged from their holes — he moved from Yu to serve Xia.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the eight winds flowed in harmony, celebratory clouds gathered in clusters. Coiled dragons stirred swiftly in their lairs, flood-dragons and fish leaped in their depths, tortoises and turtles emerged from their holes — and he transferred from Yu to serve Xia.

sentences.zh: 舜乃設壇於河，依堯故事。

translations.literal: Shun then set up an altar at the River, following Yao's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Shun then established an altar at the River, following Yao's precedent.

sentences.zh: 至于下昃，榮光休氣至，黃龍負圖，長三十二尺，廣九尺，出于壇畔，赤文綠錯，其文言當禪禹。

translations.literal: By late afternoon, glorious light and auspicious qi arrived; a yellow dragon bore the chart, thirty-two feet long and nine feet wide, emerging beside the altar — red text on green ground — its words stating that he should abdicate to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: By late afternoon, glorious light and auspicious qi arrived. A yellow dragon bore the chart, thirty-two feet long and nine feet wide, emerging beside the altar with red characters on green ground. Its text declared that Shun should abdicate to Yu.

sentences.zh: 三代

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dynasties

sentences.zh: 帝禹有夏氏，母曰脩己，出行，見流星貫昴，夢接意感，既而吞神珠。

translations.literal: Emperor Yu of the Youxia clan — his mother was called Xiuji; while traveling abroad she saw a shooting star pierce Mao, dreamed of union and conceived through spiritual influence, then swallowed a divine pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yu of the Youxia clan — his mother was Xiuji. While traveling she saw a shooting star pierce the Mao constellation, dreamed of union, conceived through divine influence, and swallowed a divine pearl.

sentences.zh: 脩己背剖，而生禹於石紐。

translations.literal: Xiuji's back split open and she bore Yu at Shiniu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuji's back split open, and she gave birth to Yu at Shiniu.

sentences.zh: 虎鼻大口，

translations.literal: Tiger nose, large mouth,
translations.idiomatic: Tiger nose, large mouth,

sentences.zh: 〈虎鼻大口　各本並脫「大」字，據元龜四四、御覽八二引帝王世紀補。〉

translations.literal: (Tiger nose, large mouth — all editions omit the character "large"; supplied according to Yuan Gui 44 and Taiping Yulan 82 citing Diwang Shiji.)
translations.idiomatic: (Tiger nose, large mouth — all editions omit the character "large"; this reading is restored from Yuan Gui 44 and Taiping Yulan 82, which cite the Diwang Shiji.)

sentences.zh: 兩耳參鏤，首戴鉤鈐，胸有玉斗，足文履己，故名文命。

translations.literal: Both ears intricately carved, upon his head he wore Gouling, on his chest a jade dipper, on his feet the pattern Li-ji — hence he was named Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: His ears were intricately carved, he wore Gouling upon his head, a jade dipper on his chest, and the pattern Li-ji on his feet — hence his name Wenming.

sentences.zh: 長有聖德。

translations.literal: When grown he possessed sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew to manhood, he possessed sage virtue.

sentences.zh: 長九尺九寸，夢自洗於河，以手取水飲之。

translations.literal: Nine feet nine inches tall; he dreamed of bathing himself in the river and drinking water scooped up in his hands.
translations.idiomatic: He stood nine feet nine inches tall. He dreamed of bathing in the river and drinking water scooped up in his hands.

sentences.zh: 又有白狐九尾之瑞。

translations.literal: There was also the auspicious sign of the white fox with nine tails.
translations.idiomatic: The portent of the white fox with nine tails also appeared.

sentences.zh: 當堯之世，舜舉之。

translations.literal: In Yao's age, Shun recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: During the age of Yao, Shun recommended him.

sentences.zh: 禹觀於河，有長人白面魚身，出曰：「吾河精也。

translations.literal: Yu observed at the River; a tall man with white face and fish body emerged, saying: "I am the spirit of the River.
translations.idiomatic: While observing the River, Yu saw a tall figure with a white face and fish body emerge, saying: "I am the spirit of the River.

sentences.zh: 」呼禹曰：「文命治淫。

translations.literal: " He called to Yu: "Wenming, control the floods.
translations.idiomatic: " He called to Yu: "Wenming, control the floods.

sentences.zh: 」言訖，授禹河圖，言治水之事，乃退入于淵。

translations.literal: " When he had spoken, he gave Yu the River Chart, spoke of controlling the waters, then withdrew into the depths.
translations.idiomatic: " Having spoken, he gave Yu the River Chart and instructed him on controlling the waters, then withdrew into the depths.

sentences.zh: 禹治水既畢，天錫玄珪，以告成功。

translations.literal: When Yu had finished controlling the waters, Heaven bestowed a dark jade tablet to announce his success.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu had finished controlling the waters, Heaven bestowed a dark jade tablet to proclaim his success.

sentences.zh: 夏道將興，草木暢茂，青龍止於郊，祝融之神，降于崇山。

translations.literal: The Way of Xia was about to rise; grass and trees flourished luxuriantly; the green dragon halted at the suburbs; the spirit of Zhurong descended upon Mount Chong.
translations.idiomatic: As the Way of Xia was about to rise, grass and trees flourished luxuriantly. The green dragon halted at the suburbs, and the spirit of Zhurong descended upon Mount Chong.

sentences.zh: 乃受舜禪，即天子之位。

translations.literal: He thereupon received Shun's abdication and assumed the Son of Heaven's throne.
translations.idiomatic: He then received Shun's abdication and ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 洛出龜書六十五字，是為洪範，此謂「洛出書」者也。

translations.literal: The Luo brought forth the Tortoise Writ of sixty-five characters — this is the Great Plan — this is what is called "the Luo brings forth the Writ."
translations.idiomatic: The Luo brought forth the Tortoise Writ of sixty-five characters, which became the Great Plan — the event known as "the Luo brings forth the Writ."

sentences.zh: 南巡狩，濟江，中流有二黃龍負舟，舟人皆懼。

translations.literal: On a southern tour of inspection, crossing the river, midstream two yellow dragons bore up the boat — all aboard were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: On a southern tour of inspection, while crossing the river, two yellow dragons bore up the boat midstream, and all aboard were terrified.

sentences.zh: 禹笑曰：「吾受命於天，屈力以養人。

translations.literal: Yu laughed and said: "I have received the mandate from Heaven and bend my strength to nourish the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yu laughed and said: "I have received Heaven's mandate and bend my strength to nourish the people.

sentences.zh: 生，性也。

translations.literal: Life is one's nature.
translations.idiomatic: Life is one's nature.

sentences.zh: 死，命也。

translations.literal: Death is one's fate.
translations.idiomatic: Death is one's fate.

sentences.zh: 奚憂龍哉！

translations.literal: Why worry about dragons!
translations.idiomatic: Why should I fear dragons!

sentences.zh: 」龍於是曳尾而逝。

translations.literal: " The dragons thereupon dragged their tails and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " The dragons then dragged their tails and departed.

sentences.zh: 高辛氏之世妃曰簡狄，以春分玄鳥至之日，從帝祀郊禖，與其妹浴於玄丘之水。

translations.literal: In the age of Gaoxin, a consort named Jiandi — on the day of the spring equinox when the dark bird arrives, she followed the Emperor in sacrificing at the suburban Mound of Birth, and with her sister bathed in the waters of Xuansqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Gaoxin, there was a consort named Jiandi. On the spring equinox, when the dark bird arrives, she followed the emperor to sacrifice at the suburban Mound of Birth and bathed with her sister in the waters of Xuansqiu.

sentences.zh: 有玄鳥銜卵而墜之，五色甚好，二人競取，覆以玉筐。

translations.literal: A dark bird came carrying an egg and dropped it — of five colors, very fine; the two women competed to take it and covered it with a jade basket.
translations.idiomatic: A dark bird flew down carrying an egg and dropped it. The egg was finely colored in five hues. The two women raced to pick it up and covered it with a jade basket.

sentences.zh: 簡狄先得而吞之，遂孕。

translations.literal: Jiandi got it first and swallowed it, and thereupon conceived.
translations.idiomatic: Jiandi reached it first, swallowed it, and conceived.

sentences.zh: 胸剖而生契。

translations.literal: Her chest split open and she bore Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Her chest split open, and she gave birth to Xie.

sentences.zh: 長為堯司徒，成功於民，受封于商。

translations.literal: When grown he became Yao's Minister over the Masses, achieved success for the people, and received enfeoffment at Shang.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew to manhood, he became Yao's Minister over the Masses, achieved success for the people, and received a fief at Shang.

sentences.zh: 後十三世，生主癸。

translations.literal: Thirteen generations later, Zhugui was born.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen generations later, Zhugui was born.

sentences.zh: 主癸之妃曰扶都，見白氣貫月，意感，以乙日生湯，號天乙。

translations.literal: Zhugui's consort was called Fudu; she saw white qi pierce the moon, was moved in her heart, and on a yi day bore Tang — styled Tianyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhugui's consort was Fudu. She saw a white vapor pierce the moon and conceived through spiritual influence. On a yi day she bore Tang, who was styled Tianyi.

sentences.zh: 豐下銳上，晳而有髥，句身而揚聲，身長九尺，臂有四肘，是曰殷湯。

translations.literal: Full below and sharp above, fair-skinned with a beard, body bent yet voice resounding — nine feet tall, arms with four elbows — this was Tang of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He was full below and sharp above, fair-skinned with a beard, his body slightly bent yet his voice resounding. He stood nine feet tall, his arms had four elbows, and he was known as Tang of Yin.

sentences.zh: 湯在亳，能修其德。

translations.literal: Tang was at Bo and was able to cultivate his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ruled from Bo and cultivated his virtue.

sentences.zh: 伊摯將應湯命，夢乘船過日月之傍，湯乃東至于洛，觀帝堯之壇，沈璧退立，黃魚雙踴，黑鳥隨魚止于壇，化為黑玉。

translations.literal: Yi Yin was about to answer Tang's mandate and dreamed of sailing a boat past the sun and moon; Tang then went east to the Luo, viewed Emperor Yao's altar, sank a jade disk and withdrew to stand — two yellow fish leaped in pairs, a black bird followed the fish and halted at the altar, transforming into black jade.
translations.idiomatic: As Yi Yin was about to answer Tang's mandate, he dreamed of sailing a boat past the sun and moon. Tang then traveled east to the Luo River, visited Emperor Yao's altar, sank a jade disk, and withdrew to stand aside. Two yellow fish leaped together, a black bird followed the fish to the altar, and changed into black jade.

sentences.zh: 又有黑龜，並赤文成字，言夏桀無道，湯當代之。

translations.literal: There was also a black tortoise, with red script forming characters, stating that Jie of Xia was without the Way and Tang should replace him.
translations.idiomatic: A black tortoise also appeared, bearing red characters that declared Jie of Xia devoid of the Way and Tang destined to replace him.

sentences.zh: 檮杌之神，見于邳山。

translations.literal: The spirit of Taowu appeared at Mount Pi.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit of Taowu appeared on Mount Pi.

sentences.zh: 有神牽白狼銜鉤而入商朝。

translations.literal: A spirit led a white wolf carrying a hook into the court of Shang.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit led a white wolf bearing a hook into the court of Shang.

sentences.zh: 金德將盛，銀自山溢。

translations.literal: The Metal Virtue was about to flourish; silver overflowed from the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: As the Metal Virtue was about to flourish, silver overflowed from the mountains.

sentences.zh: 湯將奉天命放桀，夢及天而舓之，遂有天下。

translations.literal: Tang was about to follow Heaven's mandate and release Jie; he dreamed of reaching Heaven and traversing it, and thereupon possessed the realm under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: As Tang prepared to follow Heaven's mandate and banish Jie, he dreamed of reaching Heaven and passing through it — and so he came to possess the realm.

sentences.zh: 商人後改天下之號曰殷。

translations.literal: The people of Shang later changed the name of the realm under Heaven to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shang later changed the name of the realm to Yin.

sentences.zh: 高辛氏之世妃曰姜嫄，助祭郊禖，見大人迹履之，當時歆如有人道感己，遂有身而生男。

translations.literal: In the age of Gaoxin, a consort named Jiang Yuan — assisting at the suburban sacrifice to the Mound of Birth, she saw a great man's footprint and trod in it; then and there she was moved as though by a human Way affecting her, and conceived and bore a male child.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Gaoxin, there was a consort named Jiang Yuan. While assisting at the suburban sacrifice to the Mound of Birth, she saw a great man's footprint and stepped in it. She was suddenly moved as though touched by a human presence, conceived, and bore a son.

sentences.zh: 以為不祥，棄之阨巷，羊牛避而不踐；

translations.literal: Deeming it inauspicious, she abandoned him in a narrow lane — sheep and cattle avoided him and would not tread upon him;
translations.idiomatic: Thinking him ill-omened, she abandoned him in a narrow alley. Sheep and cattle avoided him and would not step on him;

sentences.zh: 又送之山林之中，會伐林者薦覆之；

translations.literal: She sent him again into the mountains and forests; woodcutters happened to cover him with brushwood;
translations.idiomatic: She sent him again into the forest, where woodcutters happened to cover him with brushwood;

sentences.zh: 又取而置寒冰上，大鳥來以一翼藉覆之。

translations.literal: She took him again and placed him on frozen ice; a great bird came and covered him with one wing.
translations.idiomatic: She took him again and set him on the frozen ice. A great bird came and sheltered him beneath one wing.

sentences.zh: 姜嫄以為異，乃收養焉，名之曰棄。

translations.literal: Jiang Yuan considered this extraordinary and thereupon took him in to raise; she named him Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan saw this as a marvel and took him in to raise. She named him Qi.

sentences.zh: 枝頤有異相。

translations.literal: His jaw projected — he had an unusual appearance.
translations.idiomatic: His projecting jaw gave him an unusual appearance.

sentences.zh: 長為堯稷官，有功於民。

translations.literal: When grown he became Yao's minister of grain and had merit for the people.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew to manhood, he served as Yao's minister of grain and achieved merit for the people.

sentences.zh: 后稷之孫曰公劉，有德，諸侯皆以天子之禮待之。

translations.literal: Hou Ji's grandson was called Gong Liu — possessing virtue, the feudal lords all treated him with the rites due the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ji's grandson was Gong Liu. Endowed with virtue, the feudal lords all treated him with the rites due a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 初黃帝之世，讖言曰：「西北為王，期在甲子，昌制命，發行誅，旦行道。

translations.literal: In the first age of the Yellow Emperor, a prognostic saying ran: "He who is king in the northwest — his term comes in the jiazi cycle; Chang controls the mandate, Fa carries out punishment, Dan walks the Way."
translations.idiomatic: In the age of the Yellow Emperor, a prophecy said: "He who will be king in the northwest — his time comes in the jiazi cycle. Chang will hold the mandate, Fa will carry out punishment, and Dan will walk the Way."

sentences.zh: 」及公劉之後，十三世而生季歷。

translations.literal: " Thirteen generations after Gong Liu, Jili was born.
translations.idiomatic: " Thirteen generations after Gong Liu, Jili was born.

sentences.zh: 季歷之十年，飛龍盈於殷之牧野，此蓋聖人在下位將起之符也。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jili, flying dragons filled the pasture lands of Yin — this was likely the omen of a sage in a low station about to rise.
translations.idiomatic: In Jili's tenth year, flying dragons filled the pastures of Yin. This was the omen of a sage in humble station about to rise.

sentences.zh: 季歷之妃曰太任，夢長人感己，溲于豕牢而生昌，是為周文王。

translations.literal: Jili's consort was called Tai Ren; she dreamed a tall man affected her, and while relieving herself in the pigsty she bore Chang — this was King Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jili's consort was Tai Ren. She dreamed that a tall figure touched her, and while relieving herself in the pigsty she bore Chang — who became King Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 龍顏虎肩，身長十尺，胸有四乳。

translations.literal: Dragon countenance, tiger shoulders, body ten feet long, chest with four nipples.
translations.idiomatic: He had a dragon-like face and tiger-like shoulders, stood ten feet tall, and had four nipples on his chest.

sentences.zh: 太王曰：「吾世當有興者，其在昌乎！

translations.literal: The Grand King said: "In my generation there should be one who rises — could it be Chang!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand King said: "Our line is destined to rise in my generation — surely it is Chang!

sentences.zh: 」季歷之兄曰太伯，知天命在昌，適越終身不反。

translations.literal: " Jili's elder brother was called Taibo; knowing Heaven's mandate rested with Chang, he went to Yue and never returned in his lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: " Jili's elder brother Taibo, knowing Heaven's mandate rested with Chang, went to Yue and never returned.

sentences.zh: 弟仲雍從之，故季歷為嗣以及昌。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhongyong followed him, so Jili became the successor and the succession reached Chang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhongyong followed him, so Jili became the heir and the succession passed to Chang.

sentences.zh: 昌為西伯，作邑于豐。

translations.literal: Chang became the Western Earl and founded his settlement at Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Chang became the Western Earl and established his capital at Feng.

sentences.zh: 文王之妃曰太姒，夢商庭生棘，太子發植梓樹於闕間，化為松栢棫柞。

translations.literal: King Wen's consort was called Taisi; she dreamed thorns grew in the court of Shang — the heir apparent Fa planted a catalpa tree between the gate towers, which transformed into pine, cypress, oak, and zha trees.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen's consort Taisi dreamed that thorns sprang up in the Shang court. The crown prince Fa planted a catalpa between the gate towers, and it transformed into pine, cypress, oak, and zha trees.

sentences.zh: 以告文王，文王幣告羣臣，與發並拜告夢。

translations.literal: She told King Wen; King Wen made offerings and announced it to the assembled ministers; he and Fa bowed together in reporting the dream.
translations.idiomatic: She told King Wen, who made offerings and announced the dream to his ministers. He and Fa bowed together in reporting it.

sentences.zh: 季秋之甲子，赤爵銜書及豐，止于昌戶，昌拜稽首受之。

translations.literal: On a jiazi day in late autumn, a red sparrow bearing a writ arrived at Feng, halting at Chang's door; Chang bowed prostrate and received it.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiazi day in late autumn, a red sparrow bearing a writ arrived at Feng and stopped at Chang's door. Chang bowed prostrate to receive it.

sentences.zh: 其文要曰：「姬昌，蒼帝子，亡殷者紂王。

translations.literal: Its text in essence said: "Ji Chang, son of the Azure Emperor — King Zhou is the one who will bring ruin to Yin."
translations.idiomatic: Its text in essence read: "Ji Chang, son of the Azure Emperor — King Zhou is the one who will bring ruin to Yin."

sentences.zh: 」將畋，史徧卜之，曰：「將大獲，非熊非羆，天遺汝師以佐昌。

translations.literal: " About to hunt, the historian Bian divined for him, saying: "You will gain greatly — neither bear nor brown bear; Heaven sends you a teacher to assist Chang."
translations.idiomatic: " When he was about to go hunting, the historian Bian divined and said: "You will make a great catch — neither bear nor brown bear. Heaven sends you a teacher to assist Chang."

sentences.zh: 臣太祖史疇為禹卜畋，得臯陶。

translations.literal: Your servant's founding ancestor, the historian Chou, divined for Yu on a hunt and obtained Gao Yao.
translations.idiomatic: My founding ancestor, the historian Chou, once divined for Yu on a hunt and obtained Gao Yao.

sentences.zh: 其兆如此。

translations.literal: The omen was like this.
translations.idiomatic: The omen will be just like that.

sentences.zh: 」王至于磻谿之水，呂尚釣於涯，王下趨拜曰：「望公七年，乃今見光景于斯。

translations.literal: " The king arrived at the waters of Panxi; Lü Shang was fishing on the bank; the king came down in haste and bowed, saying: "For seven years I have looked for you, sir — only now do I see your radiance here."
translations.idiomatic: " The king arrived at the waters of Panxi, where Lü Shang was fishing on the bank. The king hurried down and bowed, saying: "For seven years I have sought you, sir — only now do I behold your radiance here."

sentences.zh: 」尚立變名答曰：「望釣得玉璜，其文要曰：『姬受命，昌來提，撰爾雒鈐報在齊。

translations.literal: " Shang stood, changed his name, and replied: "While fishing I obtained a jade tablet; its text in essence said: 'The Ji receive the mandate; Chang comes to carry it; take up your Luogou — your reward lies in Qi.'"
translations.idiomatic: " Shang stood, changed his name, and replied: "While fishing I obtained a jade tablet. Its text in essence read: 'The Ji receive the mandate; Chang comes to carry it; take up your Luogou — your reward lies in Qi.'"

sentences.zh: 』」尚出游，見赤人自雒出，授尚書曰：「命曰呂，佐昌者子。

translations.literal: "' Shang traveled abroad and saw a red man emerge from the Luo; he gave Shang a book, saying: "Your mandate is called Lü; you are the one who assists Chang."
translations.idiomatic: "' On his travels Shang saw a red man emerge from the Luo River. The man gave Shang a book, saying: "Your mandate is called Lü; you are the one who assists Chang."

sentences.zh: 」文王夢日月著其身，又鸑鷟鳴於岐山。

translations.literal: " King Wen dreamed the sun and moon rested upon his body; again, the simurgh called on Mount Qi.
translations.idiomatic: " King Wen dreamed the sun and moon rested upon his body, and the simurgh called out on Mount Qi.

sentences.zh: 孟春六旬，五緯聚房。

translations.literal: In the sixty days of early spring, the five planets gathered in Fang.
translations.idiomatic: During the sixty days of early spring, the five planets gathered in the Fang constellation.

sentences.zh: 後有鳳皇銜書，游文王之都。

translations.literal: Afterwards a phoenix bearing a book wandered through King Wen's capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later a phoenix bearing a book flew through King Wen's capital.

sentences.zh: 書又曰：「殷帝無道，虐亂天下，皇命已移，不得復久，靈祇遠離，百神吹去，五星聚房，昭理四海。

translations.literal: The book also said: "The Emperor of Yin is without the Way, tyrannizing and disordering all under Heaven; the imperial mandate has already shifted — he cannot endure much longer. Spirits and earth-gods stand afar; the hundred spirits are blown away; the five stars gather in Fang, illumining and ordering the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: The book also declared: "The Emperor of Yin is without the Way, tyrannizing and plunging the realm into chaos. The imperial mandate has already shifted — he cannot last much longer. Spirits and earth-gods withdraw; the hundred deities depart. The five stars gather in Fang to bring order to the four seas."

sentences.zh: 」文王既沒，太子發代立，是為武王。

translations.literal: " After King Wen passed away, the heir apparent Fa succeeded in his place — this was King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: " After King Wen died, the crown prince Fa succeeded him — this was King Wu.

sentences.zh: 武王駢齒望羊。

translations.literal: King Wu had paired teeth and sheep-like eyes.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu had paired teeth and eyes like a sheep's.

sentences.zh: 將伐紂，至于孟津，八百諸侯，不期而會。

translations.literal: About to attack Zhou, he reached Mengjin; eight hundred feudal lords, without appointment, assembled together.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to attack Zhou, he reached Mengjin, where eight hundred feudal lords gathered without prior arrangement.

sentences.zh: 咸曰：「紂可伐矣。

translations.literal: All said: "Zhou can be attacked."
translations.idiomatic: All said: "Zhou can be attacked now."

sentences.zh: 」武王不從。

translations.literal: " King Wu did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " King Wu did not agree.

sentences.zh: 及紂殺比干，囚箕子，微子去之，乃伐紂。

translations.literal: When Zhou killed Bi Gan, imprisoned Jizi, and Weizi left him, then he attacked Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou killed Bi Gan, imprisoned Jizi, and Weizi fled, King Wu marched to attack Zhou.

sentences.zh: 度孟津，中流，白魚躍入王舟。

translations.literal: Crossing Mengjin, midstream, a white fish leaped into the king's boat.
translations.idiomatic: While crossing Mengjin, midstream, a white fish leaped into the king's boat.

sentences.zh: 王俯取魚，長三尺，目下有赤文成字，言紂可伐。

translations.literal: The king bent down and took the fish — three feet long; beneath its eyes were red characters forming words, stating that Zhou could be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The king leaned down and took the fish. It was three feet long, with red characters beneath its eyes declaring that Zhou could be attacked.

sentences.zh: 王寫以世字，魚文消。

translations.literal: The king copied it in the script of his generation; the fish's characters vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The king copied the text in the script of his age, and the characters on the fish vanished.

sentences.zh: 燔魚以告天。

translations.literal: He burned the fish to announce it to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He burned the fish as an offering to announce it to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 有火自天止于王屋，流為赤烏，烏銜穀焉。

translations.literal: Fire came from Heaven and halted on the king's house; flowing, it became a red crow, and the crow bore grain in its beak.
translations.idiomatic: Fire descended from Heaven and stopped on the royal house. It flowed into the form of a red crow, which bore grain in its beak.

sentences.zh: 穀者，紀后稷之德；

translations.literal: The grain — to commemorate Hou Ji's virtue;
translations.idiomatic: The grain commemorated Hou Ji's virtue;

sentences.zh: 火者，燔魚以告天，天火流下，應以吉也。

translations.literal: The fire — burning the fish to announce to Heaven, Heaven's fire flowed down, responding with auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: The fire responded to the burnt offering of the fish — Heaven's fire flowed down as an auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 遂東伐紂，勝於牧野，兵不血刃，而天下歸之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attacked Zhou eastward, prevailed at Muye, weapons unstained with blood, and all under Heaven submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched east to attack Zhou, prevailed at Muye without staining a blade with blood, and all under Heaven submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 乃封呂望於齊。

translations.literal: He thereupon enfeoffed Lü Wang at Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He then enfeoffed Lü Wang at Qi.

sentences.zh: 周德既隆，草木茂盛，蒿堪為宮室，因名蒿宮。

translations.literal: Zhou's virtue being already lofty, grass and trees flourished luxuriantly; artemisia could serve for palace halls — hence it was named the Artemisia Palace.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhou's virtue flourished, grass and trees grew luxuriantly. Artemisia grew sturdy enough to serve as palace walls, so the palace was named the Artemisia Palace.

sentences.zh: 武王沒，成王少，周公旦攝政七年，制禮作樂，神鳥鳳皇見，蓂莢生。

translations.literal: When King Wu passed away, King Cheng was young; the Duke of Zhou, Dan, acted as regent for seven years, established rites and composed music; the divine bird, the phoenix, appeared; felicitous plants grew.
translations.idiomatic: After King Wu died, the young King Cheng took the throne. The Duke of Zhou, Dan, served as regent for seven years, established rites and composed music. The divine phoenix appeared, and felicitous plants sprouted.

sentences.zh: 乃與成王觀于河、洛，沈璧。

translations.literal: He then went with King Cheng to observe at the He and Luo, sinking jade disks.
translations.idiomatic: He then went with King Cheng to observe at the He and Luo Rivers and sank jade disks as offerings.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，王退俟，至于日昧，榮光並出幕河，青雲浮至，青龍臨壇，銜玄甲之圖，坐之而去。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, the king withdrew to wait; by dusk, glorious light emerged together beyond the river, azure clouds floated up, the green dragon approached the altar, bore the chart on dark armor, sat and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, the king withdrew to wait. By dusk, radiant light shone beyond the river, azure clouds drifted in, and a green dragon approached the altar bearing the chart on dark armor. It sat a moment, then departed.

sentences.zh: 禮于洛，亦如之。

translations.literal: Performing rites at the Luo — it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: At the Luo, the rites were performed, and the same wonders occurred.

sentences.zh: 玄龜青龍蒼兕止于壇，

translations.literal: Dark tortoise, green dragon, and azure rhinoceros halted at the altar,
translations.idiomatic: A dark tortoise, green dragon, and azure rhinoceros halted at the altar,

sentences.zh: 〈玄龜青龍蒼兕止于壇　「蒼兕」各本並譌「蒼光」，據元龜二二改。〉

translations.literal: (Dark tortoise, green dragon, and azure rhinoceros halted at the altar — all editions corrupt "azure rhinoceros" to "azure light"; emended according to Yuan Gui 22.)
translations.idiomatic: (Dark tortoise, green dragon, and azure rhinoceros halted at the altar — all editions read "azure light" in place of "azure rhinoceros"; this reading is restored from Yuan Gui 22.)

sentences.zh: 背甲刻書，赤文成字，周公援筆以世文寫之，書成文消，龜墮甲而去。

translations.literal: On the back shell was inscribed a book; red script formed characters; the Duke of Zhou took up the brush and copied it in the script of the age; when the writing was finished the characters vanished; the tortoise dropped its shell and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Characters in red script were carved on its back shell. The Duke of Zhou took up his brush and copied them in the script of the age. When he finished writing, the characters vanished, and the tortoise shed its shell and departed.

sentences.zh: 其言自周公訖于秦、漢盛衰之符。

translations.literal: Its words ran from the Duke of Zhou down to omens of the rise and decline of Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Its text recorded omens from the Duke of Zhou down through the rise and fall of Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 麒麟遊苑，鳳皇翔庭，成王援琴而歌曰：「鳳皇翔兮於紫庭，余何德兮以感靈，賴先王兮恩澤臻，于胥樂兮民以寧。」

translations.literal: The qilin wandered the gardens; the phoenix soared in the courtyard; King Cheng took up the zither and sang: "Phoenix soaring in the purple court — what virtue have I to move the spirits? Relying on the former king's grace arriving in fullness — all rejoice in joy; the people find peace."
translations.idiomatic: The qilin roamed the gardens and the phoenix soared in the courtyard. King Cheng took up his zither and sang: "The phoenix soars in the purple court — what virtue have I to move the spirits? By the former king's grace, blessings have arrived — let us all rejoice, and may the people find peace."

sentences.zh: 魯哀公十四年，孔子夜夢三槐之間，豐、沛之邦，有赤煙氣起，乃呼顏淵、子夏往視之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Duke Ai of Lu, Confucius dreamed at night between three sophoras in the land of Feng and Pei — red smoke arose; he thereupon called Yan Yuan and Zixia to go view it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Duke Ai of Lu, Confucius dreamed one night of the land of Feng and Pei between three sophoras, where red smoke was rising. He called Yan Yuan and Zixia to go and see.

sentences.zh: 驅車到楚西北范氏街，見芻兒摘麟，傷其左前足，薪而覆之。

translations.literal: Driving his carriage to Fan Family Street in the northwest of Chu, he saw a hay-gathering boy capture a qilin, injuring its left foreleg; he gathered firewood and covered it.
translations.idiomatic: He drove to Fan Family Street in northwest Chu, where he saw a boy gathering hay who had captured a qilin and injured its left foreleg. The boy piled firewood over it.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「兒來，汝姓為赤誦，名子喬，字受紀。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Boy, come — your surname is Chisong, your given name Ziqiao, your style Shouji."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Come here, boy — your surname is Chisong, your given name is Ziqiao, and your style is Shouji."

sentences.zh: 」孔子曰：「汝豈有所見邪？

translations.literal: " Confucius said: "Have you perhaps seen something?"
translations.idiomatic: " Confucius said: "Have you seen something unusual?"

sentences.zh: 」兒曰：「見一禽，巨如羔羊，頭上有角，其末有肉。

translations.literal: " The boy said: "I saw one bird, large as a lamb, with horns on its head; their tips had flesh."
translations.idiomatic: " The boy said, "I saw a creature as large as a lamb, with horns on its head — and flesh at the tips of the horns."

sentences.zh: 」孔子曰：「天下已有主也，為赤劉，陳、項為輔，五星入井從歲星。

translations.literal: " Confucius said: "The realm already has its lord — the Red Liu; Chen and Xiang shall be his auxiliaries; the five stars enter the Well following the Year Star."
translations.idiomatic: " Confucius said, "The realm already has its master — it will be the Red Liu. Chen and Xiang will serve as his helpers. The five planets will enter the Well, following Jupiter."

sentences.zh: 」兒發薪下麟示孔子，孔子趨而往，麟蒙其耳，吐三卷圖，廣三寸，長八寸，每卷二十四字，其言赤劉當起，曰：「周亡，赤氣起，大燿興，玄丘制命，帝卯金。

translations.literal: " The boy lifted the firewood and showed the qilin to Confucius; Confucius hastened toward it; the qilin covered its ears and spat out three scroll-diagrams, three inches wide and eight inches long, twenty-four characters on each scroll — their meaning, that the Red Liu should rise — saying: "Zhou perishes; red vapor rises; Great Yao rises; the Dark Mound receives the mandate; emperor Mao-jin."
translations.idiomatic: " The boy removed the firewood and revealed the qilin to Confucius. Confucius hurried over. The qilin covered its ears and spat out three scroll-diagrams, three inches wide and eight inches long, with twenty-four characters on each, foretelling the rise of the Red Liu: "Zhou will fall, red vapor will rise, Great Yao will ascend, the Dark Mound will receive Heaven's command — the emperor of Mao-jin."

sentences.zh: 」孔子作春秋，制孝經，既成，使七十二弟子向北辰星罄折而立，使曾子抱河、洛事北向。

translations.literal: " Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn and fashioned the Classic of Filial Piety; when complete, he had seventy-two disciples stand bowed to the North Star, and had Zengzi hold the River and Luo materials facing north.
translations.idiomatic: " After Confucius finished the Spring and Autumn Annals and composed the Classic of Filial Piety, he had his seventy-two disciples stand with deep bows toward the North Star, and had Zengzi hold the documents of the River and Luo, facing north.

sentences.zh: 孔子齋戒向北辰而拜，告備于天曰：「孝經四卷，春秋、河、洛凡八十一卷，謹已備。

translations.literal: Confucius fasted and purified himself, bowed toward the North Star, and reported completion to Heaven, saying: "The Classic of Filial Piety, four scrolls; Spring and Autumn, River and Luo — eighty-one scrolls in all — are now duly prepared."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius fasted and made ritual purification, then bowed toward the North Star and reported to Heaven: "The Classic of Filial Piety in four scrolls, together with the Spring and Autumn and the River and Luo texts — eighty-one scrolls in all — have been duly completed."

sentences.zh: 」天乃洪鬱起白霧摩地，赤虹自上下，化為黃玉，長三尺，上有刻文。

translations.literal: " Heaven then grew thick and somber; white mist rose brushing the ground; a red rainbow descended from above and transformed into yellow jade, three feet long, with inscriptions upon it.
translations.idiomatic: " Then Heaven grew dark and heavy; white mist rose until it brushed the ground. A red rainbow descended from above and turned into a piece of yellow jade three feet long, bearing engraved characters.

sentences.zh: 孔子跪受而讀之曰：「寶文出，劉季握。

translations.literal: Confucius knelt to receive it and read aloud: "The precious text emerges; Liu Ji holds it."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius knelt to receive it and read: "The precious text has appeared; Liu Ji will grasp power."

sentences.zh: 卯金刀，在軫北。

translations.literal: Mao-jin knife, north of the Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The Mao-jin blade lies north of the Chariot.

sentences.zh: 字禾子，天下服。」

translations.literal: Character He-zi; all under Heaven submits."
translations.idiomatic: The character formed by He and zi — and all under Heaven will submit."

sentences.zh: 西漢

translations.literal: Western Han
translations.idiomatic: Western Han

sentences.zh: 漢高帝父曰劉執嘉。

translations.literal: The Han High Emperor's father was named Liu Zhijia.
translations.idiomatic: The father of the Han High Emperor was named Liu Zhijia.

sentences.zh: 執嘉之母，夢赤鳥若龍戲己，而生執嘉，是為太上皇帝。

translations.literal: Zhijia's mother dreamed a red bird like a dragon sporting with her; she gave birth to Zhijia — this is the Supreme Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijia's mother dreamed of a red bird like a dragon sporting with her, and bore Zhijia — who became the Supreme Emperor.

sentences.zh: 母名含始，是為昭靈后。

translations.literal: Her name was Hanshi — she is the Empress Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Her name was Hanshi — she is known as Empress Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 昭靈后游於洛池，有玉雞銜赤珠，刻曰玉英，吞此者王。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaoling roamed at the Luo Pool; there was a jade rooster holding a red pearl, inscribed "Jade Splendor — whoever swallows this shall be king."
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Zhaoling was strolling at the Luo Pool, a jade rooster appeared holding a red pearl inscribed "Jade Splendor — whoever swallows this shall become king."

sentences.zh: 昭靈后取而吞之。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaoling took it and swallowed it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaoling took the pearl and swallowed it.

sentences.zh: 又寢於大澤，夢與神遇。

translations.literal: Again she slept in a great marsh and dreamed of meeting a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Later she slept in a great marsh and dreamed that she met a spirit.

sentences.zh: 是時雷電晦冥，太上皇視之，見蛟龍在其上，遂有身而生季，是為高帝。

translations.literal: At that time thunder and lightning made the sky dark; the Supreme Emperor looked and saw a flood dragon upon her; she conceived and bore Ji — this is the High Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder and lightning then darkened the sky. The Supreme Emperor looked and saw a flood dragon upon her. She conceived and bore Ji — who became the High Emperor.

sentences.zh: 高帝隆準而龍顏，美須髥，左股有七十二黑子。

translations.literal: The High Emperor had a high nose and dragon countenance, a fine beard and whiskers, and seventy-two black moles on his left thigh.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor had a high-bridged nose and a dragon-like face, a handsome beard and whiskers, and seventy-two black moles on his left thigh.

sentences.zh: 微時，數從王媼、武負貰酒，醉臥，上常有光怪。

translations.literal: In humble times he often visited Wang Ao and Wu Fu to buy wine on credit; when drunk he would lie down, and above him strange lights often appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In his humble days he often bought wine on credit from Wang Ao and Wu Fu. When he lay drunk, strange lights would appear above him.

sentences.zh: 每留飲，售輒數倍。

translations.literal: Whenever he stayed drinking, sales were several times greater.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he stayed to drink, sales were several times what they normally were.

sentences.zh: 武負異之，輒折其契。

translations.literal: Wu Fu marveled at this and always tore up his debt slips.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fu was astonished by this and always tore up his debt slips.

sentences.zh: 單父人呂公好相人，見高帝，謂曰：「臣少好相人，相人多矣，無如季相，願季自愛。

translations.literal: Lu Gong of Shanfu was fond of reading faces; seeing the High Emperor, he said: "Your servant from youth has loved reading faces; I have read many, but none like Ji's — may Ji cherish himself."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gong of Shanfu was skilled at reading faces. When he saw the High Emperor, he said, "I have read faces since youth and have read countless men, but none like Ji. May Ji take care of himself."

sentences.zh: 臣有息女，願為箕箒妾。

translations.literal: I have a daughter; I wish her to be a broom-and-dustpan concubine.
translations.idiomatic: I have a daughter, and I wish to offer her as a humble wife.

sentences.zh: 」呂公妻媼怒呂公曰：「公常奇此女，欲為貴人。

translations.literal: " Lu Gong's wife angrily said to Lu Gong: "You always prized this daughter, wanting her to marry into nobility."
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Gong's wife angrily said to him, "You always prized this daughter and wanted her to marry into nobility."

sentences.zh: 沛令善公，求不與。

translations.literal: The chief of Pei was good to the elder and sought her — you did not give her.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Pei treated you well and sought her hand — yet you would not give her to him.

sentences.zh: 何妄許劉季。

translations.literal: Why rashly promise her to Liu Ji?
translations.idiomatic: Why would you rashly promise her to Liu Ji?

sentences.zh: 」呂公曰：「非女子所知。

translations.literal: " Lu Gong said: "This is not what a woman would understand."
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Gong said, "This is not something a woman would understand."

sentences.zh: 」卒與高帝。

translations.literal: " In the end he gave her to the High Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he gave her to the High Emperor.

sentences.zh: 生惠帝、魯元公主。

translations.literal: She bore Emperor Hui and the Princess of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Emperor Hui and the Princess of Lu.

sentences.zh: 呂后嘗與兩子居田中，有一老公過，請飲，呂后因饋之食。

translations.literal: Empress Lü once lived in the fields with her two children; an old man came by and asked for a drink; Empress Lü gave him food.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü once lived in the fields with her two children. An old man passed by and asked for a drink, and Empress Lü gave him food.

sentences.zh: 老父相呂后曰：「夫人，天下貴人也。

translations.literal: The old man read Empress Lü's face and said: "Madam, you are a person of noble rank under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The old man read Empress Lü's face and said, "Madam, you are destined for the highest rank under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」令相二子，見惠帝曰：「夫人所以貴者，乃此男。

translations.literal: " He had the two children read; seeing Emperor Hui, he said: "The reason Madam is noble is this boy."
translations.idiomatic: " He then read the two children. Seeing Emperor Hui, he said, "The reason Madam is destined for greatness is this boy."

sentences.zh: 」相魯元公主，亦貴。

translations.literal: " He read the Princess of Lu — she too was noble.
translations.idiomatic: " He read the Princess of Lu as well — she too was destined for nobility.

sentences.zh: 老父已去，高帝適從傍舍來，呂后具言之。

translations.literal: The old man had gone; the High Emperor happened to come from a neighboring house; Empress Lü told him everything.
translations.idiomatic: The old man had already gone when the High Emperor happened to return from a neighboring house. Empress Lü told him everything.

sentences.zh: 高帝追問老父。

translations.literal: The High Emperor chased after the old man.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor went after the old man.

sentences.zh: 老父曰：「向者夫人、兒子之貴，皆以君相。

translations.literal: The old man said: "The nobility of Madam and her sons just now — all was read from your face."
translations.idiomatic: The old man said, "The nobility I read in Madam and her sons just now all came from your face."

sentences.zh: 君貴不可言。

translations.literal: Your nobility cannot be put into words.
translations.idiomatic: Your destiny for greatness is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」高帝被飲，夜行徑澤中。

translations.literal: " The High Emperor, having drunk, traveled by night straight through the marsh.
translations.idiomatic: " The High Emperor, having drunk heavily, traveled by night straight through the marsh.

sentences.zh: 前人反曰：「有大蛇當道，願還。

translations.literal: Those ahead came back saying: "A great serpent blocks the path — we wish to turn back."
translations.idiomatic: Those ahead came back and said, "A great serpent blocks the road — we wish to turn back."

sentences.zh: 」高帝醉，曰：「壯士行，何畏。

translations.literal: " The High Emperor, drunk, said: "A brave man walks — what is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: " The High Emperor, drunk, said, "A brave man walks on — what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」乃前，拔劍斬蛇，蛇分為兩，道開而過。

translations.literal: " He went forward, drew his sword and cut the serpent; the serpent split in two; the way opened and he passed.
translations.idiomatic: " He went forward, drew his sword, and cut the serpent in two. The road cleared, and he passed through.

sentences.zh: 後人來者，見老嫗守蛇曰：「向者赤帝子過，殺之。

translations.literal: Those who came later saw an old woman guarding the serpent, saying: "The Red Emperor's son just passed and killed it."
translations.idiomatic: Those who came later saw an old woman guarding the serpent. She said, "The Red Emperor's son just passed and killed it."

sentences.zh: 」見者疑嫗為詐，欲笞之，忽然不見。

translations.literal: " Those who saw her suspected fraud and wanted to whip her; suddenly she vanished.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who saw her suspected trickery and wanted to whip her, but suddenly she vanished.

sentences.zh: 具以狀告高帝，帝心喜。

translations.literal: They fully reported this to the High Emperor; the Emperor's heart was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: They reported the whole affair to the High Emperor, and the Emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇帝曰：「東南有天子氣。

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin said: "In the southeast there is the qi of a Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin said, "In the southeast there is the aura of a Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」於是東遊以厭之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he toured east to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he toured east to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 高帝隱於芒、碭山澤之間，呂后常知其處。

translations.literal: The High Emperor hid among the marshes of Mount Mang and Mount Dang; Empress Lü always knew his whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor hid among the marshes between Mount Mang and Mount Dang, yet Empress Lü always knew where he was.

sentences.zh: 高帝怪問之，對曰：「季所居，上常有雲氣，故知之。

translations.literal: The High Emperor wondered and asked; she replied: "Where Ji dwells, cloud-qi often appears above — that is how I know."
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor wondered at this and asked her. She replied, "Wherever Ji stays, clouds and vapor always gather above — that is how I know."

sentences.zh: 」高帝為沛公，入秦，五星聚于東井，歲星先至，而四星從之。

translations.literal: " The High Emperor became Duke of Pei, entered Qin; the five stars gathered in the Eastern Well; the Year Star arrived first, and the four stars followed.
translations.idiomatic: " When the High Emperor became Duke of Pei and entered Qin, the five planets gathered in the Eastern Well. Jupiter arrived first, and the four other planets followed.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「以義取天下。

translations.literal: The divination read: "By righteousness one takes the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The divination read, "The realm will be taken by righteousness."

sentences.zh: 」初，張良遊於下邳沂水之上，

translations.literal: " At first, Zhang Liang wandered above the Yi River at Xiapi,
