translations.idiomatic: " At first, Zhang Liang was wandering above the Yi River at Xiapi,

sentences.zh: 〈張良遊於下邳沂水之上　漢書張良傳作下邳圯上。

translations.literal: 〈Zhang Liang wandered above the Yi River at Xiapi — the Hanshu Biography of Zhang Liang has "above the bridge at Xiapi."
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhang Liang wandered above the Yi River at Xiapi — the Hanshu Biography of Zhang Liang reads "above the bridge at Xiapi."

sentences.zh: 服虔曰：「圯音頤。

translations.literal: Fu Qian says: "Yi (圯) is pronounced yi (頤)."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian says, "Yi (圯) is pronounced yi (頤)."

sentences.zh: 楚人謂橋曰圯。

translations.literal: The people of Chu call a bridge yi.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chu call a bridge yi.

sentences.zh: 」應劭曰：「汜水之上也。

translations.literal: " Ying Shao says: "Above the Si River."
translations.idiomatic: " Ying Shao says, "Above the Si River."

sentences.zh: 」文穎曰：「沂水上橋也。

translations.literal: " Wen Ying says: "The bridge above the Yi River."
translations.idiomatic: " Wen Ying says, "The bridge above the Yi River."

sentences.zh: 」師古曰：「下邳之水，非汜水也，又非沂水。

translations.literal: " Ban Gu says: "The water at Xiapi is neither the Si River nor the Yi River."
translations.idiomatic: " Ban Gu says, "The water at Xiapi is neither the Si River nor the Yi River."

sentences.zh: 服說是矣。」〉

translations.literal: Fu's explanation is correct."〉
translations.idiomatic: Fu's explanation is correct."〉

sentences.zh: 有老父來，直至良前，而墮其履。

translations.literal: An old man came, walked straight to Zhang Liang, and dropped his shoe.
translations.idiomatic: An old man came, walked straight up to Zhang Liang, and dropped his shoe.

sentences.zh: 顧謂良曰：「孺子下取履。

translations.literal: He turned and said to Zhang Liang: "Youngster, go down and fetch the shoe."
translations.idiomatic: He turned and said to Zhang Liang, "Boy, go down and fetch the shoe."

sentences.zh: 」良愕然，欲毆之，以其老，乃下取跪進。

translations.literal: " Zhang Liang was startled and wanted to strike him; because he was old, he went down, fetched it, and kneeling, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Liang was startled and wanted to strike him, but because the man was old, he went down, retrieved the shoe, and kneeling, presented it.

sentences.zh: 父以足受，笑而去，良殊大驚。

translations.literal: The old man received it with his foot, smiled and left; Zhang Liang was deeply astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The old man received it with his foot, smiled, and left. Zhang Liang was deeply astonished.

sentences.zh: 父去里所復來，曰：「孺子可教也。

translations.literal: The old man went about a li and returned, saying: "This youngster can be taught."
translations.idiomatic: The old man went about a li and returned, saying, "This boy can be taught."

sentences.zh: 後五日平明，與我會此。

translations.literal: In five days at dawn, meet me here."
translations.idiomatic: In five days at dawn, meet me here."

sentences.zh: 」良怪之，跪應曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " Zhang Liang wondered at this, knelt and replied: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Liang was puzzled by this, knelt, and replied, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」五日，良往，父已先來，怒曰：「何與長者期而後也？

translations.literal: " After five days Zhang Liang went; the old man had already arrived first and angrily said: "Why make an appointment with an elder and arrive late?"
translations.idiomatic: " Five days later Zhang Liang went, but the old man had already arrived first. Angrily he said, "Why make an appointment with an elder and arrive late?"

sentences.zh: 五日，更與我會此。

translations.literal: In five days, meet me here again."
translations.idiomatic: In five days, meet me here again."

sentences.zh: 」凡三期而良前至。

translations.literal: " In all three appointments Zhang Liang arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: " After three such appointments, Zhang Liang arrived first each time.

sentences.zh: 老父喜曰：「不當如是邪！

translations.literal: The old man said with pleasure: "Should it not be just so!"
translations.idiomatic: The old man said with pleasure, "Should it not be just so!"

sentences.zh: 」即出懷中一卷書與之，曰：「讀之，此為王者師。

translations.literal: " He took from his bosom a scroll and gave it to him, saying: "Read this — it is the teacher of one who would be king."
translations.idiomatic: " He took from his bosom a scroll and gave it to him, saying, "Read this — it will be the teacher of a king."

sentences.zh: 後十三年，孺子見我濟北穀城山下，黃石即我也。

translations.literal: In thirteen years, youngster, you will see me at Mount Gucheng north of the Ji River — Yellow Stone is me."
translations.idiomatic: In thirteen years, boy, you will see me at Mount Gucheng north of the Ji River — Yellow Stone is me."

sentences.zh: 」旦視其書，乃太公兵法。

translations.literal: " At dawn he looked at the book — it was Taigong's Art of War.
translations.idiomatic: " At dawn he looked at the book — it was Taigong's Art of War.

sentences.zh: 良以黃石篇為他人說，皆不省，唯高帝說焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang explained the Yellow Stone text to others — none understood; only the High Emperor understood.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Liang explained the Yellow Stone text to others, none understood it — only the High Emperor did.

sentences.zh: 良曰：「此殆天所授矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang said: "This is presumably Heaven's gift."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang said, "This must be Heaven's gift."

sentences.zh: 」五年而成帝業。

translations.literal: " In five years the imperial enterprise was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: " In five years the imperial enterprise was accomplished.

sentences.zh: 後十三年，張良果得穀城山下黃石，寶而祠之，死與合葬。

translations.literal: Thirteen years later Zhang Liang indeed obtained the Yellow Stone at Mount Gucheng; he treasured it and sacrificed to it; when he died it was buried with him.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years later Zhang Liang indeed obtained the Yellow Stone at Mount Gucheng. He treasured it and made offerings to it, and when he died it was buried with him.

sentences.zh: 文帝之母薄姬，魏豹為魏王，納之後宮。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen's mother Lady Bo — when Wei Bao was King of Wei, she was taken into the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's mother, Lady Bo, was taken into the rear palace when Wei Bao was King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 許負相之，當生天子，魏王豹於是背漢，漢高帝擊虜，而薄姬輸織室。

translations.literal: Xu Fu read her face — she would bear a Son of Heaven; King Bao of Wei thereupon turned against Han; the Han High Emperor defeated and captured him, and Lady Bo was sent to the weaving rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu read her face and said she would bear a Son of Heaven. King Bao of Wei thereupon turned against Han. The Han High Emperor defeated and captured him, and Lady Bo was sent to the weaving rooms.

sentences.zh: 高帝見而美之，內於後宮，歲餘乃得幸。

translations.literal: The High Emperor saw her and admired her beauty; he took her into the rear palace; after more than a year she finally gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor saw her and admired her beauty. He took her into the rear palace, but more than a year passed before she finally gained his favor.

sentences.zh: 將見幸，薄姬言：「妾昨夢青龍據妾心。

translations.literal: About to receive favor, Lady Bo said: "Your handmaid yesterday dreamed a blue dragon resting upon my heart."
translations.idiomatic: As she was about to receive his favor, Lady Bo said, "Your handmaid dreamed last night that a blue dragon rested upon my heart."

sentences.zh: 」高帝曰：「我是也。

translations.literal: " The High Emperor said: "That is me."
translations.idiomatic: " The High Emperor said, "That is me."

sentences.zh: 吾為爾成之。

translations.literal: I shall fulfill it for you."
translations.idiomatic: I shall fulfill it for you."

sentences.zh: 」一御而生文帝。

translations.literal: " After one visit she bore Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: " After a single visit she bore Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 景帝王皇后初嫁為金王孫妻，母臧兒卜筮曰：「當貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing's Empress Wang — she had first married the Jin prince's grandson; her mother Zang Er divined and said: "She shall be noble."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing's Empress Wang had first married a man surnamed Jin. Her mother Zang Er divined and said, "She is destined for greatness."

sentences.zh: 」乃奪金氏而內太子宮，生男。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they took her from the Jin family and placed her in the crown prince's palace; she bore a son.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they took her from the Jin family and placed her in the crown prince's palace, where she bore a son.

sentences.zh: 男方在身，夢日入其懷，以告太子。

translations.literal: While the boy was in her womb, she dreamed the sun entered her bosom; she told the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: While the boy was still in her womb, she dreamed that the sun entered her bosom, and she told the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「是貴徵也。

translations.literal: The crown prince said: "That is a noble omen."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "That is a sign of greatness."

sentences.zh: 」生男，是為武帝。

translations.literal: " She bore a son — this is Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: " She bore a son — who became Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 武帝趙婕妤，家在河間，生而兩手皆拳，不可開。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's Lady Zhao — her family was in Hejian; from birth both her hands were clenched and could not be opened.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's Lady Zhao came from Hejian. From birth both her hands were clenched and could not be opened.

sentences.zh: 武帝巡狩過河間，

translations.literal: Emperor Wu on imperial tour passed through Hejian,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu passed through Hejian on an imperial tour,

sentences.zh: 〈武帝巡狩過河間　「狩」各本並作「守」，據漢書外戚傳改。〉

translations.literal: 〈Emperor Wu on imperial tour passed through Hejian — all editions had "guard" (shou) rather than "hunt/tour" (shou); emended per the Hanshu Biography of the Empresses and Consorts. Note: shou for guard and shou for hunt are homographs in pinyin; the source contrasts the two characters.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emperor Wu on imperial tour passed through Hejian — all editions read "guard" rather than "hunt/tour"; emended according to the Hanshu Biography of the Empresses and Consorts.〉

sentences.zh: 望氣者言，此有奇女天子氣。

translations.literal: A reader of atmospheric signs said there was an extraordinary woman with the qi of a Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: A reader of atmospheric signs said that there was an extraordinary woman here with the aura of a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 召而見之。

translations.literal: She was summoned and presented.
translations.idiomatic: She was summoned and brought before him.

sentences.zh: 武帝自披其手，既時申，得一玉鉤。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu himself pried open her hands; at once they extended, and a jade hook was found.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu himself pried open her hands. At once they extended, and a jade hook was found inside.

sentences.zh: 由是見幸，號曰「拳夫人」。

translations.literal: Thereby she gained favor and was styled "Lady Fist."
translations.idiomatic: Thereby she gained his favor and was styled "Lady Fist."

sentences.zh: 進為婕妤，居鉤弋宮，大有寵。

translations.literal: Advanced to Lady of Handsome Fairness, she dwelt in the Hook-and-Bow Palace and enjoyed great favor.
translations.idiomatic: She was advanced to Lady of Handsome Fairness, took up residence in the Hook-and-Bow Palace, and enjoyed great favor.

sentences.zh: 十四月生男，是為昭帝，號曰「鉤弋子」。

translations.literal: After fourteen months she bore a son — this is Emperor Zhao, styled "the Hook-and-Bow Son."
translations.idiomatic: After fourteen months she bore a son — who became Emperor Zhao, styled "the Hook-and-Bow Son."

sentences.zh: 武帝曰：「聞昔堯十四月而生，今鉤弋子亦然。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu said: "I hear that in antiquity Yao was born after fourteen months; now the Hook-and-Bow Son is the same."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said, "I have heard that in antiquity Yao was born after fourteen months. Now the Hook-and-Bow Son is the same."

sentences.zh: 」乃名其門曰堯母門。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he named her gate the Gate of Yao's Mother.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he named her gate the Gate of Yao's Mother.

sentences.zh: 昭帝元鳳三年正月，

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Yuanfeng of Emperor Zhao,
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Zhao,

sentences.zh: 〈昭帝元鳳三年正月　「三年」各本並作「二年」，據漢書眭弘傳、漢書五行志、元龜二一改。〉

translations.literal: 〈In the first month of the third year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Zhao — all editions read "second year" rather than "third year"; emended per the Hanshu Biography of Sui Hong, Hanshu Treatise on the Five Processes, and Yuan Gui II.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈In the first month of the third year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Zhao — all editions read "second year" rather than "third year"; emended according to the Hanshu Biography of Sui Hong, Hanshu Treatise on the Five Processes, and Yuan Gui II.〉

sentences.zh: 泰山、萊蕪山南，民夜聞訩訩有數千人聲，晨往視之，見大石自立，高丈五尺，大四十八圍，

translations.literal: South of Mount Tai and Mount Laigu — at night the people heard clamorous sounds as of several thousand voices; at dawn they went to look and saw a great stone stand upright by itself, fifteen chi in height and forty-eight wei in circumference,
translations.idiomatic: South of Mount Tai and Mount Laigu, the people heard at night a clamor like several thousand voices. At dawn they went to look and saw a great stone standing upright by itself, fifteen chi high and forty-eight wei around,

sentences.zh: 〈大四十八圍　各本並作「大三十八圍」，據漢書眭弘傳、漢書五行志、元龜二一改。〉

translations.literal: 〈Forty-eight wei in circumference — all editions read "thirty-eight wei in circumference" rather than "forty-eight wei"; emended per the Hanshu Biography of Sui Hong, Hanshu Treatise on the Five Processes, and Yuan Gui II.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Forty-eight wei in circumference — all editions read "thirty-eight wei in circumference" rather than "forty-eight wei"; emended according to the Hanshu Biography of Sui Hong, Hanshu Treatise on the Five Processes, and Yuan Gui II.〉

sentences.zh: 入地八尺，三石為足，立後，白烏數千集其旁。

translations.literal: sunk eight chi into the earth, with three stones as feet; after it stood, several thousand white crows gathered beside it.
translations.idiomatic: It sank eight chi into the earth, with three stones serving as feet. Once it stood upright, several thousand white crows gathered beside it.

sentences.zh: 又上林苑中柳樹斷臥地，一朝自起生枝葉，蟲齧其葉成文，曰：「公孫病已立。

translations.literal: Also, in the Shanglin Park a willow tree, broken off and lying on the ground, one morning rose by itself and sprouted branches and leaves; insects gnawed its leaves into characters reading: "Gongsun Bingyi is established."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the Shanglin Park a willow tree that had broken and lain on the ground rose up one morning of its own accord and sprouted branches and leaves. Insects gnawed its leaves into characters that read, "Gongsun Bingyi is established."

sentences.zh: 」陳留襄邑王社忽移至長安。

translations.literal: " The altar of the land god at Xiangyi in Chenliu suddenly moved to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " The altar of the land god at Xiangyi in Chenliu suddenly relocated to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 博士眭孟占之曰：「石，陰類。

translations.literal: Erudite Su Meng divined it and said: "Stone is a yin category.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Su Meng interpreted the omen and said, "Stone belongs to the yin category.

sentences.zh: 泰山，岱宗，王者禪代之處。

translations.literal: Mount Tai, the Daizong — the place where the sovereign performs the rites of abdication and succession."
translations.idiomatic: Mount Tai, the Daizong, is the place where sovereigns perform the rites of ceding and receiving the mandate."

sentences.zh: 將有廢故之家，姓公孫，名病已，從白衣為天子者。

translations.literal: There will be one from a deposed former house, surnamed Gongsun, named Bingyi, who from plain white garments will become Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: There will be a man from a deposed former house, surnamed Gongsun and named Bingyi, who from the ranks of commoners in white will become Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」時昭帝幼少，霍光輔政，以孟妖言誅之。

translations.literal: " At the time Emperor Zhao was young, Huo Guang assisted in government, and because of Meng's portentous words he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Emperor Zhao was still young, and Huo Guang served as regent. Because of Meng's prophetic words, he had Meng executed.

sentences.zh: 及昭帝崩，昌邑王又廢，光立宣帝，武帝曾孫，本名病已，在民間白衣三世，如孟言焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhao died and the Prince of Changyi was also deposed, Guang installed Emperor Xuan — a great-grandson of Emperor Wu, whose original name was Bingyi, who had worn plain white among the people for three generations — just as Meng had said.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhao died and the Prince of Changyi was also deposed, Guang enthroned Emperor Xuan, a great-grandson of Emperor Wu whose original name was Bingyi. He had lived among the people in plain white for three generations, just as Meng had foretold.

sentences.zh: 元帝王皇后，齊田氏之苗裔。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan's Empress Wang — a descendant of the Tian clan of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan's Empress Wang was a descendant of the Tian clan of Qi.

sentences.zh: 祖父翁孺，自東平陵徙元城。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Weng Ru moved from Dongpingling to Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Weng Ru had moved from Dongpingling to Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 元城建公曰：「昔春秋沙鹿崩，晉史卜之，陰為陽雄，土火相乘，故沙鹿崩。

translations.literal: The Lord of Yuancheng said: "In antiquity during the Spring and Autumn period the Sha Plain collapsed; the Jin historian divined it — yin serving as yang's consort, earth and fire multiplying each other — therefore the Sha Plain collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Yuancheng said, "In antiquity during the Spring and Autumn period the Sha Plain collapsed. The Jin historian divined it: yin serving as yang's consort, earth and fire multiplying each other — therefore the Sha Plain collapsed.

sentences.zh: 後六百四十五年，宜有聖女興，其齊田乎？

translations.literal: After six hundred forty-five years a sage woman should arise — will it not be of the Tian of Qi?"
translations.idiomatic: After six hundred forty-five years a sage woman should arise. Will she not be of the Tian clan of Qi?"

sentences.zh: 今翁孺之徙，正值其地，日月當之。

translations.literal: Now Weng Ru's move falls exactly upon that place; sun and moon are aligned with it.
translations.idiomatic: Now Weng Ru's move fell exactly upon that place, with sun and moon aligned with it.

sentences.zh: 元城郭東有五鹿之墟，即沙鹿地。

translations.literal: East of Yuancheng's outer wall is the ruins of Wulu — that is the place of the Sha Plain.
translations.idiomatic: East of Yuancheng's outer wall lay the ruins of Wulu — the very site of the Sha Plain.

sentences.zh: 後八十年，當有貴女興天下。

translations.literal: After eighty years there should be a noble woman who rises to dominate the realm."
translations.idiomatic: After eighty years a noble woman would rise to dominate the realm."

sentences.zh: 」翁孺生禁。

translations.literal: " Weng Ru begat Jin.
translations.idiomatic: " Weng Ru begat Jin.

sentences.zh: 禁妻李氏方任身，夢月入其懷，生女，是為元后。

translations.literal: Jin's wife Lady Li was just pregnant when she dreamed the moon entered her bosom; she bore a daughter — this is the Grand Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's wife Lady Li was pregnant when she dreamed the moon entered her bosom. She bore a daughter — who became the Grand Empress.

sentences.zh: 每許嫁，未行，所許者輒死。

translations.literal: Each time she was promised in marriage, before the wedding could take place the betrothed man would suddenly die.
translations.idiomatic: Each time she was promised in marriage, the betrothed man would die before the wedding could take place.

sentences.zh: 卜相者云：「當大貴。

translations.literal: A diviner and physiognomist said: "She shall be greatly noble."
translations.idiomatic: A diviner and physiognomist said, "She is destined for greatness."

sentences.zh: 」遂為元帝皇后，生成帝。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she became Emperor Yuan's empress and bore Emperor Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon she became Emperor Yuan's empress and bore Emperor Cheng.

sentences.zh: 初，秦始皇世，有長人十二，身長五丈，足跡六尺，見於隴西臨洮，前史以為秦亡之徵，史臣以為漢興之符也。

translations.literal: In the beginning, during the era of Qin Shihuangdi, there were twelve tall men, bodies five zhang in height, footprints six chi — they appeared at Lintao in Longxi. Earlier histories took this as a sign of Qin's downfall; the historiographer takes it as an omen of Han's rise.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning, during the reign of the First Emperor of Qin, twelve tall men appeared at Lintao in Longxi — each five zhang in height, with footprints six chi across. Earlier histories took this as a sign of Qin's downfall; the historiographer takes it as an omen of Han's rise.

sentences.zh: 自高帝至于平帝，十二主焉。

translations.literal: From the High Emperor down to Emperor Ping, there were twelve rulers.
translations.idiomatic: From the High Emperor down to Emperor Ping, there were twelve rulers.

sentences.zh: 東漢

translations.literal: Eastern Han
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han

sentences.zh: 光武皇帝，父為濟陽令。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu — his father was magistrate of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu — his father was magistrate of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 濟陽有武帝行宮，常封閉。

translations.literal: Jiyang had an imperial traveling palace of Emperor Wu, which was always sealed and closed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyang had an imperial traveling palace built by Emperor Wu, which was always sealed and closed.

sentences.zh: 哀帝建平元年十二月甲子夜，光武將產，乃開而居之。

translations.literal: On the night of the jiazi day in the twelfth month of the first year of Jianping under Emperor Ai, Guangwu was about to be born, so they opened it and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the jiazi day in the twelfth month of the first year of Jianping under Emperor Ai, as Guangwu was about to be born, they opened it and took up residence there.

sentences.zh: 時有赤光，室中盡明，皇考異焉。

translations.literal: At that time there was red light; the room was entirely bright; the imperial father was astonished by it.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment red light filled the room until it was entirely bright, and the imperial father was astonished.

sentences.zh: 使卜者王長卜之。

translations.literal: He had the diviner Wang Chang divining it.
translations.idiomatic: He had the diviner Wang Chang perform a divination.

sentences.zh: 長辟左右曰：「此善事，不可言。

translations.literal: Chang withdrew from those standing by and said: "This is an auspicious matter — it cannot be spoken of."
translations.idiomatic: Chang withdrew from those standing by and said, "This is an auspicious matter — it cannot be spoken of."

sentences.zh: 」是歲，有嘉禾生產屋景天中，一莖九穗，異於凡禾，縣界大豐，故名光武曰秀。

translations.literal: " That year, fine grain sprouted in the roof timbers above the birthing room — one stalk with nine ears, unlike ordinary grain. The county's borders had a great harvest, so they named Guangwu Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: " That year fine grain sprouted in the roof timbers above the birthing room — one stalk bearing nine ears, unlike ordinary grain. The county enjoyed a great harvest, so they named Guangwu Xiu.

sentences.zh: 時又有鳳皇集濟陽，於是畫宮為鳳皇之象。

translations.literal: At that time a phoenix also gathered at Jiyang; thereupon they painted the palace with the likeness of a phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a phoenix also alighted at Jiyang, whereupon they painted the palace with the likeness of a phoenix.

sentences.zh: 明年，方士有夏賀良者，上言哀帝云：「漢家歷運中衰，當再受命。

translations.literal: The following year there was a fangshi named Xia Heliang who submitted a memorial to Emperor Ai saying: "The Han house's allotted fortune is in mid-decline; it should receive the mandate anew."
translations.idiomatic: The following year a fangshi named Xia Heliang submitted a memorial to Emperor Ai saying, "The Han house's allotted fortune is in mid-decline; it should receive the mandate anew."

sentences.zh: 」於是改號為太初元將元年，稱陳聖劉太平皇帝以厭勝之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the reign era was changed to the first year of the Grand Primordial Primordial General, and Chen Sheng Liu Taiping Emperor was styled to counter it by apotropaic magic.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the reign era was changed to the first year of the Grand Primordial Primordial General, and Chen Sheng Liu Taiping Emperor was styled as a counter-charm.

sentences.zh: 王莽時，善望氣者蘇伯阿望光武所居縣舂陵城郭，唶曰：「氣佳哉！

translations.literal: During Wang Mang's time, the expert in reading atmospheric signs Su Bo'a gazed upon the walls of Chunling county where Guangwu dwelt and clicked his tongue, saying: "Excellent qi!
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Mang's time, the expert in reading atmospheric signs Su Bo'a gazed upon the walls of Chunling county where Guangwu dwelt and clicked his tongue, saying, "Excellent qi!

sentences.zh: 鬱鬱葱葱然。

translations.literal: Lush and verdant."
translations.idiomatic: Lush and verdant."

sentences.zh: 」莽忌惡漢，而錢文有金，乃改鑄貨泉以易之。

translations.literal: " Mang hated the Han, and since the coin inscriptions contained the character for metal, he had Huoquan coins recast to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: " Mang hated the Han, and since the coin inscriptions contained the character for metal, he had Huoquan coins recast to replace them.

sentences.zh: 既而光武起於舂陵之白水鄉，貨泉之文為「白水真人」也。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Guangwu rose at Baishui Township in Chunling, and the text of the Huoquan coin reads "Baishui True Man."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Guangwu rose at Baishui Township in Chunling — and the text of the Huoquan coin reads "Baishui True Man."

sentences.zh: 初起兵，望見家南有火光，以為人持火，呼之而光遂盛，䓇然上屬天，有頃不見。

translations.literal: When he first raised troops, he saw firelight south of his home, thinking someone held a torch; he called out and the light then blazed, flaming upward to reach heaven; in a moment it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: When he first raised troops, he saw firelight south of his home and thought someone held a torch. He called out, and the light blazed up, flaming skyward until it reached heaven — then in a moment it vanished.

sentences.zh: 及在河北，為王郎所逼，將南濟滹沱河。

translations.literal: When he was in Hebei, pressed by Wang Lang, he was about to cross the Hutuo River southward.
translations.idiomatic: When he was in Hebei, pressed by Wang Lang, he prepared to cross the Hutuo River heading south.

sentences.zh: 導吏還云：「河水流澌，無船可渡。

translations.literal: The guide officer returned and said: "The river water runs with ice floes; there are no boats to cross."
translations.idiomatic: The guide officer returned and reported, "The river runs with ice floes — there are no boats to cross."

sentences.zh: 」左右皆恐懼。

translations.literal: " Those at his side were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: " Those at his side were all afraid.

sentences.zh: 帝更遣王霸視之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Wang Ba again to look.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wang Ba again to look.

sentences.zh: 霸往視，如吏言。

translations.literal: Ba went to look — it was as the officer had said.
translations.idiomatic: Ba went to look — it was exactly as the officer had said.

sentences.zh: 霸慮還以實對，驚動眾心，乃謬云：「冰堅可渡。

translations.literal: Ba feared that returning and answering truthfully would shake the hearts of the multitude, so he falsely said: "The ice is solid enough to cross."
translations.idiomatic: Ba feared that reporting the truth would shake the hearts of the multitude, so he falsely declared, "The ice is solid enough to cross."

sentences.zh: 」帝馳進。

translations.literal: " The emperor galloped forward.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor galloped forward.

sentences.zh: 比至，而河冰皆合，其堅可乘。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, the river ice had all joined, firm enough to be traversed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, the river ice had all joined, firm enough to bear crossing.

sentences.zh: 既渡，餘數乘車未畢而冰陷。

translations.literal: After crossing, several remaining chariots had not yet finished when the ice gave way.
translations.idiomatic: After he had crossed, several chariots that had not yet finished crossing fell through as the ice gave way.

sentences.zh: 前至下博城西，疑所之。

translations.literal: Advancing to west of Xiabo city, he was uncertain where to go.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to west of Xiabo city, he was uncertain which way to go.

sentences.zh: 有一白衣老公在道旁，曰：「努力！

translations.literal: There was an old man in plain white clothes by the roadside who said: "Press on!
translations.idiomatic: An old man in plain white clothes stood by the roadside and said, "Press on!

sentences.zh: 信都為長安城守，去此八十里耳。

translations.literal: Xindu holds Chang'an city; it is only eighty li from here."
translations.idiomatic: Xindu holds Chang'an city — it is only eighty li from here."

sentences.zh: 」言畢，失所在。

translations.literal: " When he finished speaking, he vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: " When he finished speaking, he vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 遂至信都，投太守任光。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reached Xindu and joined himself to Governor Ren Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he reached Xindu and placed himself under Governor Ren Guang.

sentences.zh: 初光武微時，穰人蔡少公曰：「讖言劉秀發兵捕不道，卯金修德為天子。

translations.literal: When Guangwu was first still obscure, Cai Shaogong of Rang said: "A prophecy reads: Liu Xiu will raise troops to capture the lawless; mao-jin cultivating virtue shall be Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu was still obscure, Cai Shaogong of Rang said, "A prophecy reads: Liu Xiu will raise troops to capture the lawless; mao-jin cultivating virtue shall be Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」國師公劉子駿名秀。

translations.literal: " The Duke and National Preceptor Liu Zijun was named Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: " The Duke and National Preceptor Liu Zijun was named Xiu.

sentences.zh: 少公曰：「國師公是也。

translations.literal: Shaogong said: "The Duke and National Preceptor is the one."
translations.idiomatic: Shaogong said, "The Duke and National Preceptor is the one."

sentences.zh: 」光武笑曰：「何用知非僕？

translations.literal: " Guangwu laughed and said: "How do you know it is not me?"
translations.idiomatic: " Guangwu laughed and said, "How do you know it is not me?"

sentences.zh: 」道士西門君惠等並云：「劉秀當為天子。

translations.literal: " The daoshi Ximen Junhui and others all said: "Liu Xiu is destined to be Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: " The daoshi Ximen Junhui and others all said, "Liu Xiu is destined to be Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」光武平定河北，還至中山，將軍萬脩得赤伏符，言光武當受命。

translations.literal: " Guangwu pacified Hebei and returned to Zhongshan; General Wan Xiu obtained the Red Manifest talisman, which said Guangwu was to receive the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangwu pacified Hebei and returned to Zhongshan. General Wan Xiu obtained the Red Manifest talisman, which declared that Guangwu was to receive the mandate.

sentences.zh: 羣臣上尊號，光武辭。

translations.literal: The ministers presented him the honorific title; Guangwu declined.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers presented him with the honorific title, but Guangwu declined.

sentences.zh: 前至鄗縣，諸生彊華又自長安詣鄗，上赤伏符，文與脩合。

translations.literal: Advancing to Gao county, the scholar Qiang Hua also came from Chang'an to Gao and presented the Red Manifest talisman — its text matched Xiu's.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Gao county, the scholar Qiang Hua also came from Chang'an to Gao and presented the Red Manifest talisman — its text matched Xiu's.

sentences.zh: 羣下又請曰：「受命之符，人應為大。

translations.literal: The subordinates again requested: "The talisman of receiving the mandate — a man should answer to what is great."
translations.idiomatic: The subordinates again petitioned, "The talisman of receiving the mandate — a man should answer to what is great."

sentences.zh: 」光武又夢乘赤龍登天，乃即位，都洛陽，營宮闕。

translations.literal: " Guangwu also dreamed of riding a red dragon up to heaven; thereupon he ascended the throne, made Luoyang his capital, and built palaces and towers.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangwu also dreamed of riding a red dragon up to heaven. Thereupon he ascended the throne, made Luoyang his capital, and built palaces and towers.

sentences.zh: 一夕有門材自至，是時琅邪開陽縣城門，一夕無故自亡，檢所得材，即是也，遂名其門曰開陽門。

translations.literal: One night gate timber arrived of itself. At that time the city gate of Kaiyang county in Langye vanished without cause in a single night; examining the timber recovered, it was exactly that timber — thereupon they named its gate Kaiyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: One night gate timber arrived of itself. At that time the city gate of Kaiyang county in Langye vanished without cause in a single night. Examining the timber recovered, they found it was exactly that timber — thereupon they named the gate Kaiyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 先是秦穆公時，陳倉人掘地得物，若羊非羊，若猪非猪，怪，將獻之。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the time of Duke Mu of Qin, a man of Chen Cang dug in the earth and obtained a thing — not quite a sheep, not quite a pig; finding it strange, he was about to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the time of Duke Mu of Qin, a man of Chen Cang dug in the earth and obtained a creature — not quite a sheep, not quite a pig. Finding it strange, he was about to present it as tribute.

sentences.zh: 道逢二僮子，謂之曰：「子知彼乎，名為，常在地下食死人腦。

translations.literal: On the road he met two youths who said to him: "Do you know that thing? Its name is — [character missing in text]; it always dwells underground eating the brains of the dead.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met two youths who said to him, "Do you know that thing? Its name is — [character missing in text]; it always dwells underground eating the brains of the dead.

sentences.zh: 若欲殺之，以栢東南枝指之，則死矣。

translations.literal: If you wish to kill it, point the southeast branch of a cypress at it, and it will die."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to kill it, point the southeast branch of a cypress at it, and it will die."

sentences.zh: 」因言曰：「此二僮子，名為寶。

translations.literal: " Then he said: "These two youths are named Bao.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he said, "These two youths are named Bao.

sentences.zh: 得其雄者王，得其雌者霸。

translations.literal: Whoever obtains the male shall be king; whoever obtains the female shall be hegemon."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever obtains the male shall be king; whoever obtains the female shall be hegemon."

sentences.zh: 」於是陳倉人遂棄而逐二僮子，二僮子化為雉，飛入林。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Chen Cang man abandoned it and pursued the two youths; the two youths transformed into pheasants and flew into the forest.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the Chen Cang man abandoned it and pursued the two youths. The two youths transformed into pheasants and flew into the forest.

sentences.zh: 陳倉人以告穆公，穆公發徒大獵，得其雌者，化而為石，置之汧、渭之間。

translations.literal: The Chen Cang man reported this to Duke Mu; Duke Mu dispatched men on a great hunt and obtained the female, which transformed into stone and was placed between the Qian and Wei rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen Cang man reported this to Duke Mu. Duke Mu dispatched men on a great hunt and obtained the female, which transformed into stone and was placed between the Qian and Wei rivers.

sentences.zh: 至文公，為之立祠，名曰陳寶祠。

translations.literal: Down to Duke Wen, a shrine was established for it, named the Chen Bao Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Duke Wen, a shrine had been established for it, named the Chen Bao Shrine.

sentences.zh: 雄南飛集南陽穰縣，其後光武興於南陽。

translations.literal: The male flew south and alighted at Rang county in Nanyang; afterward Guangwu rose in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The male flew south and alighted at Rang county in Nanyang — and afterward Guangwu rose in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 光武之初興也，隗囂擁眾隴右，招集英俊，而公孫述稱帝於蜀，天下雲擾，大者連州郡，小者據縣邑。

translations.literal: At Guangwu's first rise, Wei Xiao held the multitude in Longyou and gathered outstanding men, while Gongsun Shu declared himself emperor in Shu; the realm was cloud-tossed in turmoil — the great linked province and commandery, the small seized counties and townships.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangwu's first rise, Wei Xiao held the multitude in Longyou and gathered outstanding men, while Gongsun Shu declared himself emperor in Shu. The realm was cloud-tossed in turmoil — the great linked province to province and commandery to commandery, the small seized counties and townships.

sentences.zh: 囂問扶風人班彪曰：「往者周亡，戰國並爭，天下分裂，數世然後定。

translations.literal: Xiao asked Ban Biao of Fufeng: "In the past when Zhou perished, the Warring States contended together; the realm split apart, and only after several generations was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao asked Ban Biao of Fufeng, "In the past when Zhou perished, the Warring States contended together. The realm split apart, and only after several generations was it settled.

sentences.zh: 縱橫之事，復起於今乎？

translations.literal: Will the affairs of the Vertical and Horizontal alliances rise again in the present age?
translations.idiomatic: Will the affairs of the Vertical and Horizontal alliances rise again in the present age?

sentences.zh: 將承運迭興，在於一人也？

translations.literal: Or will fortune pass in succession and rise in a single man?
translations.idiomatic: Or will fortune pass in succession and rise in a single man?

sentences.zh: 願先生論之。

translations.literal: I wish you, sir, to discuss this."
translations.idiomatic: I wish you, sir, to discuss this."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「周之廢興與漢異。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The rise and fall of Zhou differ from Han.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "The rise and fall of Zhou differ from Han.

sentences.zh: 昔周立爵五等，諸侯從政，本根既微，枝葉強大，故其末流有縱橫之事，其勢然也。

translations.literal: In the past Zhou established five ranks of nobility; feudal lords shared in government — the root was already weak while branches and leaves were strong; therefore at the end there were affairs of Vertical and Horizontal alliances. Such was the force of circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Zhou established five ranks of nobility, and feudal lords shared in government. The root was already weak while branches and leaves were strong; therefore at the end there were affairs of Vertical and Horizontal alliances. Such was the force of circumstances.

sentences.zh: 漢家承秦之制，郡縣治民，主有專己之威，臣無百年之柄。

translations.literal: The Han house received Qin's system — commanderies and counties governed the people; the ruler had sole authority, and ministers had no power lasting a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: The Han house received Qin's system — commanderies and counties governed the people. The ruler held sole authority, and ministers had no power lasting a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 至於成帝，假借外家，哀、平短祚，國嗣三絕，禍自上起，傷不及下。

translations.literal: As for Emperor Cheng, power was lent to the maternal kin; Emperors Ai and Ping had short reigns, and the imperial succession was extinguished three times — calamity arose from above, and harm did not reach below.
translations.idiomatic: As for Emperor Cheng, power was lent to the maternal kin. Emperors Ai and Ping had short reigns, and the imperial succession was extinguished three times — calamity arose from above, and harm did not reach below.

sentences.zh: 故王氏之貴，傾擅朝廷，能竊號位，而不根於民，是以即真之後，天下莫不引領而歎。

translations.literal: Therefore the Wang family's nobility monopolized the court, able to usurp title and throne yet without roots among the people — hence after Wang Mang took the throne, none under heaven did not stretch their necks and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Wang family's nobility monopolized the court, able to usurp title and throne yet without roots among the people. Hence after Wang Mang took the throne, none under heaven did not stretch their necks and sigh.

sentences.zh: 十餘年間，中外騷擾，遠近俱發，假號雲合，咸稱劉氏，不謀而同辭。

translations.literal: Within a dozen years, turmoil spread at home and abroad; near and far all arose; those who assumed titles gathered like clouds, all calling themselves Liu — of one mind without prior consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Within a dozen years turmoil spread at home and abroad. Near and far all arose; those who assumed titles gathered like clouds, all calling themselves Liu — of one mind without prior consultation.

sentences.zh: 方今雄桀帶州域者，皆無七國世業之資。

translations.literal: The heroes and champions of today who hold commanderies within their grasp all lack the hereditary resources of the Seven Kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: The heroes and champions of today who hold commanderies within their grasp all lack the hereditary resources of the Seven Kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 詩云：『皇矣上帝，臨下有赫。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'Great is God on high, looking down below with majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: 'Great is God on high, looking down below with majesty.

sentences.zh: 鑒觀四方，求民之瘼。

translations.literal: Surveying the four directions, seeking the people's afflictions.'
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the four directions, seeking the people's afflictions.'

sentences.zh: 』今民皆謳吟思漢，向仰劉氏，已可知矣。

translations.literal: ' Now the people all sing and sigh, longing for Han, turning toward the Liu house — this can already be known."
translations.idiomatic: ' Now the people all sing and sigh, longing for Han, turning toward the Liu house — this can already be known."

sentences.zh: 」隗囂曰：「先生言周、漢之勢，可也。

translations.literal: " Wei Xiao said: "Sir, what you say about the fortunes of Zhou and Han is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Xiao said, "Sir, what you say about the fortunes of Zhou and Han is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 至於但見愚民習識劉氏姓號之故，而謂漢復興，疎矣。

translations.literal: As for merely seeing that ignorant people are accustomed to the Liu surname and title and therefore saying Han will revive — that is shallow.
translations.idiomatic: As for merely seeing that ignorant people are accustomed to the Liu surname and title and therefore saying Han will revive — that is shallow.

sentences.zh: 昔秦失其鹿，劉季逐而掎之，時民復知漢乎？

translations.literal: In the past Qin lost the deer; Liu Ji pursued and grappled for it — did the people then yet know of Han?"
translations.idiomatic: In the past Qin lost the deer; Liu Ji pursued and grappled for it — did the people then yet know of Han?"

sentences.zh: 」彪既感囂言，又愍狂狡之不息，乃著王命論以救時難。

translations.literal: " Biao, moved by Xiao's words and also grieving that mad and cunning men would not cease, thereupon composed the Discourse on the Mandate of Kings to rescue the age from calamity.
translations.idiomatic: " Biao, moved by Xiao's words and grieving that mad and cunning men would not cease, thereupon composed the Discourse on the Mandate of Kings to rescue the age from calamity.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：

translations.literal: The text reads:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: :昔在帝堯之禪曰：「咨爾舜，天之曆數在爾躬。

translations.literal: :In antiquity, at Emperor Yao's cession it was said: "Consult you, Shun — Heaven's allotted span is in your person."
translations.idiomatic: :In antiquity, at Emperor Yao's cession it was said, "Consult you, Shun — Heaven's allotted span is in your person."

sentences.zh: 」舜亦以命禹。

translations.literal: " Shun also used it to charge Yu.
translations.idiomatic: " Shun also used it to charge Yu.

sentences.zh: 洎于稷、契，咸佐唐、虞，光濟四海，奕世載德，至于湯、武，而有天下。

translations.literal: Down through Ji and Qi, all assisted Tang and Yu, their radiance aiding the four seas; generation after generation they carried virtue, down to Tang and Wu — and they possessed the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Ji and Qi, all assisted Tang and Yu, their radiance aiding the four seas. Generation after generation they carried virtue, down to Tang and Wu — and they possessed the realm.

sentences.zh: 雖其遭遇異時，禪代不同，至于應天從民，其揆一焉。

translations.literal: Though their encounters were in different times and their modes of abdication and succession differed, as for responding to Heaven and following the people, their measure was one.
translations.idiomatic: Though their encounters were in different times and their modes of abdication and succession differed, in responding to Heaven and following the people their measure was one.

sentences.zh: 是故劉氏承堯之祚，氏族之世，著于春秋。

translations.literal: Therefore the Liu house received Yao's mandate; the generations of the clan are recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Liu house received Yao's mandate, and the generations of the clan are recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 唐據火德，而漢紹之。

translations.literal: Tang held the virtue of Fire, and Han succeeded it.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's house stood for the element fire, and Han took up that line.

sentences.zh: 始起沛澤，則神母夜號，以章赤帝之符。

translations.literal: When it first arose in Pei marsh, the divine mother cried out in the night to manifest the token of the Red Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the first rising in the Pei marshes the spirit mother wailed by night to prove the Red Emperor's omen.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，帝王之祚，必有明聖顯懿之德，豐功厚利積累之業，然後精誠通于神明，流澤加於生民。

translations.literal: From this it may be said that the fortune of emperors and kings must have manifest sagely and brilliant virtue, enterprises of abundant merit and thick benefit accumulated layer upon layer; only then does essential sincerity penetrate the spirits, and flowing favor reaches the living people.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that imperial fortune demands luminous virtue and piled-up achievements before sincerity moves the spirits and blessing reaches the people.

sentences.zh: 故能為鬼神所福嚮，天下所歸往。

translations.literal: Therefore they can be blessed and favored by ghosts and spirits, and be the object to which all under Heaven turns.
translations.idiomatic: Then ghosts and spirits bless them and all under Heaven turns their way.

sentences.zh: 未見運世無本，功德不紀，而得堀起在此位者也。

translations.literal: One has never seen someone without root in the age's fortune, without recorded merit and virtue, who could yet vault up and occupy this position.
translations.idiomatic: No one has ever seen a man without mandate or merit vault onto this throne from nothing.

sentences.zh: 世俗見高祖興於布衣，不達其故，以為適遭暴亂，得奮其劍。

translations.literal: The vulgar world, seeing the Founding Ancestor rise from common cloth and not penetrating the reason, thinks he simply met violent disorder and was able to brandish his sword.
translations.idiomatic: Common opinion sees Gaozu rise from the ranks, misses the real cause, and thinks he merely seized a sword in chaotic times.

sentences.zh: 游說之士，至比天下於逐鹿，幸捷而得之。

translations.literal: Wandering persuaders even liken all under Heaven to chasing a deer, getting it by a lucky grab.
translations.idiomatic: Rhetoricians liken the realm to a deer hunt, won by whoever gets lucky.

sentences.zh: 不知神器有命，不可以智力求也。

translations.literal: They do not know that the divine regalia have a destined possessor and cannot be sought by wit or force.
translations.idiomatic: They miss that the sacred vessel answers only to fate, not to cunning or muscle.

sentences.zh: 悲夫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: A bitter pity.

sentences.zh: 此世之所以多亂臣賊子者也。

translations.literal: This is why the age has so many traitorous ministers and rebellious sons.
translations.idiomatic: That blindness is why treason and usurpation multiply.

sentences.zh: 若然者，豈徒闇於天道哉，又不覩之於人事矣。

translations.literal: If it is so, is it only darkness about the Way of Heaven? They have also failed to observe it in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If so, is the fault only ignorance of Heaven's Way? They have not even looked at the evidence of human affairs.

sentences.zh: :夫餓饉流隸，饑寒道路，思有裋褐之褻，檐石之畜，所願不過一金，然終於轉死溝壑。

translations.literal: :As for starving vagrants, the famished on the roads who long for the mean comfort of a short coat and stores of a few pecks of grain, whose desires reach no further than a single piece of gold, yet in the end they die turned over in ditches and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: :Starving drifters on the highway dream only of a patched coat, a sack of grain, a few coins of wealth—and still rot in the ditch.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is it so?
translations.idiomatic: Why should that be?

sentences.zh: 貧窮亦有命也。

translations.literal: Want and wealth also have their allotted fate.
translations.idiomatic: Even poverty and plenty ride an appointed lot.

sentences.zh: 況乎天子之貴，四海之富，神明之祚，可得而妄據哉！

translations.literal: How much more the honor of the Son of Heaven, the riches of the four seas, the blessing of the spirits—can these be seized recklessly?
translations.idiomatic: How then could anyone lightly seize the Son of Heaven's rank, the wealth of the realm, and the spirits' favor?

sentences.zh: 故雖遭罹厄會，竊其權柄，勇如信、布，強如梁、籍，成如王莽，然卒潤鑊伏鑕，烹菹分裂；

translations.literal: Therefore although they encountered hard straits and usurped the handles of power—brave as Xin and Bu, strong as Liang and Ji, accomplished as Wang Mang—still in the end they were boiled in the cauldron, exposed on the chopping block, diced in pickle and torn apart;
translations.idiomatic: Think of Xin, Bu, Xiang Yu, or even Wang Mang, who briefly seized power yet ended in the pot or on the block, diced and torn apart;

sentences.zh: 又況么麼不及數子，而欲闇干天位者乎？

translations.literal: How much more trifling mites who do not match those men yet would darkly encroach on Heaven's seat?
translations.idiomatic: What hope have petty upstarts far beneath them of darkly grasping the throne?

sentences.zh: 是故駑蹇之乘，不騁千里之塗；

translations.literal: Therefore a lame gelding does not gallop a thousand-li course;
translations.idiomatic: A cripple nag cannot run the thousand-mile road;

sentences.zh: 䴏雀之儔，不奮六翮之用；

translations.literal: a flock of swallows and sparrows does not spread six-pinioned flight;
translations.idiomatic: sparrows cannot soar like great birds;

sentences.zh: 楶梲之材，不荷棟梁之任；

translations.literal: rafter-end wood cannot bear the load of beams and pillars;
translations.idiomatic: splinter wood will not roof a hall;

sentences.zh: 斗筲之子，不秉帝王之重。

translations.literal: a peck-and-dipper fellow cannot sustain the weight of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: a small-minded man cannot wear the crown.

sentences.zh: 易曰：「鼎折足，覆公餗。

translations.literal: The Changes say: "The tripod breaks its legs and spills the duke's gruel.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou yi warns that when the tripod snaps its legs and spills the lord's porridge,

sentences.zh: 」不勝其任也。

translations.literal: " It could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: the office has outstripped the man.

sentences.zh: 當秦之末，豪桀共推陳嬰而王之。

translations.literal: At the end of Qin, the bold men together urged Chen Ying to take the kingly title.
translations.idiomatic: Near Qin's fall the warlords tried to crown Chen Ying.

sentences.zh: 嬰母止嬰曰：「自吾為子家婦，而世貧賤，卒富貴，不祥。

translations.literal: Ying's mother stopped him, saying: "Ever since I became your family's daughter-in-law, generation after generation we have been poor and base; to end in wealth and honor is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: His mother warned that sudden fortune after generations of poverty boded ill,

sentences.zh: 不如以兵屬人，事成，少受其利，不成，禍有所歸。

translations.literal: Better to hand the troops to another—if the affair succeeds you will receive a little benefit; if it fails disaster will have somewhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: and urged him to lend his army to a stronger leader so success would bring modest reward and failure would not crush the clan.

sentences.zh: 」嬰從其言，而陳氏以寧。

translations.literal: " Ying followed her words, and the Chen clan thereby enjoyed peace.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ying obeyed, and his house survived the wars unscathed.

sentences.zh: 王陵之母，亦見項氏之必亡，而劉氏之將興也。

translations.literal: The mother of Wang Ling also saw that the Xiang clan was sure to perish and the Liu house was about to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling's mother likewise saw that Xiang Yu would fall and Han would rise.

sentences.zh: 是時陵為漢將，而母獲於楚。

translations.literal: At that time Ling was a Han general, but his mother had been taken by Chu.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Ling served Han, his mother languished in Chu captivity.

sentences.zh: 有漢使來，陵母見之，謂曰：「願告吾子，漢王長者，必得天下，子謹事之，無有二心。

translations.literal: When a Han envoy arrived, Ling's mother saw him and said to him: "I beg you tell my son: the King of Han is a man of generous nature and is sure to gain all under Heaven; let him serve him carefully and harbor no second heart.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting a Han envoy she begged him to tell her son that Liu Bang was the true victor and deserved undivided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」遂對漢使，伏劍而死，以固勉陵。

translations.literal: " She thereupon fell on a sword before the Han envoy and died, thereby to firm Ling's resolve.
translations.idiomatic: She then drew a blade before the envoy and fell dead to steel her son's resolve.

sentences.zh: 其後果定於漢，陵為宰相封侯。

translations.literal: Afterward it was indeed settled with Han, and Ling became chancellor and was enfeoffed as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Han triumphed, Wang Ling rose to chancellor, and ennoblement followed.

sentences.zh: 夫以匹婦之明，猶能推事理之致，探禍福之機，全宗祀於無窮，垂冊書於春秋，而況大丈夫之事乎。

translations.literal: If by the insight of a mere woman one can still push principle to its limit, probe the pivot of fortune and disaster, and preserve the ancestral sacrifices without end, leaving one's record in the Spring and Autumn Annals, how much more the affairs of a great husband!
translations.idiomatic: If a woman's wit could read fate, save her lineage, and earn a line in the annals, how much more should a grown man grasp the mandate!

sentences.zh: 是故窮達有命，吉凶由人，嬰母知廢，陵母知興，審此二者，帝王之分決矣。

translations.literal: Therefore failure and success have their allotted fate, good and ill come from men; Ying's mother knew what to abolish, Ling's mother knew what would rise; when these two points are examined, the portion of emperors and kings is decided.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune governs rise and fall, yet human choice steers blessing or curse; Chen's mother knew whom to quit, Wang's mother knew whom to back, and those two judgments settle who may be king.

sentences.zh: :蓋在高祖，其興也有五：一曰帝堯之苗裔，二曰體貌多奇異，三曰神武有徵應，四曰寬明而仁恕，五曰知人善任使。

translations.literal: :As for the Founding Ancestor, there were five reasons for his rise: first, he was a descendant of Emperor Yao; second, his body and appearance held many marvels; third, his divine martial prowess had confirming omens; fourth, he was lenient, enlightened, humane, and forgiving; fifth, he knew men and employed them well.
translations.idiomatic: :Gaozu's ascent rested on five signs: Yao's bloodline, a singular physique, omens that blessed his arms, a generous humane temper, and a gift for placing the right men.

sentences.zh: 加之以信誠好謀，達於聽受，見善如不及，用人如由己，從諫如從流，趨時如響赴；

translations.literal: Add to this that he was trustworthy, sincere, fond of planning, open in hearing and accepting counsel; he saw good as if he could not catch up, employed men as if using himself, followed remonstrance like going with the current, and hastened to the timely moment as if answering a summons;
translations.idiomatic: He was candid, loved strategy, listened well, chased every good counsel, handed offices as freely as if they were his own limbs, took advice like running water, and seized each moment as though answering a call;

sentences.zh: 當食吐哺，納子房之策；

translations.literal: when it was time to eat he spat out his food and nursed his breast, adopting Zifang's plan;
translations.idiomatic: he spat out a mouthful mid-meal to enact Zhang Liang's scheme;

sentences.zh: 拔足揮洗，揖酈生之說；

translations.literal: he pulled off his foot and waved aside the washing, bowing to Lisheng's proposal;
translations.idiomatic: he broke off his bath to salute Li Yiji's plea;

sentences.zh: 寤戍卒之言，斷懷土之情；

translations.literal: he awoke to the words of garrison soldiers and cut short his longing for native soil;
translations.idiomatic: he heeded a guardsman's plea and checked his homesick march;

sentences.zh: 高四皓之名，割肌膚之愛；

translations.literal: he prized the fame of the Four Hoary Ones and sliced flesh-close affection;
translations.idiomatic: he courted the Four Elders though it cost him a father's love;

sentences.zh: 舉韓信於行陣，收陳平於亡命；

translations.literal: he raised Han Xin from the ranks of battle and gathered Chen Ping from life as a fugitive;
translations.idiomatic: He pulled Han Xin from the ranks and rescued Chen Ping from flight;

sentences.zh: 英雄陳力，羣才畢舉，此高祖之大略所以成帝業也。

translations.literal: heroes deployed their strength, every talent was offered: this was the Founding Ancestor's grand design whereby he completed the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: and let every able man lend strength until the imperial work was done.

sentences.zh: 若乃靈瑞符應，又可略聞矣。

translations.literal: As for numinous omens and confirming tokens, one may also hear them in outline.
translations.idiomatic: The portents that marked him deserve a word as well.

sentences.zh: 初劉媼任高祖而夢與神遇，震雷晦冥，有龍蛇之怪。

translations.literal: At first, when the elder Liu was pregnant with the Founding Ancestor, she dreamed of meeting a spirit; thunder flashed and the darkness was murky, with prodigies of dragons and serpents.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu dreamed of a spirit when she conceived him; thunder rolled in black sky and dragon shapes writhed.

sentences.zh: 及長多靈異，有殊於眾，是以王、武感物而折契，呂公覩貌而進女；

translations.literal: When he grew and showed many spiritual marvels, different from the multitude, therefore Wang and Wu were moved by things and tore their bonds, and Duke Lü, seeing his appearance, advanced his daughter;
translations.idiomatic: As he matured, uncanny signs set him apart, so Wang and Wu tore up old debts at a glance and Lü Gong married him a daughter for his bearing;

sentences.zh: 秦皇東遊以厭其氣，呂后望雲而知所處；

translations.literal: the First Emperor of Qin toured east to suppress his aura, and Empress Lü watched clouds to know where he dwelt;
translations.idiomatic: the Qin First Emperor toured east to smother his qi, while Empress Lü read clouds to find him;

sentences.zh: 始受命則白蛇分，西入關則五星聚。

translations.literal: when he first received the mandate the white serpent was cleft; when he entered Guan in the west the five planets gathered.
translations.idiomatic: His first mandate split the white serpent, and the five planets clustered when he entered the passes.

sentences.zh: 故淮陰、留侯謂之天授，非人力也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Marquis of Huaiyin and the Marquis of Liu called it Heaven's gift, not human power.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin and Zhang Liang called such things Heaven's investiture, not mortal striving.

sentences.zh: :歷古今之得失，驗行事之成敗，稽帝王之世運，考五者之所謂，取舍不厭斯位，符應不同斯度，而欲昧於權利，越次妄據，

translations.literal: :Reviewing the gains and losses of ancient and modern times, testing the success and failure of deeds done, examining the age's fortune of emperors and kings, investigating what these five mean, if in choosing and rejecting one does not shrink from this position, if auspicious tokens do not match this measure, yet one blindly covets power and profit, leaps out of order and occupies it rashly,
translations.idiomatic: :Survey history, weigh deeds, test the five signs of true kingship, and if you still covet the throne without the omens or the merit, if you blindly grasp for power and leap out of turn to seize the seat,

sentences.zh: 〈越次妄據　「次」各本並作「久」，據漢書序傳及文選卷五二所載改。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "leaps out of order and occupies it rashly": in all editions "order" is written as "long"; emended according to the Hanshu afterword and Wen xuan, juan 52.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "leaps out of order and occupies it rashly": all editions read "long" for "order"; corrected per the Hanshu afterword and Wen xuan, juan 52.〉

sentences.zh: 外不量力，內不知命，則必喪保家之主，失天年之壽，

translations.literal: outwardly not measuring strength, inwardly not knowing fate, then one is sure to lose the lord who could preserve the family, forfeit the years Heaven grants,
translations.idiomatic: outwardly overreaching and inwardly blind to fate, you invite family ruin and forfeit the years Heaven grants,

sentences.zh: 〈失天年之壽　「天年」各本並作「大年」，據漢書序傳及文選卷五二所載改。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "forfeit the years Heaven grants": in all editions "years Heaven grants" is written as "great years"; emended according to the Hanshu afterword and Wen xuan, juan 52.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "forfeit the years Heaven grants": all editions read "great years" for "years Heaven grants"; corrected per the Hanshu afterword and Wen xuan, juan 52.〉

sentences.zh: 遇折足之凶，伏鈇鉞之誅。

translations.literal: meet the misfortune of broken legs, and lie under the executioner's axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: meet the broken tripod's curse, and lie under the headsman's block.

sentences.zh: 英雄誠知覺寤，畏若禍戒，超然遠覽，淵然深識，收陵、嬰之明分，絕信、布之覬覦，距逐鹿之瞽說，審神器之有授，無貪不可幾，為二母之所笑，則福祚流于子孫，天祿其永終矣。

translations.literal: If heroes truly awaken in fear as if to omens of disaster, stand aloof with far-ranging sight, plumb the depths with silent understanding, take to heart the clear portions shown by Ling and Ying, cut off the covetous glances of Xin and Bu, reject the blind talk of deer-chasing, examine that the divine regalia have a recipient, do not greedily grasp what cannot be approached, and avoid being laughed at by the two mothers, then blessing and rank will flow to their sons and grandsons and Heaven's stipend will end only with time.
translations.idiomatic: Wake to that lesson, shun Xin and Bu's ambition, laugh off the deer hunt, respect Heaven's chosen vessel, and you may pass fortune to your heirs instead of becoming a jest to history's mothers.

sentences.zh: 隗囂不納，果敗。

translations.literal: Wei Xiao did not accept it; in the end he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao refused the warning and was destroyed in the end.

sentences.zh: 漢元、成世，道士言：「讖者云：『赤厄三七。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Yuandi and Chengdi of Han, Taoists said: "The prophetic texts say: 'Red calamity, three-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the reigns of Emperors Yuan and Cheng of Han, Taoists said, "The prophetic texts declare: 'Red calamity, three-seven.

sentences.zh: 』三七，二百一十年，有外戚之篡。

translations.literal: ' Three-seven means two hundred ten years; then will come usurpation by consort kin.
translations.idiomatic: ' Three-seven means two hundred ten years—then consort kin will usurp the throne.

sentences.zh: 祚極三六，當有龍飛之秀，興復祖宗。

translations.literal: When the mandate reaches three-six, there will be one of dragon-flight excellence who will revive the ancestral house.
translations.idiomatic: When the mandate reaches three-six, a dragon-rising hero will restore the ancestral house.

sentences.zh: 」及莽篡漢，漢二百一十年矣。

translations.literal: " When Wang Mang usurped Han, Han had indeed lasted two hundred ten years.
translations.idiomatic: " When Wang Mang usurped Han, the dynasty had indeed lasted two hundred ten years.

sentences.zh: 莽十八年而敗，光武興焉。

translations.literal: After eighteen years Mang failed, and Guangwu rose.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen years later Mang fell, and Guangwu rose.

sentences.zh: 明帝初生，豐下兌上，赤色似堯，終登帝位。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was first born, his lower part was broad and his upper part narrow, red in color resembling Yao; in the end he ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: At birth Emperor Ming's broad jaw and narrow forehead glowed red like Yao's; he went on to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 和帝鄧皇后，祖父禹，佐命光武，常曰：「我將百萬人，未嘗妄殺一人，子孫當大興。

translations.literal: Empress Deng of Emperor He—her grandfather Yu, who aided Guangwu in receiving the mandate, often said: "I have led a million men and never killed a person without cause; my descendants will surely flourish greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Deng of Emperor He was granddaughter of Yu, who had helped Guangwu win the throne; he often said, "I have led a million men and never killed without cause—my line will flourish.

sentences.zh: 」后少時，相者蘇文見后，

translations.literal: " When the empress was young, the physiognomist Su Wen saw the empress,
translations.idiomatic: " When she was young the physiognomist Su Wen saw her,

sentences.zh: 〈相者蘇文見后　「蘇文」各本並作「蘇大」，據後漢書和熹鄧皇后傳李賢注引續漢書改。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "the physiognomist Su Wen saw the empress": in all editions "Su Wen" is written as "Su Da"; emended according to Li Xian's commentary on the Hou Hanshu biography of Empress Hexi Deng, citing the Xu Hanshu.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "the physiognomist Su Wen saw the empress": all editions read "Su Da" for "Su Wen"; corrected per Li Xian's Hou Hanshu commentary citing the Xu Hanshu.〉

sentences.zh: 驚曰：「此成湯之骨法也，貴不可言。

translations.literal: startled, said: "This is the bone pattern of Cheng Tang; nobility beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: and cried in astonishment, "This is the bone pattern of Cheng Tang—nobility beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」后嘗夢登梯，以手捫天，天體蕩蕩正青而滑，有若鍾乳者，后仰吮之。

translations.literal: " The empress once dreamed she climbed a ladder, reached up with her hand and touched heaven; the heavenly body was vast, clear blue and smooth, like stalactites; she raised her head back and sucked them.
translations.idiomatic: " She once dreamed she climbed a ladder, touched heaven with her hand, found the sky vast, clear blue and smooth like stalactites, and raised her head to sip and drink.

sentences.zh: 以訊之占夢。

translations.literal: She put the question to dream diviners.
translations.idiomatic: She asked the dream interpreters.

sentences.zh: 占夢者曰：「堯夢攀天而上，

translations.literal: The dream diviners said: "Yao dreamed of climbing heaven and ascending,
translations.idiomatic: They said, "Yao dreamed of climbing to heaven,

sentences.zh: 〈堯夢攀天而上　各本並作「堯攀天而止」，據後漢書和熹鄧皇后傳補正。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "Yao dreamed of climbing heaven and ascending": in all editions it reads "Yao climbed heaven and stopped"; supplemented and corrected according to the Hou Hanshu biography of Empress Hexi Deng.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "Yao dreamed of climbing heaven and ascending": all editions read "Yao climbed heaven and stopped"; corrected per the Hou Hanshu biography of Empress Hexi Deng.〉

sentences.zh: 湯夢及天而[口+氏]之，

translations.literal: Tang dreamed of reaching heaven and licking it,
translations.idiomatic: Tang dreamed of reaching heaven and licking it,

sentences.zh: 〈湯夢及天而[口+氏]之　「[口+氏]」後漢書和熹鄧皇后傳作「咶」。

translations.literal: 〈On "Tang dreamed of reaching heaven and licking it": the character for "lick" in the Hou Hanshu biography of Empress Hexi Deng is written as "gua."
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "Tang dreamed of reaching heaven and licking it": the Hou Hanshu biography of Empress Hexi Deng writes the lick-character as "gua."

sentences.zh: 按說文：「舓，以舌取食也。

translations.literal: According to the Shuowen: "Shi, to take food with the tongue.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuowen defines the character shi as "to take food with the tongue."

sentences.zh: 從舌易聲。

translations.literal: From the 'tongue' radical with 'yi' as phonetic.
translations.idiomatic: It combines the tongue radical with yi as phonetic.

sentences.zh: 或從也作𦧇。

translations.literal: Or with 'ye' it is written as [variant form].
translations.idiomatic: With ye as phonetic it appears in another variant form.

sentences.zh: 」段玉裁注云：「[口+氏]或作舐，或作狧。

translations.literal: " Duan Yucai's commentary says: "[mouth+shi] may be written as shi or ta.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yucai notes that the mouth-plus-shi form may also be written shi or ta.

sentences.zh: 」此「[口+氏]」字，蓋又「舐」之省文。〉

translations.literal: " This character is probably an abbreviated form of shi (to lick).〉
translations.idiomatic: This mouth-plus-shi character is probably an abbreviated form of shi, "to lick."〉

sentences.zh: 此皆非常夢也。

translations.literal: These are all extraordinary dreams.
translations.idiomatic: These were all extraordinary dreams.

sentences.zh: 」既而入宮，遂登尊位。

translations.literal: " Thereafter she entered the palace and ascended the exalted throne.
translations.idiomatic: " She then entered the palace and ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 安帝未即大位，在邸，數有神光赤蛇嘉應，照曜室內，磐紆殿屋牀第之間，後遂入承大統。

translations.literal: Before Emperor An took the great throne, while he was at the princely residence, there were repeatedly auspicious responses of divine light and a red serpent, shining within the rooms and coiling among the hall, roof beams, bed, and mat; afterward he entered and succeeded to the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before Emperor An took the throne, while he still lived at his princely residence, divine light and a red serpent repeatedly appeared as auspicious signs, shining through the rooms and coiling among hall beams and bed curtains; he later entered and succeeded to the great succession.

sentences.zh: 初桓帝之世，有黃星見於楚、宋之分。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Huan's reign, a yellow star appeared in the division between Chu and Song.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Huan's reign a yellow star appeared over the Chu–Song sky sector.

sentences.zh: 遼東殷馗曰：「後五十年，當有真人起於譙、沛之間，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Yin Kui of Liaodong said: "After fifty years a true man will rise between Qiao and Pei; his edge cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Kui of Liaodong said, "Within fifty years a true man will rise between Qiao and Pei, and his force will be irresistible.

sentences.zh: 」靈帝熹平五年，黃龍見譙。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year of Xiping under Emperor Ling, a yellow dragon appeared at Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth year of Xiping under Emperor Ling, a yellow dragon appeared at Qiao.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫橋玄問太史令單颺曰：

translations.literal: Grand Counselor of the Household Qiao Xuan asked the Grand Astrologer Shan Yang, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor of the Household Qiao Xuan asked Grand Astrologer Shan Yang,

sentences.zh: 〈光祿大夫橋玄問太史令單颺曰　「橋玄」各本並作「喬玄」，據三國志魏志武帝紀改。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "Grand Counselor of the Household Qiao Xuan asked the Grand Astrologer Shan Yang, saying": in all editions "Qiao Xuan" is written as "Qiao Xuan" with a different first character; emended according to the Sanguo zhi biography of Emperor Wu in the Wei Annals.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "Grand Counselor of the Household Qiao Xuan asked Grand Astrologer Shan Yang": all editions write a homophone for Qiao Xuan's surname; corrected per the Sanguo zhi biography of Emperor Wu.〉

sentences.zh: 「此何祥也？

translations.literal: "What kind of auspice is this?
translations.idiomatic: "What omen is this?

sentences.zh: 」颺曰：「其國後當有王者興，不及五十年，亦當復見天事恒象，此其徵也。

translations.literal: " Yang said: "Afterwards in this state a king will arise; before fifty years have passed, the constant signs of Heaven's affairs should also appear again—this is its token.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Yang answered, "This land will one day produce a true king; within fifty years Heaven's constant signs should appear again—this is the token."

sentences.zh: 」內黃殷登默記之。

translations.literal: " Yin Deng of Neihuang silently recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Deng of Neihuang quietly committed the prophecy to memory.

sentences.zh: 其後曹操起於譙，是為魏武帝。

translations.literal: Afterward Cao Cao rose at Qiao; this was Emperor Wu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cao Cao rose at Qiao—this was Emperor Wu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 建安五年，於黃星見之，歲五十年矣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jian'an, when the yellow star appeared, fifty years had passed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jian'an, when the yellow star appeared, fifty years had passed.

sentences.zh: 而武帝破袁紹，天下莫敵。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu broke Yuan Shao, and none under Heaven could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu broke Yuan Shao, and none under Heaven could match him.

sentences.zh: 春秋讖曰：「代漢者，當塗高也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn prophecy says: "He who replaces Han will be tall by the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn prophecy says, "The one who replaces Han shall be the height by the road."

sentences.zh: 」漢有周舒者，善內學。

translations.literal: " In Han there was one Zhou Shu, skilled in inner learning.
translations.idiomatic: In Han there was Zhou Shu, skilled in occult learning.

sentences.zh: 人或問之，舒曰：「當塗高者，魏也。

translations.literal: When someone asked him, Shu said: "Tall by the road means Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked him, Zhou Shu answered that "tall by the road" meant Wei.

sentences.zh: 」舒既沒，譙周又問術士杜瓊曰：「周徵君以為當塗高，魏也。

translations.literal: " After Shu had died, Qiao Zhou again asked the adept Du Qiong, saying: "Master Zhou held that tall by the road is Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Shu died, Qiao Zhou asked the adept Du Qiong, "Master Zhou held that 'tall by the road' meant Wei.

sentences.zh: 其義何在？

translations.literal: Where lies the meaning?
translations.idiomatic: What is the reasoning?

sentences.zh: 」瓊曰：「魏，闕名也。

translations.literal: " Qiong said: "Wei is the name of the palace gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qiong replied that wei was the name of the palace gate tower.

sentences.zh: 當塗而高，聖人以類言耳。

translations.literal: Standing on the road and high—the sage spoke by analogy, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Blocking the road and high—the sage had spoken by analogy.

sentences.zh: 」又問周曰：「寧復有所怪邪？

translations.literal: " He again asked Zhou: "Might there still be something strange about it?
translations.idiomatic: He asked Zhou again, "Is there still something odd about it?

sentences.zh: 」周曰：「未達也。

translations.literal: " Zhou said: "I have not yet understood.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said, "I have not yet understood.

sentences.zh: 」瓊曰：「古者名官職不言曹，自漢以來，名官盡言曹，吏言屬曹，卒言侍曹，此殆天意也。

translations.literal: " Qiong said: "In antiquity naming offices did not say cao; since Han onward, naming offices all say cao—clerks speak of belonging to a cao, runners speak of attending cao; this is probably Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qiong said, "Ancient offices were not called cao, but since Han every bureau has been called cao—clerks belong to cao, runners attend cao; this is probably Heaven's intent."

sentences.zh: 」周曰：「魏者，大也。

translations.literal: " Zhou said: "Wei — this means 'great.'
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou said, "Wei — this means 'great.'

sentences.zh: 曹者，眾也。

translations.literal: Cao — this means 'the multitude.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao — this means 'the multitude.'

sentences.zh: 眾而且大，天下之所歸乎。

translations.literal: Multitudinous and moreover great — toward this all under Heaven turns, does it not?
translations.idiomatic: Multitudinous and great — is this not what all under Heaven turns toward?

sentences.zh: 」建安十八年，武帝為公，又進爵為王。

translations.literal: " In the eighteenth year of Jian'an, Emperor Wu became Duke, then was further ennobled as King.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighteenth year of Jian'an, Emperor Wu became Duke and was further ennobled as King.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，武帝薨，太子丕嗣為魏王，是為文帝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Emperor Wu passed away; Crown Prince Pi succeeded as King of Wei — this was Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, Emperor Wu died; Crown Prince Pi succeeded as King of Wei — this was Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 文帝始生，有雲青色，圓如車蓋，當其上終日。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was first born, there was a green cloud, round as a chariot canopy, remaining above him all day.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was born, a green cloud round as a chariot canopy hovered above him all day.

sentences.zh: 望氣者以為至貴之祥，非人臣之氣。

translations.literal: Those who read the heavens' vapors took it for an omen of supreme nobility — not the qi of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Those who read celestial signs took it as an omen of supreme nobility — not the aura of a subject.

sentences.zh: 善相者高元呂曰：「其貴不可言。

translations.literal: The skilled physiognomist Gao Yuanlu said: "His nobility cannot be put into words.
translations.idiomatic: The skilled physiognomist Gao Yuanlu said, "His nobility is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」延康元年三月，黃龍又見譙，殷登猶存，歎曰：「黃龍見於熹平也，單颺云：『不及五十年，亦當復見。

translations.literal: " In the third month of the first year of Yankang, a yellow dragon again appeared at Qiao. Yin Deng was still alive and sighed: "When the yellow dragon appeared in the Xiping era, Shan Yang said: 'Within fifty years it should appear again.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third month of the first year of Yankang, a yellow dragon again appeared at Qiao. Yin Deng was still alive and sighed, "When the yellow dragon appeared in the Xiping era, Shan Yang said, 'Within fifty years it should appear again.

sentences.zh: 』今四十五年矣，颺之言其驗茲乎。

translations.literal: ' Now forty-five years have passed — has Yang's word been fulfilled in this?
translations.idiomatic: ' Now forty-five years have passed — has Yang's prophecy been fulfilled in this?

sentences.zh: 」四月，饒安言白虎見。

translations.literal: " In the fourth month, Rao'an reported that a white tiger appeared.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth month, Rao'an reported that a white tiger had appeared.

sentences.zh: 〈四月饒安言白虎見　「四月」各本並作「十月」，下又出八月，今據符瑞志改。

translations.literal: 〈In the fourth month Rao'an reported that a white tiger appeared — all editions read "tenth month" rather than "fourth month"; since the eighth month appears below, emended per the Treatise on Auspicious Signs.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈In the fourth month Rao'an reported that a white tiger appeared — all editions read "tenth month" rather than "fourth month"; since the eighth month appears below, emended according to the Treatise on Auspicious Signs.〉

sentences.zh: 符瑞志中云：「延康元年四月丁巳，饒安縣言白虎見。」〉

translations.literal: The Treatise on Auspicious Signs states: "On dingsi day in the fourth month of the first year of Yankang, Rao'an County reported that a white tiger appeared."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Auspicious Signs states: "On dingsi day in the fourth month of the first year of Yankang, Rao'an County reported that a white tiger appeared."〉

sentences.zh: 八月，石邑言鳳凰集，又有麒麟見。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Shiyi reported that the phoenix gathered, and a qilin also appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Shiyi reported that phoenixes had gathered, and a qilin also appeared.

sentences.zh: 十月，漢帝禪位於魏，魏王辭讓不受，博士蘇林、董巴上言：「臣聞天之去就，固有常分，聖人當之，昭然不疑。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Han emperor abdicated in favor of Wei; the King of Wei declined and refused to accept. Academicians Su Lin and Dong Ba submitted a memorial: "We have heard that Heaven's coming and going has its fixed allotment; when the sage receives it, clearly and without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, the Han emperor abdicated in favor of Wei; the King of Wei declined and refused to accept. Academicians Su Lin and Dong Ba submitted a memorial: "We have heard that Heaven's coming and going follows a fixed order; when the sage receives the mandate, he does so clearly and without doubt.

sentences.zh: 故堯捐骨肉而禪有虞，終無吝色。

translations.literal: Therefore Yao relinquished his flesh and blood and abdicated to You Yu — to the end he showed no reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Yao gave up his own kin and abdicated to You Yu — yet to the end he showed no reluctance.

sentences.zh: 舜發壟畝而居天下，若固有之。

translations.literal: Shun rose from the furrows and took possession of the realm, as though he had held it all along.
translations.idiomatic: Shun rose from the fields and took possession of the realm, as though it had always been his.

sentences.zh: 其相授間，不稽漏刻，天下已傳矣。

translations.literal: Between their mutual investiture, not a water-clock drip was delayed — all under Heaven was already handed over.
