translations.idiomatic: Between their successive investitures, not a single drip of the water clock was delayed — all under Heaven had already been transferred.

sentences.zh: 所以急天命，明天下不可一日無君。

translations.literal: This is why they hurried the Mandate of Heaven — to make clear that the realm cannot go a single day without a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: This is why they hastened the Mandate of Heaven — to show that the realm cannot go a single day without a ruler.

sentences.zh: 今漢期運已終，妖異絕之已審。

translations.literal: Now the Han dynasty's allotted term has ended; portents cutting it off have been thoroughly confirmed.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Han dynasty's allotted span has ended; omens foretelling its severance have been thoroughly confirmed.

sentences.zh: 陛下受天之命，符瑞告徵，丁寧詳悉，反覆備至，雖言語相諭，無以代此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has received Heaven's mandate; auspicious tokens proclaim the signs — earnest, detailed, repeated to fullness — though words may instruct one another, nothing can substitute for this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has received Heaven's mandate; auspicious tokens proclaim the signs — earnest, detailed, and repeated to the full — and though words may instruct one another, nothing can take the place of this.

sentences.zh: 今既發詔書，璽綬未御，固執謙讓，上稽天命，下違民情。

translations.literal: Now the decree has already been issued, yet the seal and cord have not been assumed; holding stubbornly to humility and refusal — above it delays Heaven's mandate, below it goes against the people's will.
translations.idiomatic: Now the decree has already been issued, yet the seal and cord have not been assumed; by stubbornly clinging to humility and refusal, you delay Heaven's mandate above and go against the people's will below.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按古之典籍，參以圖緯，魏之行運及天道所在，即尊之驗，在於今年此月，昭晢分明。

translations.literal: We respectfully examine the ancient canonical texts, cross-reference the charts and weft-texts — Wei's cycle of fortune and the place where Heaven's Way resides: the verification of elevation is in this year and this month, clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully examine the ancient canonical texts and cross-reference the charts and weft-texts — Wei's cycle of fortune and the place where Heaven's Way resides: the proof of elevation falls in this year and this month, clear and unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 謹條奏如左。

translations.literal: We respectfully itemize and submit as follows.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully itemize and submit as follows.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下遷思易慮，以時即位，顯告上帝，布詔天下。

translations.literal: We only ask that Your Majesty change your thoughts and shift your considerations, take the throne in timely fashion, proclaim this clearly to High God, and issue the edict to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We only ask that Your Majesty reconsider and change your mind, take the throne at the proper time, proclaim this clearly to High God, and issue an edict to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 然後改正朔，易服色，正大號，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Then alter the calendar and first month, change the court colors, establish the great title — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: Then revise the calendar and first month, change the court colors, and establish the great title — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 」其所陳事曰：

translations.literal: " What they presented read:
translations.idiomatic: " What they presented read:

sentences.zh: :天有十二次，以為分野，王公之國，各有所屬。

translations.literal: Heaven has twelve stations, taken as territorial divisions; the domains of kings and dukes each have their allotted correspondences.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has twelve stations, which serve as territorial divisions; the domains of kings and dukes each have their allotted correspondences.

sentences.zh: 周在鶉火，魏在大梁，歲星行歷，凡十二次，所在國天子受命，諸侯以封。

translations.literal: Zhou was at Quail Fire; Wei is at Great Bridge. The Year Star traverses twelve stations in its course; in whichever country it resides, the Son of Heaven receives the mandate and feudal lords are enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou lay in Quail Fire; Wei lies in Great Bridge. The Year Star passes through twelve stations in its course; wherever it resides, the Son of Heaven receives the mandate and feudal lords are enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 周文王始受命，歲星在鶉火，至武王伐紂，十三年，歲星復在鶉火。

translations.literal: When King Wen of Zhou first received the mandate, the Year Star was at Quail Fire; when King Wu attacked Zhou, thirteen years had passed, and the Year Star was again at Quail Fire.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wen of Zhou first received the mandate, the Year Star was at Quail Fire; when King Wu attacked Zhou thirteen years later, the Year Star was again at Quail Fire.

sentences.zh: 故春秋傳曰：「武王伐紂，歲在鶉火。

translations.literal: Therefore the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals says: "When King Wu attacked Zhou, the year-star was at Quail Fire.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals says, "When King Wu attacked Zhou, the year-star was at Quail Fire.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「歲之所在，則我有周之分野也。

translations.literal: " It also says: "Where the year-star stands — that is the territorial allotment of our Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says, "Where the year-star stands — that is the territorial allotment of our Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」昔光和七年，

translations.literal: " In the seventh year of the Guanghe era,
translations.idiomatic: " In the seventh year of the Guanghe era,

sentences.zh: 〈昔光和七年　「七年」各本並作「十七年」。

translations.literal: 〈In the seventh year of Guanghe — all editions read "seventeenth year" rather than "seventh year."
translations.idiomatic: 〈In the seventh year of Guanghe — all editions read "seventeenth year" rather than "seventh year."

sentences.zh: 按後漢書靈帝紀，光和止七年，其年十二月，改元中平。

translations.literal: According to the Annals of Emperor Ling in the Hou Hanshu, Guanghe lasted only seven years; in the twelfth month of that year the reign era was changed to Zhongping.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Annals of Emperor Ling in the Hou Hanshu, Guanghe lasted only seven years; in the twelfth month of that year the reign era was changed to Zhongping.

sentences.zh: 「十」字衍文，今刪去。〉

translations.literal: The character "ten" is a superfluous interpolation; it is now deleted.〉
translations.idiomatic: The character "ten" is a superfluous interpolation; it is now deleted.〉

sentences.zh: 歲在大梁，武王始受命為將，討黃巾。

translations.literal: The Year Star was at Great Bridge; Emperor Wu first received the mandate as a general and campaigned against the Yellow Turbans.
translations.idiomatic: The Year Star was at Great Bridge; Emperor Wu first received the mandate as a general and campaigned against the Yellow Turbans.

sentences.zh: 是歲改年為中平元年。

translations.literal: In that year the era name was changed to the first year of Zhongping.
translations.idiomatic: In that year the era name was changed to the first year of Zhongping.

sentences.zh: 建安元年，歲復在大梁，始拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jian'an, the Year Star was again at Great Bridge; he was first appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jian'an, the Year Star was again at Great Bridge; he was first appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復在大梁，始拜丞相。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, again at Great Bridge; he was first appointed Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, again at Great Bridge; he was first appointed Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 今二十五年，歲復在大梁，陛下受命。

translations.literal: Now in the twenty-fifth year, the Year Star is again at Great Bridge; Your Majesty has received the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the twenty-fifth year, the Year Star is again at Great Bridge; Your Majesty has received the mandate.

sentences.zh: 此魏得歲與周文、武受命相應。

translations.literal: This is Wei gaining the Year Star — corresponding to Zhou Wen and Wu receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: This is Wei gaining the Year Star — corresponding to Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou receiving the mandate.

sentences.zh: :今年青龍在庚子，詩推度災曰：「庚者，更也。

translations.literal: This year the Azure Dragon is at gengzi. The Poetic Interpretation of Measuring Calamities says: "Geng means 'change.'
translations.idiomatic: This year the Azure Dragon is at gengzi. The Poetic Interpretation of Measuring Calamities says, "Geng means 'change.'

sentences.zh: 子者，茲也。

translations.literal: Zi means 'this.'
translations.idiomatic: Zi means 'this.'

sentences.zh: 聖人制法天下治。

translations.literal: The sage establishes institutions and the realm is governed.
translations.idiomatic: The sage establishes institutions and the realm is governed.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「王者布德於子，治成於丑。

translations.literal: " It also says: "The king spreads virtue in zi; governance is perfected in chou.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says, "The king spreads virtue in zi; governance is perfected in chou.

sentences.zh: 」此言今年天更命聖人，制法天下，布德於民也。

translations.literal: " This says that this year Heaven changes the mandate to a sage — establishes institutions for the realm, spreads virtue among the people.
translations.idiomatic: " This means that this year Heaven changes the mandate to a sage — establishes institutions for the realm and spreads virtue among the people.

sentences.zh: 魏以改制天下，

translations.literal: Wei remakes institutions for the realm,
translations.idiomatic: Wei remakes institutions for the realm,

sentences.zh: 〈魏以改制天下　「改」各本並作「政」，據三國志魏志文帝紀裴注所引改。〉

translations.literal: 〈Wei remakes institutions for the realm — all editions read "governs" rather than "remakes"; emended per Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Annals of Emperor Wen in the Wei section of the Sanguo Zhi.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Wei remakes institutions for the realm — all editions read "governs" rather than "remakes"; emended according to Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Annals of Emperor Wen in the Wei section of the Sanguo Zhi.〉

sentences.zh: 與詩協矣。

translations.literal: in accord with the Poetic Interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: in accord with the Poetic Interpretation.

sentences.zh: 顓頊受命，歲在豕韋，衞居其地，亦在豕韋。

translations.literal: When Zhuanxu received the mandate, the year was at Boar-Wei; the domain of Wey occupied that place — also at Boar-Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuanxu received the mandate, the year was at Boar-Wei; the domain of Wey lay in that place — also at Boar-Wei.

sentences.zh: 故春秋傳曰：「衛，顓頊之墟也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Zuo Commentary says: "Wey — the ruins of Zhuanxu.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Zuo Commentary says, "Wey — the ruins of Zhuanxu.

sentences.zh: 」今十月，斗之所建，則顓頊受命之分也。

translations.literal: " Now the tenth month is where the Dipper sets its marker — the allotment of Zhuanxu's reception of the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: " Now the tenth month is where the Dipper sets its marker — the allotment of Zhuanxu's reception of the mandate.

sentences.zh: 魏以十月受禪，此同符始祖受命之驗也。

translations.literal: Wei received the abdication in the tenth month — this matches the verification of the primal ancestor receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Wei received the abdication in the tenth month — this matches the proof of the primal ancestor receiving the mandate.

sentences.zh: 三國

translations.literal: Three Kingdoms
translations.idiomatic: Three Kingdoms

sentences.zh: 魏之氏族，出自顓頊，與舜同祖，見于春秋世家。

translations.literal: The clan of Wei sprang from Zhuanxu, sharing an ancestor with Shun — as seen in the Hereditary Houses of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: The clan of Wei sprang from Zhuanxu and shared an ancestor with Shun — as recorded in the Hereditary Houses of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 舜以土德承堯之火，今魏亦以土德承漢之火，其於行運合於堯、舜授受之次。

translations.literal: Shun with the virtue of Earth succeeded Yao's Fire; now Wei also with Earth virtue succeeds Han's Fire — in cyclical fortune it conforms to the sequence of Yao and Shun's handover.
translations.idiomatic: Shun with the virtue of Earth succeeded Yao's Fire; now Wei also with Earth virtue succeeds Han's Fire — in cyclical fortune it matches the sequence of the transfer between Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 魏王猶未許。

translations.literal: The King of Wei still had not assented.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wei still had not assented.

sentences.zh: 太史丞許芝又上天文祥瑞：

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Assistant Xu Zhi also submitted astronomical auspicious signs:
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Assistant Xu Zhi also submitted astronomical auspicious signs:

sentences.zh: :自建安三年十二月戊辰，有新天子氣見於東南，到今積二十三年。

translations.literal: From the third year of Jian'an, on wuchen day of the twelfth month, a new Son-of-Heaven qi appeared in the southeast — accumulating to twenty-three years to the present.
translations.idiomatic: From the third year of Jian'an, on wuchen day of the twelfth month, a new Son-of-Heaven aura appeared in the southeast — twenty-three years have accumulated to the present.

sentences.zh: 建安十年，茀星出庫樓，歷犯氐、房宿，北入天市，犯北斗、紫微。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jian'an, the Broom Star emerged from Storehouse Tower, passing through and invading the lodges Di and Fang, entering the Celestial Market northward, invading the Northern Dipper and Purple Forbidden Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jian'an, the Broom Star emerged from Storehouse Tower, passing through and invading the lodges Di and Fang, entering the Celestial Market northward and invading the Northern Dipper and Purple Forbidden Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 氐為天子宿宮，路寢所止。

translations.literal: Di is the lodge of the Son of Heaven's resting palace — where the inner bedroom stops.
translations.idiomatic: Di is the lodge of the Son of Heaven's resting palace — where the inner bedroom lies.

sentences.zh: 房為天子明堂政教之首。

translations.literal: Fang is the head of the Son of Heaven's Bright Hall of governance and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Fang is the head of the Son of Heaven's Bright Hall of governance and instruction.

sentences.zh: 北斗七星，主尊輔象近臣。

translations.literal: The Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper govern honored assistants — emblems of close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper govern honored assistants — emblems of close ministers.

sentences.zh: 紫微者，北極最尊。

translations.literal: Purple Forbidden Enclosure — most honored at the Northern Pole.
translations.idiomatic: The Purple Forbidden Enclosure — most honored at the Northern Pole.

sentences.zh: 此除掃漢家之大異也。

translations.literal: This is the great anomaly of sweeping away and clearing the Han house.
translations.idiomatic: This is the great omen of sweeping away and clearing the Han house.

sentences.zh: 建安十八年秋，歲星、鎮星、熒惑俱入太微，逆行留守帝坐百有餘日。

translations.literal: In autumn of the eighteenth year of Jian'an, the Year Star, the Stationary Star, and the Sparkling Deluder all entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure, moving retrograde and remaining stationed at the Imperial Seat for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the eighteenth year of Jian'an, the Year Star, the Stationary Star, and the Sparkling Deluder all entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure, moving retrograde and remaining at the Imperial Seat for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 歲星入太微，人主改姓。

translations.literal: When the Year Star enters the Supreme Palace Enclosure, the ruler's house changes surname.
translations.idiomatic: When the Year Star enters the Supreme Palace Enclosure, the ruling house changes surname.

sentences.zh: 鎮星入太微，內有兵亂，人主以弱。

translations.literal: When the Stationary Star enters the Supreme Palace Enclosure, there is military disorder within and the ruler is weakened.
translations.idiomatic: When the Stationary Star enters the Supreme Palace Enclosure, there is internal military disorder and the ruler is weakened.

sentences.zh: 三者，漢改姓易代之異也。

translations.literal: These three — anomalies of the Han house changing surname and exchanging dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: These three are omens of the Han house changing surname and exchanging dynasties.

sentences.zh: 建安十九年正月，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year of Jian'an, a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the nineteenth year of Jian'an, a white rainbow pierced the sun.

sentences.zh: 易傳曰：「后妃擅國，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Changes says: "When empress and consorts monopolize the realm, a white rainbow pierces the sun.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Changes says, "When empresses and consorts monopolize the realm, a white rainbow pierces the sun.

sentences.zh: 」建安二十一年五月朔己亥，日蝕。

translations.literal: " On the new moon of the fifth month of the twenty-first year of Jian'an, on jihai day, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: " On the new moon of the fifth month of the twenty-first year of Jian'an, on jihai day, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 建安二十三年三月，茀星晨見東方二十餘日，夕出西方，犯歷五車、東井、五諸侯、文昌、軒轅、太微，鋒炎刺帝坐。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-third year of Jian'an, the Broom Star appeared at dawn in the east for more than twenty days, at dusk emerging in the west, invading and passing through the Five Chariots, Well, Five Feudal Lords, Literary Glory, Chariot Pivot, and Supreme Palace Enclosure — its blazing tip stabbing the Imperial Seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-third year of Jian'an, the Broom Star appeared at dawn in the east for more than twenty days and at dusk emerged in the west, invading and passing through the Five Chariots, Well, Five Feudal Lords, Literary Glory, Chariot Pivot, and Supreme Palace Enclosure — its blazing tip stabbing the Imperial Seat.

sentences.zh: 茀者除舊布新，亡惡興聖之異也。

translations.literal: The Broom Star — anomaly of clearing out the old and spreading the new, extinguishing evil and raising the sage.
translations.idiomatic: The Broom Star — an omen of clearing out the old and spreading the new, extinguishing evil and raising the sage.

sentences.zh: 建安二十四年二月晦壬子，日蝕。

translations.literal: In the last day of the second month of the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an, on renzi day, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the second month of the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an, on renzi day, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 日者陽精，月為侯王，而以亥子日蝕，皆水滅火之異也。

translations.literal: The sun is yang essence; the moon is emblem of feudal lords and kings — yet eclipses on hai and zi days are all anomalies of water extinguishing fire.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is yang essence; the moon is the emblem of feudal lords and kings — yet eclipses on hai and zi days are all omens of water extinguishing fire.

sentences.zh: 延康元年九月十日黃昏時，月蝕熒惑，過人定時，熒惑出營室，宿羽林。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the ninth month of the first year of Yankang, at dusk, there was a lunar eclipse of the Sparkling Deluder; past the hour of Human Settlement, the Sparkling Deluder emerged from Encampment and lodged at Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the ninth month of the first year of Yankang, at dusk, the moon eclipsed the Sparkling Deluder; past the hour of Human Settlement, the Sparkling Deluder emerged from Encampment and lodged at Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 月為大臣侯王之象；

translations.literal: The moon is emblem of great ministers and feudal kings;
translations.idiomatic: The moon is the emblem of great ministers and feudal kings;

sentences.zh: 熒惑火精，漢氏之行。

translations.literal: The Sparkling Deluder is fire essence — the cyclical phase of the Han house.
translations.idiomatic: The Sparkling Deluder is fire essence — the cyclical phase of the Han house.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「漢家以兵亡。

translations.literal: Astrology says: "The Han house will perish by arms.
translations.idiomatic: Astrology says, "The Han house will perish by arms.

sentences.zh: 」延康元年九月二十日，剝卦天子氣不見，皆崩亡之異也。

translations.literal: " On the twentieth day of the ninth month of the first year of Yankang, the hexagram Stripping's Son-of-Heaven qi was no longer visible — all anomalies of collapse and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: " On the twentieth day of the ninth month of the first year of Yankang, the Son-of-Heaven aura of the hexagram Stripping was no longer visible — all omens of collapse and extinction.

sentences.zh: 熒惑火精，行縮日一度有餘。

translations.literal: The Sparkling Deluder, fire essence, travels with its pace shortened by more than one degree per day.
translations.idiomatic: The Sparkling Deluder, fire essence, travels with its pace shortened by more than one degree per day.

sentences.zh: 故太史令王昱以為漢家衰亡之極。

translations.literal: Therefore Grand Astrologer Wang Yu took it as the utmost of the Han house's decline and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Grand Astrologer Wang Yu took it as the utmost sign of the Han house's decline and extinction.

sentences.zh: 熒惑大而赤色；

translations.literal: When the Sparkling Deluder is large and red in color,
translations.idiomatic: When the Sparkling Deluder is large and red in color,

sentences.zh: 光不明，赤而小，與小星無別，皆漢家衰亡之異也。

translations.literal: its light is not bright; when red and small, indistinguishable from lesser stars — all anomalies of the Han house's decline and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: its light is not bright; when red and small, indistinguishable from lesser stars — all omens of the Han house's decline and extinction.

sentences.zh: :易傳曰：「上下流通聖賢昌，厥應帝德鳳皇翔，萬民喜樂無咎殃。

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Changes says: "Above and below flow freely — sages and worthies flourish; in response to imperial virtue the phoenix soars; the myriad people rejoice without calamity or disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Changes says, "Above and below flow freely — sages and worthies flourish; in response to imperial virtue the phoenix soars; the myriad people rejoice without calamity or disaster.

sentences.zh: 」易傳又曰：「聖人受命，厥應鳳皇下，天子虜。

translations.literal: " The Commentary on the Changes also says: "The sage receives the mandate; in response the phoenix descends; the Son of Heaven is made captive.
translations.idiomatic: " The Commentary on the Changes also says, "The sage receives the mandate; in response the phoenix descends; the Son of Heaven is made captive.

sentences.zh: 」易傳又曰：「黃龍見，天災將至，天子絀，聖人出。

translations.literal: " The Commentary also says: "When the yellow dragon appears, heavenly disaster is about to arrive; the Son of Heaven is disgraced; the sage emerges.
translations.idiomatic: " The Commentary also says, "When the yellow dragon appears, heavenly disaster is about to arrive; the Son of Heaven is disgraced; the sage emerges.

sentences.zh: 」黃龍以戊己日見，五色文章皆具，聖人得天受命。

translations.literal: " When the yellow dragon appears on wu or ji days, all five colors and patterns are complete — the sage receives Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: " When the yellow dragon appears on wu or ji days, all five colors and patterns are complete — the sage receives Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 黃龍以戊寅見，此帝王受命之符瑞最著明者也。

translations.literal: When the yellow dragon appears on wuyin — this is the most conspicuous token of an emperor receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When the yellow dragon appears on wuyin — this is the most conspicuous token of an emperor receiving the mandate.

sentences.zh: 易傳又曰：「聖人清靜行中正，賢人至，民從命，厥應麒麟來。

translations.literal: The Commentary also says: "The sage is pure and still, acting with centered correctness; worthies arrive, the people follow the mandate; in response the qilin comes.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary also says, "The sage is pure and still, acting with centered correctness; worthies arrive, the people follow the mandate; in response the qilin comes.

sentences.zh: 」春秋玉版讖曰：「代赤者魏公子。

translations.literal: " The Spring and Autumn Jade-Board Prophecy says: "He who replaces the Red — the Lord of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " The Spring and Autumn Jade-Board Prophecy says, "He who replaces the Red — the Lord of Wei.

sentences.zh: 」春秋佐助期曰：「漢以許昌失天下。

translations.literal: " The Spring and Autumn Assistant Term Prophecy says: "Han will lose the realm at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: " The Spring and Autumn Assistant Term Prophecy says, "Han will lose the realm at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 」故白馬令甘陵李雲上事，言許昌氣見，當塗高已萌，欲使漢家防絕萌牙。

translations.literal: " Therefore Li Yun, magistrate of Baima in Ganling, submitted a memorial saying that the qi of Xuchang had appeared and dang tu gao had already sprouted — wishing to make the Han house guard against and sever the budding germ.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore Li Yun, magistrate of Baima in Ganling, submitted a memorial saying that the aura of Xuchang had appeared and dang tu gao had already sprouted — wishing to make the Han house guard against and cut off the budding germ.

sentences.zh: 今漢都許，日以微弱，當居許昌以失天下。

translations.literal: Now Han's capital is Xu, daily growing weaker — it should reside at Xuchang to lose the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Now Han's capital is Xu, daily growing weaker — it should move to Xuchang to lose the realm.

sentences.zh: 當塗高者，魏也；

translations.literal: Dang tu gao — this is Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Dang tu gao — this is Wei;

sentences.zh: 魏者，象魏兩闕之名當道而高大者也。

translations.literal: Wei is the name of the two gate-towers of the signal-banners that face the road and stand high.
translations.idiomatic: Wei is the name of the two gate-towers of the signal-banners that face the road and stand high.

sentences.zh: 魏當代漢，如李雲之言也。

translations.literal: Wei should replace Han — as Li Yun's words said.
translations.idiomatic: Wei should replace Han — as Li Yun's words said.

sentences.zh: 春秋佐助期又曰：「漢以蒙孫亡。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Assistant Term Prophecy also says: "Han will perish through meng sun.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Assistant Term Prophecy also says, "Han will perish through meng sun.

sentences.zh: 」說者以蒙孫直漢二十四帝，童蒙愚惑以弱亡。

translations.literal: " Commentators take meng sun to refer directly to Han's twenty-four emperors — childishly obscured and deluded, perishing in weakness.
translations.idiomatic: " Commentators take meng sun to refer directly to Han's twenty-four emperors — childishly blinded and confused, and so perishing in weakness.

sentences.zh: 漢帝少時名為董侯，名不正，蒙亂荒惑，其子孫以弱亡也。

translations.literal: The Han emperor in his youth was named Marquis Dong; his name was not proper; obscured by chaos and wild delusion, his descendants perished in weakness.
translations.idiomatic: The Han emperor in his youth was called Marquis Dong — an improper name. Obscured by chaos and delusion, his line perished in weakness.

sentences.zh: 孝經中黃讖曰：「日載東，紀火光。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety Central Yellow Prophecy says: "The sun carries eastward, records fire's light.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety Central Yellow Prophecy says, "The sun carries eastward, records fire's light.

sentences.zh: 不橫一，聖明聰。

translations.literal: Not crossing with one — sage, bright, and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Not crossing with one — sage, bright, and keen.

sentences.zh: 〈日載東紀火光不橫一聖明聰　殿本考證云：「日載東者，曹也。

translations.literal: 〈On "The sun carries eastward, records fire's light, not crossing with one, sage bright and keen": the Dian edition collation says: "'The sun carries eastward' — this is Cao.
translations.idiomatic: 〈On "The sun carries eastward, records fire's light, not crossing with one, sage bright and keen": the Dian edition collation notes, "'The sun carries eastward' refers to Cao.

sentences.zh: 曹，古文作𣍘。

translations.literal: Cao — in ancient script written with an archaic variant form.
translations.idiomatic: Cao — in ancient script written with an archaic variant form.

sentences.zh: 不橫一者，丕也。

translations.literal: 'Not crossing with one' — this is Pi.
translations.idiomatic: "Not crossing with one" — this is Pi.

sentences.zh: 然則『紀火光』，自應作『絕火光』，言炎漢亡也。」〉

translations.literal: Thus 'records fire's light' should properly read 'extinguishes fire's light' — meaning the Flaming Han perishes."〉
translations.idiomatic: Thus "records fire's light" should read "extinguishes fire's light" — meaning the Flaming Han perishes."〉

sentences.zh: 四百之外，易姓而王。

translations.literal: Beyond four hundred, change surname and become king.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond four hundred years, the surname changes and a new house takes the throne.

sentences.zh: 天下歸功致太平。

translations.literal: All under Heaven yields merit and attains great peace.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven yields merit and attains great peace.

sentences.zh: 」此魏王之姓諱著見圖讖也。

translations.literal: " This is the surname and taboo name of the King of Wei clearly appearing in chart prophecies.
translations.idiomatic: " This is the surname and taboo name of the King of Wei plainly revealed in chart prophecies.

sentences.zh: 易運期曰：「言居東，西有午，兩日並光日居下。

translations.literal: The Change of Fortune Period says: "Speaking of dwelling in the east, west having wu, two suns share light, the sun dwells below.
translations.idiomatic: The Change of Fortune Period says, "Speaking of dwelling in the east, west having wu, two suns share light, the sun dwells below.

sentences.zh: 其為主，反為輔，

translations.literal: What should be lord instead becomes assistant,
translations.idiomatic: What should be lord instead becomes assistant,

sentences.zh: 〈反為輔　「反」各本並作「及」，據三國志魏志文帝紀裴注改。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "instead becomes assistant": in all editions "instead" is written as "and"; emended according to Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Wei Annals, Emperor Wen Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "instead becomes assistant": all editions read "and" for "instead"; corrected per Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Wei Annals, Emperor Wen Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms.〉

sentences.zh: 五八四十，黃氣受，真人出。

translations.literal: Five eight forty, yellow qi received, the true man emerges.
translations.idiomatic: Five eight forty — yellow qi is received, and the true man emerges.

sentences.zh: 」言午「許」字，兩日「昌」字，漢當以許亡，魏當以許昌。

translations.literal: " The word wu is the character Xu; two suns is the character Chang — Han should perish through Xu, Wei should reign through Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: " The word wu is the character Xu; two suns is the character Chang — Han should perish through Xu, and Wei should reign through Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 今際會之期在許，是其大效也。

translations.literal: Now the time of convergence is at Xu — this is its great fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Now the appointed time of convergence is at Xu — this is its great fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 易運期又曰：「鬼在山，禾女運，王天下。」

translations.literal: The Change of Fortune Period also says: "Ghost on mountain, grain-woman fortune, rule all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Change of Fortune Period also says, "Ghost on mountain, grain-woman fortune, rule all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 於是魏王受漢禪，柴於繁陽，有黃鳥銜丹書，集于尚書臺，於是改元為黃初。

translations.literal: Thereupon the King of Wei received Han's abdication, performed the feng sacrifice at Fanyang; a yellow bird carrying a red writ settled on the Secretariat Terrace — and the era name was changed to Huangchu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the King of Wei received Han's abdication and performed the feng sacrifice at Fanyang. A yellow bird carrying a red writ settled on the Secretariat Terrace, and the era name was changed to Huangchu.

sentences.zh: 漢中平二年，洛陽民譌言虎賁寺有黃人，觀者日數萬，道路斷絕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongping of Han, Luoyang commoners had rhymes saying there were yellow men at Huben Temple; viewers numbered tens of thousands daily, and roads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongping, Luoyang commoners spread rhymes saying there were yellow men at Huben Temple. Viewers numbered tens of thousands each day, and the roads were impassable.

sentences.zh: 中平元年，黃巾賊起，云：「蒼天已死，黃天當立。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongping, Yellow Turban rebels rose, saying: "The azure Heaven is already dead; Yellow Heaven shall arise.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongping, Yellow Turban rebels rose, declaring, "The azure Heaven is already dead; Yellow Heaven shall arise.

sentences.zh: 」此魏氏依劉向自云土德之符也。

translations.literal: " This is the Wei clan relying on Liu Xiang's own declaration of the token of Earth virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " This is the Wei clan citing Liu Xiang's own claim of the token of Earth virtue.

sentences.zh: 先是周敬王之四十七年，宋景公問大夫邢史子臣：「天道何祥？

translations.literal: Previously, in the forty-seventh year of King Jing of Zhou, Duke Jing of Song asked the grandee Zichen of the Xing lineage: "What auspicious sign is there in Heaven's way?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the forty-seventh year of King Jing of Zhou, Duke Jing of Song asked the grandee Zichen of the Xing lineage, "What auspicious sign does Heaven's way hold?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「後五年五月丁亥，臣將死。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Five years hence, on dinghai of the fifth month, I will die.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Five years from now, on dinghai of the fifth month, I will die.

sentences.zh: 死後五年五月丁卯，吳將亡。

translations.literal: Five years after my death, on dingmao of the fifth month, Wu will perish.
translations.idiomatic: Five years after my death, on dingmao of the fifth month, Wu will perish.

sentences.zh: 亡後五年，君將終。

translations.literal: Five years after Wu's fall, Your Lordship will end.
translations.idiomatic: Five years after Wu falls, Your Lordship will reach your end.

sentences.zh: 終後四百年，邾王天下。

translations.literal: Four hundred years after your end, Zhu will rule all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred years after your end, Zhu will rule all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」皆如其言。

translations.literal: " All came to pass as he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: " All came to pass exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 邾王天下，蓋謂魏國之後。

translations.literal: Zhu ruling all under Heaven — presumably this refers to Wei's later [dynasty].
translations.idiomatic: "Zhu ruling all under Heaven" presumably refers to the later Wei state.

sentences.zh: 言四百年則錯。

translations.literal: To say four hundred years is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The figure of four hundred years is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 疑年代久遠，傳記者謬誤。

translations.literal: Presumably because the dates are remote, those who recorded it made errors.
translations.idiomatic: Presumably the dates were so remote that those who recorded the story made mistakes.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公初生，有光氣照燿室屋，其後即大位。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Gaogui Township was first born, light and qi illuminated the chamber and house; afterward he attained the supreme position.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Gaogui Township was born, light and radiance filled the chamber; afterward he ascended to the throne.

sentences.zh: 劉備身長七尺七寸，垂手過膝，顧自見耳。

translations.literal: Liu Bei was seven chi seven cun in height; his hands hung past his knees; when he turned his head he could see his own ears.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei stood seven chi seven cun tall, his hands hanging past his knees; when he turned his head he could see his own ears.

sentences.zh: 洛書甄燿度曰：「赤三日，德昌九世會備，合為帝際。」

translations.literal: The Luo Shu Appraisal Glorious Measure says: "Red three days, virtue flourishing nine generations converge Bei, meeting as the emperor's juncture."
translations.idiomatic: The Luo Shu Appraisal Glorious Measure says, "Red three days, virtue flourishing — nine generations converge on Bei, meeting at the emperor's juncture."

sentences.zh: 〈赤三日德昌九世會備合為帝際　各本並脫「日」字，「為」字，據三國志蜀志先主傳補。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "Red three days, virtue flourishing nine generations converge Bei meeting as emperor's juncture": all editions omit the characters "day" and "as"; supplemented according to the Shu Annals, Former Lord Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "Red three days, virtue flourishing nine generations converge Bei meeting as emperor's juncture": all editions omit "day" and "as"; restored per the Shu Annals, Former Lord Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms.〉

sentences.zh: 洛書寶予命曰：「天度帝道備稱皇，以統握契，百成不敗。

translations.literal: The Luo Shu Bestowing Mandate says: "Heaven's measure — the imperial way of Bei entitled emperor, grasping the covenant in rule, a hundred accomplishments without defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Luo Shu Bestowing Mandate says, "Heaven's measure — the imperial way of Bei entitled emperor, grasping the covenant in rule, a hundred accomplishments without defeat.

sentences.zh: 」洛書錄運期曰：「九侯七傑爭民命，炊骸道路，誰使主者玄且來。」

translations.literal: " The Luo Shu Recording Fortune Period says: "Nine marquis and seven heroes contend for the people's lives; corpses boil on the roads — who shall make the lord? Xuan and come."
translations.idiomatic: " The Luo Shu Recording Fortune Period says, "Nine marquis and seven heroes contend for the people's lives; corpses boil on the roads — who shall make the lord? Xuan and come."

sentences.zh: 〈九侯七傑爭民命炊骸道路誰使主者玄且來　三國志蜀志先主傳載洛書錄運期原文作「九侯七傑爭命，民炊骸，道路籍籍履人頭，誰使主者玄且來」。

translations.literal: 〈On "Nine marquis seven heroes contend for people's lives, corpses boil on roads, who shall make the lord Xuan and come": the Shu Annals, Former Lord Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms gives the original Luo Shu Recording Fortune Period text as "Nine marquis seven heroes contend for lives, people boil corpses, roads thronged treading on human heads, who shall make the lord Xuan and come."
translations.idiomatic: 〈On "Nine marquis seven heroes contend for people's lives, corpses boil on roads, who shall make the lord Xuan and come": the Shu Annals, Former Lord Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms gives the original Luo Shu Recording Fortune Period text as "Nine marquis seven heroes contend for lives, people boil corpses, roads thronged treading on human heads, who shall make the lord? Xuan and come."

sentences.zh: 與宋書文字稍有異同。〉

translations.literal: The wording differs slightly from the Song Shu text.〉
translations.idiomatic: The wording differs slightly from the Song Shu text.〉

sentences.zh: 備字玄德，故云「玄且來」也。

translations.literal: Bei's style name is Xuande — hence "Xuan and come."
translations.idiomatic: Bei's style name is Xuande — hence the phrase "Xuan and come."

sentences.zh: 孝經鉤命決曰：「帝三建，九會備。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety Hook Mandate Verdict says: "Emperor thrice established, nine converge on Bei.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety Hook Mandate Verdict says, "Emperor thrice established, nine converge on Bei.

sentences.zh: 」先是，術士周羣言，西南數有黃氣，直立數丈，如此積年，每有景雲祥風，從璿璣下來應之。

translations.literal: " Previously, the technician Zhou Qun said that in the southwest yellow qi repeatedly appeared, standing upright several zhang — thus for accumulated years; whenever there were auspicious clouds and winds, they came down from the Jade Pivot in response.
translations.idiomatic: " Previously, the technician Zhou Qun reported that in the southwest yellow qi repeatedly rose upright several zhang high, year after year; whenever auspicious clouds and winds appeared, they descended from the Jade Pivot in response.

sentences.zh: 〈每有景雲祥風從璿璣下來應之　各本並脫「來」字，據三國志蜀志先主傳補。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "whenever there are auspicious clouds and winds coming down from the Jade Pivot in response": all editions omit the character "come"; supplemented according to the Shu Annals, Former Lord Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "whenever there are auspicious clouds and winds coming down from the Jade Pivot in response": all editions omit "come"; restored per the Shu Annals, Former Lord Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms.〉

sentences.zh: 建安二十二年中，屢有氣如旗，從西竟東，中天而行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jian'an, repeatedly there was qi like banners from west to east, crossing the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Jian'an, banner-like qi repeatedly appeared, running from west to east across the sky.

sentences.zh: 圖書曰：「必有天子出其方。

translations.literal: Charts and texts say: "Surely there will be a Son of Heaven arising from that direction.
translations.idiomatic: Charts and texts say, "Surely a Son of Heaven will arise from that direction.

sentences.zh: 」太白、熒惑、鎮星從歲星，又黃龍見犍為武陽之赤水，九日乃去。

translations.literal: " Venus, Mars, and Saturn followed Jupiter; also a yellow dragon appeared at Red Water in Wuyang of Jianwei, and after nine days departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Venus, Mars, and Saturn followed Jupiter; a yellow dragon also appeared at Red Water in Wuyang of Jianwei and departed after nine days.

sentences.zh: 關羽在襄陽，男子張嘉、王休獻玉璽，備後稱帝於蜀。

translations.literal: Guan Yu was at Xiangyang; the men Zhang Jia and Wang Xiu presented a jade seal; Bei afterward declared himself emperor in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: While Guan Yu was at Xiangyang, the men Zhang Jia and Wang Xiu presented a jade seal; Bei afterward declared himself emperor in Shu.

sentences.zh: 孫堅之祖名鍾，家在吳郡富春，獨與母居。

translations.literal: Sun Jian's grandfather was named Zhong; his family was in Fuchun of Wu Commandery; he lived alone with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian's grandfather was named Zhong. His family lived in Fuchun of Wu Commandery, and he resided alone with his mother.

sentences.zh: 性至孝。

translations.literal: In nature he was supremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: He was supremely filial by nature.

sentences.zh: 遭歲荒，以種瓜為業。

translations.literal: Encountering famine years, he made melon-growing his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: During years of famine, he made his living growing melons.

sentences.zh: 忽有三少年詣鍾乞瓜，鍾厚待之。

translations.literal: Suddenly three young men came to Zhong begging melons; Zhong treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly three young men came to Zhong to beg melons, and he treated them generously.

sentences.zh: 三人謂鍾曰：「此山下善，可作冢，葬之，當出天子。

translations.literal: The three told Zhong: "Below this mountain is good ground; you may make a tomb and be buried there — from it will come a Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The three told Zhong, "Below this mountain is good ground. Make a tomb there and bury him in it — from that place will come a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 君可下山百步許，顧見我去，即可葬也。

translations.literal: My lord may go down the mountain about a hundred paces; when you look back and see us go, then you may bury him there.
translations.idiomatic: Go down the mountain about a hundred paces. When you look back and see us depart, you may bury him there.

sentences.zh: 」鍾去三十步，便反顧，見三人並乘白鶴飛去。

translations.literal: " Zhong had gone thirty paces when he turned back and saw the three together riding white cranes and flying away.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong had gone only thirty paces when he turned back and saw the three riding white cranes and flying away together.

sentences.zh: 鍾死，即葬其地。

translations.literal: When Zhong died, he was buried on that spot.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong died, he was buried on that spot.

sentences.zh: 地在縣城東，冢上數有光怪，雲氣五色上屬天，衍數里。

translations.literal: The place was east of the county seat; on the tomb repeatedly there were strange lights; cloud-qi of five colors rose to connect with Heaven, extending several li.
translations.idiomatic: The grave lay east of the county seat. Strange lights repeatedly appeared above the mound; five-colored cloud-qi rose to connect with Heaven and stretched for several li.

sentences.zh: 父老相謂此非凡氣，孫氏其興矣。

translations.literal: The elders said to one another this was no ordinary qi — the Sun clan would surely rise.
translations.idiomatic: The elders said to one another that this was no ordinary sign — the Sun clan would surely rise.

sentences.zh: 堅母任堅，夢腸出繞吳昌門。

translations.literal: Jian's mother, when carrying Jian, dreamed her intestines came out and wrapped around Wu's Chang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: While carrying Jian, his mother dreamed her intestines came out and wrapped around Wu's Chang Gate.

sentences.zh: 以告鄰母，鄰母曰：「安知非吉祥也。

translations.literal: She told a neighbor mother, who said: "How do you know it is not auspicious?
translations.idiomatic: She told a neighbor, who said, "How do you know it is not auspicious?

sentences.zh: 」昌門，吳郭門也。

translations.literal: " Chang Gate was Wu's outer city gate.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang Gate was Wu's outer city gate.

sentences.zh: 堅生而容貌奇異。

translations.literal: When Jian was born, his features were strange and extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian was born, his features were strange and extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 堅妻吳氏初任子策，夢月入其懷；

translations.literal: Jian's wife Lady Wu, when first carrying Sun Ce, dreamed the moon entered her belly;
translations.idiomatic: When Jian's wife Lady Wu first carried Sun Ce, she dreamed the moon entered her belly;

sentences.zh: 後孕子權，又夢日入懷。

translations.literal: later when pregnant with Sun Quan, she again dreamed the sun entered her belly.
translations.idiomatic: later, when pregnant with Sun Quan, she dreamed the sun entered her belly.

sentences.zh: 告堅曰：「昔任策，夢月入懷，今又夢日入懷，何也？

translations.literal: She told Jian: "Before, carrying Ce, I dreamed the moon entered my belly; now again I dream the sun enters my belly — what does it mean?
translations.idiomatic: She told Jian, "When I carried Ce, I dreamed the moon entered my belly; now I dream the sun enters my belly again — what does it mean?

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「日月陰陽之精，極貴之象，吾子孫其興乎。

translations.literal: " Jian said: "Sun and moon are the essences of yin and yang — tokens of supreme nobility; will my descendants rise?
translations.idiomatic: " Jian said, "Sun and moon are the essences of yin and yang — tokens of supreme nobility. Will my descendants rise?

sentences.zh: 」權方頤大口紫髥，長上短下。

translations.literal: " Quan had a square jaw, large mouth, and purple beard; long above and short below.
translations.idiomatic: " Quan had a square jaw, a large mouth, and a purple beard; his torso was long and his legs short.

sentences.zh: 漢世有劉琬者，能相人，見權兄弟，曰：「孫氏兄弟，雖各才智明達，然祿胙不終。

translations.literal: In Han times there was Liu Wan who could read faces; seeing Quan's brothers, he said: "The Sun brothers, though each intelligent and clear, will not enjoy blessings to the end.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times there was Liu Wan, a face-reader. Seeing Quan's brothers, he said, "The Sun brothers are each intelligent and clear, yet none will enjoy blessings to the end.

sentences.zh: 唯中弟孝廉，形貌奇偉，骨體不恒，有大貴之表，年又最壽。

translations.literal: Only the middle brother, the Filial and Incorrupt graduate, has a form strange and grand, bones and frame not ordinary, marks of great nobility, and he will live longest of all.
translations.idiomatic: Only the middle brother, the Filial and Incorrupt graduate, has a form strange and grand, bones and frame unlike others, marks of great nobility, and he will outlive them all.

sentences.zh: 爾其識之。

translations.literal: You must take note of this.
translations.idiomatic: Mark this well.

sentences.zh: 」權時為孝廉。

translations.literal: " Quan was then a Filial and Incorrupt graduate.
translations.idiomatic: " Quan was then a Filial and Incorrupt graduate.

sentences.zh: 初，秦始皇東巡，濟江。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Qin Shihuang toured east and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, Qin Shihuang toured east and crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 望氣者云：「五百年後，江東有天子氣出於吳，而金陵之地，有王者之勢。

translations.literal: Qi-readers said: "Five hundred years hence, in Jiangdong there will be Son-of-Heaven qi arising from Wu; the land of Jinling has the momentum of kingship.
translations.idiomatic: Qi-readers said, "Five hundred years hence, Son-of-Heaven qi will arise from Wu in Jiangdong, and the land of Jinling will have the momentum of kingship.

sentences.zh: 」於是秦始皇乃改金陵曰秣陵，鑿北山以絕其勢。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Qin Shihuang changed Jinling's name to Moling and tunneled through North Mountain to sever its momentum.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Qin Shihuang renamed Jinling as Moling and tunneled through North Mountain to break its momentum.

sentences.zh: 至吳，又令囚徒十餘萬人掘汙其地，表以惡名，故曰囚卷縣，今嘉興縣也。

translations.literal: Reaching Wu, he also ordered more than a hundred thousand convicts to dig and sully the land, marking it with an ill name — hence the district was called Qiujuan, now Jiaxing district.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Wu, he also ordered more than a hundred thousand convicts to dig and defile the land, marking it with an ill name — hence the district was called Qiujuan, now Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 漢世術士言：「黃旗紫蓋，見於斗、牛之間，江東有天子氣。

translations.literal: Han-era technicians said: "Yellow banner and purple canopy appear between Dipper and Ox — in Jiangdong there is Son-of-Heaven qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han-era technicians said, "Yellow banner and purple canopy appear between Dipper and Ox — in Jiangdong there is Son-of-Heaven qi.

sentences.zh: 」獻帝興平中，吳中謠言：「黃金車，斑闌耳。

translations.literal: " In Emperor Xian's Xingping era, a rhyme in Wu said: "Golden carriage, spotted bridle ears.
translations.idiomatic: " During Emperor Xian's Xingping era, a rhyme in Wu ran, "Golden carriage, spotted bridle ears.

sentences.zh: 開昌門，出天子。

translations.literal: Open Chang Gate — a Son of Heaven emerges.
translations.idiomatic: Open Chang Gate — a Son of Heaven emerges.

sentences.zh: 」魏文帝黃初三年，夏口、武昌並言黃龍、鳳皇見。

translations.literal: " In the third year of Huangchu under Wei Emperor Wen, Xiakou and Wuchang both reported yellow dragon and phoenix sightings.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third year of Huangchu under Wei Emperor Wen, Xiakou and Wuchang both reported sightings of a yellow dragon and a phoenix.

sentences.zh: 〈夏口武昌並言黃龍鳳皇見　「夏口」三朝本作「舉口」，北監本、毛本、殿本作「舉兵」。

translations.literal: 〈On "Xiakou and Wuchang both report yellow dragon and phoenix sightings": "Xiakou" in the Three Dynasties edition reads "Jukou"; the Northern Supervisory, Mao, and Dian editions read "Jubing."
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "Xiakou and Wuchang both report yellow dragon and phoenix sightings": the Three Dynasties edition reads "Jukou" for "Xiakou"; the Northern Supervisory, Mao, and Dian editions read "Jubing."

sentences.zh: 今據三國志吳志吳主權傳改正。〉

translations.literal: Now corrected according to the Wu Annals, Lord Sun Quan Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms.〉
translations.idiomatic: Corrected according to the Wu Annals, Lord Sun Quan Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms.〉

sentences.zh: 其年，權稱尊號。

translations.literal: That year, Quan assumed an honored title.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Quan assumed an imperial title.

sentences.zh: 年至七十一而薨。

translations.literal: He reached seventy-one years and passed away.
translations.idiomatic: He lived to seventy-one and then died.

sentences.zh: 權子休初封琅邪王，夢乘龍上天，顧不見尾。

translations.literal: Sun Quan's son Xiu, first enfeoffed as King of Langye, dreamed riding a dragon up to Heaven but could not see its tail when he looked back.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's son Xiu, first enfeoffed as King of Langye, dreamed of riding a dragon up to Heaven but could not see its tail when he looked back.

sentences.zh: 後得大位，其子被廢。

translations.literal: Later he attained the great position, but his son was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he attained the throne, but his son was deposed.

sentences.zh: 漢元、成之世，先識之士有言曰：「魏年有和，當有開石於西三千餘里，繫五馬，文曰討曹。

translations.literal: In the eras of Han Yuans and Cheng, prescient men had a saying: "In Wei's age there will be harmony; a split stone will appear in the west more than three thousand li away, bearing five horses, with text reading 'Strike Cao.'
translations.idiomatic: In the eras of Emperors Yuan and Cheng of Han, prescient men had a saying: "In Wei's age there will be harmony; a split stone will appear more than three thousand li to the west, bearing five horses, with text reading 'Strike Cao.'

sentences.zh: 」及魏之初興也，張掖刪丹縣金山柳谷有石生焉，周圍七尋，

translations.literal: " When Wei first rose, at Willow Valley of Golden Mountain in Shandan County of Zhangye, stone was born — circumference seven xun,
translations.idiomatic: " When Wei first rose, stone appeared at Willow Valley of Golden Mountain in Shandan County of Zhangye — seven xun in circumference,

sentences.zh: 〈周圍七尋　各本並脫「七」字，據三國志魏志明帝紀裴注引搜神記補。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "circumference seven xun": all editions omit the character "seven"; supplemented according to Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Wei Annals, Emperor Ming Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms, citing In Search of the Supernatural.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "circumference seven xun": all editions omit "seven"; restored per Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Wei Annals, Emperor Ming Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms, citing In Search of the Supernatural.〉

sentences.zh: 中高一仞，蒼質素章，有五馬、麟、鹿、鳳皇、仙人之象。

translations.literal: middle height one ren, blue-gray substance with plain markings, images of five horses, qilin, deer, phoenix, and immortals.
translations.idiomatic: one ren high at the center, of blue-gray substance with plain markings, bearing images of five horses, qilin, deer, phoenix, and immortals.

sentences.zh: 始見於建安，形成於黃初，文備於太和。

translations.literal: First seen in Jian'an, formed in Huangchu, text complete in Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: It first appeared in Jian'an, took form in Huangchu, and its inscription was complete by Taihe.

sentences.zh: 至青龍三年，柳谷之玄川溢涌，石形改易，狀似雲龜，廣一丈六尺，長一丈七尺一寸，

translations.literal: By the third year of Qinglong, the dark river of Willow Valley overflowed; the stone's form changed, resembling a cloud-tortoise — width one zhang six chi, length one zhang seven chi one cun,
translations.idiomatic: By the third year of Qinglong, the dark river of Willow Valley overflowed. The stone's form changed to resemble a cloud-tortoise — one zhang six chi wide and one zhang seven chi one cun long,

sentences.zh: 〈廣一丈六尺長一丈七尺一寸　各本脫「一丈六尺長」五字，據三國志魏志明帝紀裴注引魏氏春秋補。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "width one zhang six chi, length one zhang seven chi one cun": all editions omit the five characters "one zhang six chi length"; supplemented according to Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Wei Annals, Emperor Ming Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms, citing the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "width one zhang six chi, length one zhang seven chi one cun": all editions omit "one zhang six chi length"; restored per Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Wei Annals, Emperor Ming Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms, citing the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn.〉

sentences.zh: 圍五丈八寸，立于川西。

translations.literal: circumference five zhang eight cun, standing west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: five zhang eight cun in circumference, standing west of the river.

sentences.zh: 有石馬十二，其一仙人騎之，其一覊靽，

translations.literal: There were twelve stone horses; one an immortal riding it; one with bridle and saddle flap,
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve stone horses — one with an immortal riding it, one with bridle and saddle flap,

sentences.zh: 〈其一覊靽　「覊」各本並作「騎」，據三國志魏志明帝紀裴注引魏氏春秋改。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "one with bridle and saddle flap": in all editions "bridle" is written as "ride"; emended according to Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Wei Annals, Emperor Ming Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms, citing the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "one with bridle and saddle flap": all editions read "ride" for "bridle"; corrected per Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Wei Annals, Emperor Ming Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms, citing the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn.〉

sentences.zh: 其五有形而不善成，其五成形。

translations.literal: five had form but did not finish well; five took complete form.
translations.idiomatic: five had form but did not finish well; five were fully formed.

sentences.zh: 又有一牛八卦列宿彗星之象。

translations.literal: Also images of an ox, the Eight Trigrams, the lunar lodges, and a comet.
translations.idiomatic: There were also images of an ox, the Eight Trigrams, the lunar lodges, and a comet.

sentences.zh: 有玉匣開蓋於前，有玉玦二，玉璜一。

translations.literal: There was a jade casket with its lid open in front, two jade rings, and one jade pendant.
translations.idiomatic: A jade casket lay open in front, with two jade rings and one jade pendant.

sentences.zh: 又有麒麟、鳳皇、白虎、馬、牛於中布列。

translations.literal: Also qilin, phoenix, white tiger, horse, and ox arrayed within.
translations.idiomatic: Within were also arrayed qilin, phoenix, white tiger, horse, and ox.

sentences.zh: 有文字曰：「上上三天王述大會討大曹金但取之金立中大金馬一疋中正大吉關壽此馬甲寅述水」凡三十五字。

translations.literal: There was text reading: "Supreme above, three heavens, the king narrates the great assembly, strike great Cao, gold but take it, gold stands in the center, great gold horse one mount, centered correctness great fortune, Guan Shou, this horse jiayin, narrates water" — thirty-five characters in all.
translations.idiomatic: There was an inscription reading: "Supreme above, three heavens, the king narrates the great assembly, strike great Cao, gold but take it, gold stands in the center, great gold horse one mount, centered correctness great fortune, Guan Shou, this horse jiayin, narrates water" — thirty-five characters in all.

sentences.zh: 〈上上三天王述大會討大曹金但取之金立中大金馬一疋中正大吉關壽此馬甲寅述水凡三十五字　按此白石文三十五字，亦見三國志魏志明帝紀裴注引魏氏春秋。

translations.literal: 〈On "Supreme above three heavens the king narrates great assembly strike great Cao gold but take it gold stands in center great gold horse one mount centered correctness great fortune Guan Shou this horse jiayin narrates water thirty-five characters in all": note — these thirty-five characters on the white stone also appear in Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Wei Annals, Emperor Ming Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms, citing the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on the thirty-five-character white-stone inscription "Supreme above three heavens the king narrates great assembly strike great Cao gold but take it gold stands in center great gold horse one mount centered correctness great fortune Guan Shou this horse jiayin narrates water": these thirty-five characters also appear in Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Wei Annals, Emperor Ming Basic Annals, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms, citing the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 「會」魏氏春秋作「金」。

translations.literal: On "assembly": the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn reads "gold".
translations.idiomatic: On "assembly": the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn reads "gold".

sentences.zh: 「討大曹」魏氏春秋作「大討曹」。

translations.literal: On "strike great Cao": the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn reads "great strike Cao".
translations.idiomatic: On "strike great Cao": the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn reads "great strike Cao".

sentences.zh: 「中正」魏氏春秋作「在中」。

translations.literal: On "centered correctness": the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn reads "standing in center".
translations.idiomatic: On "centered correctness": the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn reads "standing in center".

sentences.zh: 「關」魏氏春秋作「開」。〉

translations.literal: On "Guan": the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn reads "Kai".〉
translations.idiomatic: On "Guan": the Wei Clan Spring and Autumn reads "Kai".〉

sentences.zh: 石色蒼，而物形及字，並白石書之，皆隆起。

translations.literal: The stone's color was dark green; both the object forms and characters were all written in white stone and all raised in relief.
translations.idiomatic: The stone was dark green. Both the object shapes and the characters were inscribed in white stone, all raised in relief.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝惡其文有「討曹」，鑿去為「計」，以蒼石塞之，宿昔而白石滿焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei hated that the text had "strike Cao"; he chiseled it away and changed it to "plan"; he plugged it with dark green stone, and overnight white stone filled it again.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei hated that the inscription contained "strike Cao." He had it chiseled away and altered to read "plan," then plugged the gap with dark green stone — but overnight the white stone had filled it again.

sentences.zh: 當時稱為祥瑞，班下天下。

translations.literal: At the time it was hailed as an auspicious omen and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was hailed as an auspicious omen and promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 處士張臶曰：「夫神兆未然，不追往事，此蓋將來之休徵，當今之怪異也。

translations.literal: Recluse Zhang Zan said: "Divine portents foretell what has not yet happened; they do not revisit past events — this is presumably a token of future blessing, a present marvel."
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Zhang Zan said, "Divine portents foretell what has not yet occurred; they do not revisit the past. This is surely a token of blessings to come — a marvel of the present age."

sentences.zh: 」既而晉以司馬氏受禪。

translations.literal: " Thereafter Jin received the abdication through the Sima clan.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter Jin received the mandate through the abdication of the Sima clan.

sentences.zh: 太尉屬程猗說曰：「夫大者，盛之極也。

translations.literal: Attendant to the Grand Commandant Cheng Yi explained: "What is great is the utmost of fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi, an attendant to the Grand Commandant, explained, "What is great is the utmost of fullness.

sentences.zh: 金者，晉之行也。

translations.literal: Gold is Jin's element of the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: Gold is the element governing Jin.

sentences.zh: 中者，物之會也。

translations.literal: Center is where things converge.
translations.idiomatic: Center is where things converge.

sentences.zh: 吉者，福之始也。

translations.literal: Good fortune is the beginning of blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Good fortune is the beginning of blessing.

sentences.zh: 此言司馬氏之王天下，感德而生，應正吉而王之符也。

translations.literal: This speaks of the Sima clan's kingship over all under Heaven — born in response to virtue, a token corresponding to upright fortune and kingship.
translations.idiomatic: This prophesies the Sima clan's rule over all under Heaven — arising in response to virtue, a token of rightful fortune and royal ascent.

sentences.zh: 」猗又為贊曰：「皇德遐通，實降嘉靈。

translations.literal: " Yi also composed a eulogy: "Imperial virtue reaches far; truly descends beneficent spirit.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi also composed a eulogy: "Imperial virtue reaches far and wide; truly descends a beneficent spirit.

sentences.zh: 乾生其象，坤育其形。

translations.literal: Heaven generates its image; Earth nurtures its form.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven generates its image; Earth nurtures its form.

sentences.zh: 玄石既表，素文以成。

translations.literal: The dark stone having declared itself, plain writing is thereby completed.
translations.idiomatic: The dark stone having revealed itself, the plain inscription is complete.

sentences.zh: 瑞虎合仁，白麟燿精。

translations.literal: An auspicious tiger embodies benevolence; a white qilin radiates essence.
translations.idiomatic: An auspicious tiger embodies benevolence; a white qilin radiates spiritual brilliance.

sentences.zh: 神馬自圖，金言其形。

translations.literal: The divine horse depicts itself; gold declares its form.
translations.idiomatic: The divine horse depicts itself; gold declares its form.

sentences.zh: 體正而王，中允克明。

translations.literal: Upright in body and thus king; centered and faithful, able to be clear.
translations.idiomatic: Upright in body and fit to rule; centered and faithful, shining with clarity.

sentences.zh: 關壽無疆，於萬斯齡。」

translations.literal: Guan's longevity without bound, unto ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: May Guan's years know no bound, unto ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 晉

translations.literal: Jin
translations.idiomatic: Jin

sentences.zh: 宣帝有狼顧之相，能使面正向後，而身形不異。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had the aspect of a wolf looking back — he could turn his face directly backward while his body remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor had the aspect of a wolf glancing backward — he could turn his face fully behind him while his body remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝嘗夢有三匹馬在一槽中共食，其後宣帝及景、文相係為宰相，遂傾曹氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei once dreamed of three horses feeding together from one trough; afterward the Founding Emperor and Emperors Jing and Wen succeeded one another as chief ministers, and thus toppled the Cao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei once dreamed of three horses feeding together from a single trough. Thereafter the Founding Emperor and Emperors Jing and Wen served as chief ministers in succession, and thus overturned the house of Cao.

sentences.zh: 文帝未立世子，有意於齊獻王攸。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen had not yet established an heir apparent and favored Prince Xian of Qi, You.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had not yet named an heir apparent and favored Prince Xian of Qi, You.

sentences.zh: 武帝時為中撫軍，懼不立，以相貌示裴秀，秀言於文帝曰：「中撫軍振髮籍地，垂手過膝，天表如此，非人臣之相也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was Central Pacifying General, fearing he would not be established, he showed his features to Pei Xiu. Xiu said to Emperor Wen: "The Central Pacifying General's hair stands upright and reaches the ground; his hands hang past his knees — a heaven-granted countenance such as this is not the aspect of a subject-minister.
translations.idiomatic: When he was still Central Pacifying General, fearing he would not be named successor, Emperor Wu showed his features to Pei Xiu. Xiu told Emperor Wen, "The Central Pacifying General's hair stands erect and brushes the ground; his hands reach past his knees. A heaven-granted countenance such as this is not that of a subject."

sentences.zh: 」由是得立。

translations.literal: " Thus he was established as heir.
translations.idiomatic: " By this means he was established as heir.

sentences.zh: 及嗣晉位，其月，襄武縣言有大人相，長三丈餘，足跡三尺一寸，白髮，黃單衣，黃巾，柱杖呼民王始語云：「今當太平。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the Jin throne, that same month Xiangwu County reported a great manlike figure over three zhang tall, footprints three chi one cun, white-haired, in a yellow unlined garment and yellow headcloth, leaning on a staff; he called to the people, naming himself Wang Shi, and said: "Now peace shall come.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the Jin throne, that same month Xiangwu County reported a figure over three zhang tall, with footprints three chi one cun long — white-haired, clad in a yellow unlined robe and yellow headcloth, leaning on a staff. He hailed the people, calling himself Wang Shi, and declared, "Peace is at hand."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，受魏禪。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward, he received Wei's abdication.
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly afterward, he received the abdication of Wei.

sentences.zh: 武帝咸寧元年，大風吹帝社樹折，有青氣出社中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianning under Emperor Wu, a great wind blew and broke the imperial altar tree; green vapor issued from within the altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianning under Emperor Wu, a fierce wind snapped the imperial altar tree, and green vapor rose from within the altar.

sentences.zh: 占者以為東莞有天子氣。

translations.literal: Diviners held that Dongguan had the qi of a Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners held that Dongguan bore the aura of a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 時琅邪武王伷封東莞，伷，元帝祖也。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Wu of Langya, Zhou, was enfeoffed in Dongguan — Zhou was Emperor Yuan's grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Wu of Langya, Zhou, held Dongguan — Zhou was the grandfather of Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 元帝以咸寧二年夜生，有光照室，室內盡明，有白毛生於日角之左，眼有精光燿。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was born at night in the second year of Xianning; light illuminated the chamber until the room was entirely bright; white hair grew to the left of the sun-corner of his forehead; his eyes shone with sparkling light.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was born at night in the second year of Xianning. Light filled the chamber until the room blazed bright. White hair sprouted to the left of the sun-corner of his forehead, and his eyes shone with a brilliant gleam.

sentences.zh: 隨惠帝幸鄴。

translations.literal: He accompanied Emperor Hui to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Emperor Hui to Ye.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎殺東安王繇，繇，元帝叔父也，帝懼，欲出奔，而月明，邀候急，四衢斷絕，不得去。

translations.literal: Prince Chengdu Ying killed Prince Dong'an Yao — Yao was Emperor Yuan's uncle. The Emperor feared and wished to flee, but the moon was bright, pursuit guards pressed close, and the crossroads were blocked — he could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chengdu Ying killed Prince Dong'an Yao — Yao was Emperor Yuan's uncle — the Emperor was terrified and wished to flee. But the moon was bright, pursuit guards pressed close, and every crossroads was blocked; he could not escape.

sentences.zh: 有頃，天陰，風雨大至，候者皆休，乃得去。

translations.literal: Before long the sky darkened; wind and rain came greatly; the watchers all stopped — only then could he depart.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the sky darkened and a great storm broke. The watchers all withdrew, and at last he was able to flee.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝伐吳，琅邪武王伷率眾出涂中，

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wu attacked Wu, Prince Wu of Langya Zhou led troops out from Tuzhong,
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Wu attacked Wu, Prince Wu of Langya Zhou led his forces out from Tuzhong,

sentences.zh: 〈琅邪武王伷率眾出涂中　「涂中」各本並作「塗中」，據晉書琅邪武王伷傳改。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "Prince Wu of Langya Zhou led troops out from Tuzhong": in all editions "Tuzhong" is written with the earth radical for "mud"; emended according to the biography of Prince Wu of Langya Zhou in the History of Jin.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emendation on "Prince Wu of Langya Zhou led troops out from Tuzhong": all editions write the place name with the earth radical for "mud"; corrected per the biography of Prince Wu of Langya Zhou in the History of Jin.〉

sentences.zh: 而王渾逼歷陽，王濬已次近路。

translations.literal: while Wang Hun pressed on Liyang and Wang Jun had already encamped on the near route.
translations.idiomatic: while Wang Hun pressed toward Liyang and Wang Jun had already encamped on the nearer route.

sentences.zh: 孫晧欲降，送天子璽綬，近越二將，而遠送詣伷，識者咸怪之。

translations.literal: Sun Hao wished to surrender and sent the Son of Heaven's seal and cord — bypassing the two nearby generals yet sending them from afar to Zhou; those who understood all found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao wished to surrender and sent the imperial seal and cord — bypassing the two nearby generals yet dispatching them from afar to Zhou. Those in the know all found it strange.

sentences.zh: 吳之未亡也，吳郡臨平湖一旦自開，湖邊得石函，中有小青石，刻作皇帝字。

translations.literal: Before Wu's fall, Linping Lake in Wu Commandery opened of itself in a single day; by the lakeside a stone casket was obtained, inside which was a small green stone carved with the character for emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wu fell, Linping Lake in Wu Commandery opened overnight. By the shore a stone casket was found containing a small green stone carved with the character for emperor.

sentences.zh: 舊言臨平湖塞天下亂，開則天下太平。

translations.literal: Old lore says when Linping Lake is blocked, all under Heaven falls into chaos; when it opens, all under Heaven finds great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Old lore held that when Linping Lake is blocked, the realm falls into chaos; when it opens, the realm finds great peace.

sentences.zh: 吳人以為美祥。

translations.literal: The people of Wu took it as a beautiful auspice.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu took it for a splendid omen.

sentences.zh: 俄而吳滅。

translations.literal: Before long Wu was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wu fell.

sentences.zh: 後元帝興於江左。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Yuan rose in the lands east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Yuan rose in the lands east of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 吳亡後，蔣山上常有紫雲，數術者亦云，江東猶有帝王氣。

translations.literal: After Wu's fall, on Mount Jiang purple clouds often appeared; numerologists also said the lands east of the river still had the qi of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell, purple clouds often appeared on Mount Jiang. Numerologists also declared that the lands east of the Yangzi still bore the aura of imperial destiny.

sentences.zh: 又謠言曰：「五馬游度江，一馬化為龍。

translations.literal: A ballad also said: "Five horses roam crossing the river; one horse transforms into a dragon.
translations.idiomatic: A ballad also ran: "Five horses roam across the river; one horse transforms into a dragon.

sentences.zh: 」元帝與西陽、汝南、南頓、彭城五王過江，而元帝升天位。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yuan crossed the river together with the five princes of Xiyang, Runan, Nandun, and Pengcheng — and Emperor Yuan ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Yuan crossed the river together with the princes of Xiyang, Runan, Nandun, and Pengcheng — five in all — and it was Emperor Yuan who ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 讖書曰：「銅馬入海建業期。

translations.literal: A prophecy book said: "The bronze horse enters the sea at Jianye — the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: A prophecy book said, "The bronze horse enters the sea at Jianye — the appointed hour has come.

sentences.zh: 」元帝小字銅環。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yuan's childhood name was Bronze Ring.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Yuan's childhood name was Bronze Ring.

sentences.zh: 〈元帝小字銅環　張森楷校勘記云：「晉書后妃傳言元帝母夏侯氏小字銅環，此直以為元帝。」〉

translations.literal: 〈On "Emperor Yuan's childhood name Bronze Ring": Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "The biography of empresses and consorts in the History of Jin states that Emperor Yuan's mother Lady Xiahou had the childhood name Bronze Ring; here it is applied directly to Emperor Yuan."〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Collation note on "Emperor Yuan's childhood name Bronze Ring": Zhang Senkai observes that the biography of empresses and consorts in the History of Jin gives the childhood name Bronze Ring to Emperor Yuan's mother Lady Xiahou, whereas here it is applied directly to Emperor Yuan himself.〉

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，元帝以安東將軍鎮建業，時歲、鎮星、辰、太白四星聚於牛、女之間，常裴回進退。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongjia, Emperor Yuan as Eastern Tranquilizing General garrisoned Jianye. At the time, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, and Venus — four stars — gathered between the Ox and Girl lodges, often lingering and advancing and retreating.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongjia, as Eastern Tranquilizing General Emperor Yuan garrisoned Jianye. Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, and Venus gathered between the Ox and Girl lodges, lingering and shifting back and forth.

sentences.zh: 愍帝建興四年，晉陵武進人陳龍在田中得銅鐸五枚，柄口皆有龍虎形；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianxing under Emperor Min, Chen Long of Wujin in Jinling obtained five bronze bells in his fields; their handles and mouths all bore dragon and tiger forms;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianxing under Emperor Min, Chen Long of Wujin in Jinling found five bronze bells in his fields, each handle and mouth wrought with dragon and tiger forms;

sentences.zh: 又有將雛雞雀集其前，皆驅去復還，至于再三；

translations.literal: also chicks about to hatch and young chickens and sparrows gathered before them — all were driven away yet returned, even to two or three times;
translations.idiomatic: chicks about to hatch, young chickens, and sparrows gathered before them — driven away they returned again and again;

sentences.zh: 又有鵝三四頭，高飛且鳴，周回東西，晝夜不下，如此者六七日。

translations.literal: also three or four geese, flying high and calling, circling east and west, not descending day or night — thus for six or seven days.
translations.idiomatic: three or four geese flew high, crying, circling east and west without descending day or night — for six or seven days running.

sentences.zh: 會稽剡縣陳清又於井中得棧鐘，長七寸二分，口徑四寸，其器雖小，形制甚精，上有古文書十八字，其四字可識，云：「會稽徽命。

translations.literal: Chen Qing of Shan County in Kuaiji also obtained a stacked bell from a well — length seven cun two fen, mouth diameter four cun; though the vessel was small, its form was very fine; above were eighteen characters in ancient script, four of which could be read, saying: "Kuaiji mandate emblem.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qing of Shan County in Kuaiji also retrieved a stacked bell from a well — seven cun two fen long, four cun across the mouth. Small though the vessel was, its craftsmanship was exquisite. Eighteen characters in ancient script adorned it; four could be made out: "Kuaiji mandate emblem.

sentences.zh: 」豫章有大樟樹，大三十五圍，枯死積久，永嘉中，忽更榮茂。

translations.literal: " In Yuzhang there was a great camphor tree, thirty-five arm-spans around; long dead and withered, yet in the Yongjia era it suddenly flourished anew.
translations.idiomatic: " In Yuzhang stood a great camphor tree thirty-five arm-spans around. Long dead and withered, it suddenly put forth luxuriant growth during the Yongjia era.

sentences.zh: 景純並言是元帝中興之應。

translations.literal: Jing Chun all said these were tokens of Emperor Yuan's restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Chun declared all of these omens foretold Emperor Yuan's restoration.

sentences.zh: 初武帝太康三年，建鄴有寇，餘姚人伍振筮之，曰：「寇已滅矣。

translations.literal: Earlier in the third year of Taikang under Emperor Wu, Jianye had bandits; Wu Zhen of Yuyao divined by the Book of Changes and said: "The bandits are already destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the third year of Taikang under Emperor Wu, bandits raided Jianye. Wu Zhen of Yuyao divined by the Book of Changes and said, "The bandits are already destroyed.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，揚州有天子。

translations.literal: In thirty-eight years, Yang Province will have a Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In thirty-eight years, Yang Province will have a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」至元帝即天位，果三十八年。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Yuan took the throne, it was indeed thirty-eight years.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Yuan took the throne, it was exactly thirty-eight years.

sentences.zh: 先是，宣帝有寵將牛金，屢有功，宣帝作兩口榼，一口盛毒酒，一口盛善酒，自飲善酒，毒酒與金，金飲之即斃。

translations.literal: Before this, the Founding Emperor had a favored general Niu Jin who had repeatedly won merit. The Founding Emperor made two flasks — one holding poisoned wine, one holding good wine; he himself drank the good wine and gave the poisoned wine to Jin; Jin drank it and immediately died.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the Founding Emperor had a favored general, Niu Jin, who had won repeated victories. The Founding Emperor prepared two flasks — one with poisoned wine, one with good wine. He drank the good wine himself and gave the poisoned wine to Jin, who drank it and immediately died.

sentences.zh: 景帝曰：「金名將，可大用，云何害之？

translations.literal: Emperor Jing said: "Jin is a renowned general, fit for great employment — why harm him?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing protested, "Jin is a renowned general, fit for great service — why would you harm him?

sentences.zh: 」宣帝曰：「汝忘石瑞，馬後有牛乎？

translations.literal: " The Founding Emperor said: "Have you forgotten the stone omen — after the horse comes the ox?
translations.idiomatic: " The Founding Emperor replied, "Have you forgotten the stone omen? After the horse comes the ox.

sentences.zh: 」元帝母夏侯妃與琅邪國小史姓牛私通，而生元帝。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yuan's mother, Consort Xiahou, had a secret liaison with a petty clerk of Langya Principality surnamed Niu, and bore Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Yuan's mother, Consort Xiahou, had a secret liaison with a petty clerk of Langya Principality surnamed Niu — and bore Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 愍帝之立也，改毗陵為晉陵，時元帝始霸江、揚，而戎翟稱制，西都微弱。
