translations.literal: When Emperor Min was established, Piling was renamed Jinling. At the time Emperor Yuan was first hegemon over Jiang and Yang, while barbarian tribes held power and the western capital grew weak.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min was enthroned, Piling was renamed Jinling. Emperor Yuan was then first establishing hegemony over the Jiang and Yang regions, while barbarian tribes held sway and the western capital waned.

sentences.zh: 干寶以為晉將滅於西而興於東之符也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao held this to be the token that Jin would perish in the west and rise in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao held this to be proof that Jin would perish in the west and rise in the east.

sentences.zh: 宋

translations.literal: Song
translations.idiomatic: Song

sentences.zh: 宋武帝居在丹徒，始生之夜，有神光照室，其夕，甘露降于墓樹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song dwelt in Dantu; on the night of his birth divine light illuminated the chamber; that evening sweet dew fell on the tomb-tree.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song dwelt in Dantu. On the night of his birth, divine light filled the chamber, and that evening sweet dew fell upon the tomb-tree.

sentences.zh: 皇考以高祖生有奇異，名為奇奴。

translations.literal: His Imperial Father, seeing that the High Ancestor's birth had marvels, named him Qinu.
translations.idiomatic: His Imperial Father, seeing that the High Ancestor's birth was marked by marvels, named him Qinu.

sentences.zh: 皇妣既殂，養於舅氏，改為寄奴焉。

translations.literal: After His Imperial Mother died, he was raised by his mother's clan and his name was changed to Jinu.
translations.idiomatic: After His Imperial Mother died, he was raised by his mother's clan and given the name Jinu.

sentences.zh: 少時誕節嗜酒，自京都還，息於逆旅。

translations.literal: In youth he had an unusual temperament and loved wine; returning from the capital he rested at a traveler's inn.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was singular in temperament and fond of wine. Returning from the capital, he rested at a traveler's inn.

sentences.zh: 逆旅嫗曰：「室內有酒，自入取之。

translations.literal: The innkeeper's wife said: "There is wine indoors — enter and take it yourself.
translations.idiomatic: The innkeeper's wife said, "There is wine inside — help yourself.

sentences.zh: 」帝入室，飲於盎側，醉臥地。

translations.literal: " The Emperor entered the chamber, drank by the side of a bowl, and drunkenly slept on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor entered, drank beside a wine jar, and fell drunk to the floor.

sentences.zh: 時司徒王謐有門生居在丹徒，還家，亦至此逆旅。

translations.literal: At the time a disciple of Minister over the Masses Wang Mi lived in Dantu; returning home, he also came to this inn.
translations.idiomatic: A disciple of Minister over the Masses Wang Mi, who lived in Dantu, was also returning home and stopped at the same inn.

sentences.zh: 逆旅嫗曰：「劉郎在室內，可入共飲酒。

translations.literal: The innkeeper's wife said: "Young Liu is indoors — you may enter and drink together.
translations.idiomatic: The innkeeper's wife said, "Young Liu is inside — you may go in and share a drink.

sentences.zh: 」此門生入室，驚出謂嫗曰：「室內那得此異物？

translations.literal: " This disciple entered the chamber, fled out in alarm, and said to the wife: "How can there be such a strange thing indoors?
translations.idiomatic: " The disciple entered — then fled in alarm and said to the innkeeper, "What is this uncanny thing in the room?

sentences.zh: 」嫗遽入之，見帝已覺矣。

translations.literal: " The wife hurried in and saw the Emperor already awake.
translations.idiomatic: " The innkeeper rushed inside and found the Emperor already awake.

sentences.zh: 嫗密問：「向何所見？

translations.literal: The wife asked secretly: "What did you see just now?
translations.idiomatic: She asked him quietly, "What did you see just now?

sentences.zh: 」門生曰：「見有一物，五采如蛟龍，非劉郎。

translations.literal: " The disciple said: "I saw a thing, five-colored like a horned dragon — it was not Young Liu.
translations.idiomatic: " The disciple answered, "I saw a being, five-colored like a horned dragon — that was no mere Young Liu.

sentences.zh: 」門生還以白謐，謐戒使勿言，而與結厚。

translations.literal: " The disciple returned and told Mi; Mi warned him not to speak of it and formed a deep bond with him.
translations.idiomatic: " The disciple reported this to Mi, who cautioned him to say nothing — and thereafter formed a deep bond with the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗行至下邳，遇一沙門，沙門曰：「江表尋當喪亂，拯之必君也。

translations.literal: The Emperor once traveled to Xiapi and met a Buddhist monk who said: "The lands south of the river will soon fall into chaos — he who saves them must be you.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once traveled to Xiapi and met a Buddhist monk who said, "The lands south of the Yangzi will soon be plunged into chaos — you alone can save them.

sentences.zh: 」帝患手創積年，沙門出懷中黃散一裹與帝曰：「此創難治，非此藥不能瘳也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor suffered from a hand wound for many years. The monk took from his bosom one packet of yellow powder and gave it to the Emperor, saying: "This wound is hard to cure — without this medicine it cannot be healed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor had suffered from a hand wound for years. The monk drew from his robe a packet of yellow powder and said, "This wound is hard to heal — without this medicine it cannot be cured.

sentences.zh: 」倏忽不見沙門所在。

translations.literal: " In an instant the monk could no longer be seen.
translations.idiomatic: " In an instant the monk had vanished.

sentences.zh: 以散傅創即愈。

translations.literal: Applying the powder to the wound, it immediately healed.
translations.idiomatic: He applied the powder to the wound and it healed at once.

sentences.zh: 餘散帝寶錄之，後征伐屢被傷，通中者數矣，以散傅之，無不立愈。

translations.literal: The Emperor treasured and recorded the remaining powder; afterward in campaigns he was often wounded — several times pierced through — applying the powder, none failed to heal immediately.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor treasured the remaining powder and kept it safe. In later campaigns he was wounded again and again — pierced through the body several times — yet each time the powder healed him instantly.

sentences.zh: 自少至長，目中常見二龍在前，始尚小，及貴轉大。

translations.literal: From youth to age, he constantly saw two dragons before his eyes — at first still small, and as he rose in rank they grew large.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age he constantly saw two dragons before his eyes — small at first, growing larger as he rose in power.

sentences.zh: 晉陵人車藪善相人，

translations.literal: Che Su of Jinling was skilled at reading faces,
translations.idiomatic: Che Su of Jinling was skilled at reading faces,

sentences.zh: 〈晉陵人車藪善相人　「車藪」藝文類聚一三引徐爰宋書作「韋藪」。

translations.literal: 〈On "Che Su of Jinling was skilled at reading faces": for "Che Su", the Essentials of Literature, juan 13, citing Xu Yue's Book of Song reads "Wei Su".
translations.idiomatic: 〈Collation note on "Che Su of Jinling was skilled at reading faces": "Che Su" appears as "Wei Su" in juan 13 of the Essentials of Literature, citing Xu Yue's Book of Song.

sentences.zh: 御覽一二八引徐爰宋書、御覽七三０引宋書高祖紀作「韋叟」。〉

translations.literal: Imperial Readings, juan 128 citing Xu Yue's Book of Song, and Imperial Readings, juan 730 citing the Basic Annals of the High Ancestor in the Book of Song read "Wei Sou".〉
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Readings, juan 128 citing Xu Yue's Book of Song, and Imperial Readings, juan 730 citing the Basic Annals of the High Ancestor in the Book of Song read "Wei Sou".〉

sentences.zh: 相帝曰：「君貴不可言，願無相忘。」

translations.literal: Reading the Emperor's face he said: "Your nobility is beyond words — please do not forget me."
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Emperor's face, he said, "Your nobility is beyond reckoning — promise you will not forget me."

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙初，帝始康晉亂，而興霸業焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, the Emperor first restored order amid Jin's chaos and raised a hegemonic enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yixi era under Emperor An of Jin, the Emperor first restored order amid Jin's chaos and began his rise to power.

sentences.zh: 廬江霍山常有鐘聲十二。

translations.literal: On Mount Huo in Lujiang, twelve bell-sounds were often heard.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Huo in Lujiang, the sound of twelve bells was often heard.

sentences.zh: 帝將征關、洛，霍山崩，有六鐘出，制度精奇，上有古文書一百六十字。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to campaign against Guan and Luo, Mount Huo collapsed; six bells emerged, exquisitely wrought, bearing one hundred sixty characters in ancient script above.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor prepared to campaign toward Guan and Luoyang, Mount Huo collapsed. Six bells emerged, exquisitely wrought, bearing one hundred sixty characters in ancient script.

sentences.zh: 冀州有沙門法稱將死，語其弟子普嚴曰：「嵩皇神告我云，江東有劉將軍，是漢家苗裔，當受天命。

translations.literal: In Ji Province a monk Fasheng was about to die; he told his disciple Puyan: "The god of Songgao told me that east of the river there is General Liu of the Han lineage, who is to receive Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: In Ji Province, the monk Fasheng lay dying. He told his disciple Puyan, "The god of Mount Song told me that east of the Yangzi is General Liu, a scion of the house of Han, who is destined to receive Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 吾以三十二璧，鎮金一餅，與將軍為信。

translations.literal: I entrust thirty-two jade discs and one ingot of girding gold to the general as credentials.
translations.idiomatic: I leave thirty-two jade discs and one ingot of protective gold as credentials for the general.

sentences.zh: 三十二璧者，劉氏卜世之數也。

translations.literal: The thirty-two discs are the number by which the Liu clan's fortune in the world is divined.
translations.idiomatic: The thirty-two discs signify the number of generations allotted to the house of Liu.

sentences.zh: 」普嚴以告同學法義。

translations.literal: " Puyan told his fellow disciple Fayi.
translations.idiomatic: " Puyan relayed this to his fellow disciple Fayi.

sentences.zh: 法義以十三年七月，於嵩高廟石壇下得玉璧三十二枚，黃金一餅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year Fayi obtained thirty-two jade discs and one ingot of gold beneath the stone altar at the Songgao temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year, Fayi found thirty-two jade discs and one ingot of gold beneath the stone altar at the Mount Song temple.

sentences.zh: 漢中城固縣水際，忽有雷聲，俄而岸崩，得銅鐘十二枚。

translations.literal: At the waterside in Chenggu County, Hanzhong, thunder suddenly sounded; soon the bank collapsed and twelve bronze bells were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: At the water's edge in Chenggu County, Hanzhong, thunder suddenly pealed. The bank collapsed, and twelve bronze bells were found.

sentences.zh: 又鞏縣民宋燿得嘉禾九穗。

translations.literal: Again, a commoner of Gong County named Song Yao obtained fine grain with nine ears.
translations.idiomatic: Again, a commoner of Gong County named Song Yao found an ear of fine grain bearing nine stalks.

sentences.zh: 後二年而受晉禪。

translations.literal: Two years later he received Jin's abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he received the abdication of Jin.

sentences.zh: 孔子河雒讖曰：「二口建戈不能方，兩金相刻發神鋒，空穴無主奇入中，女子獨立又為雙。

translations.literal: The Confucius River-Luo prophecy says: "Two mouths building a halberd cannot be square; two metals carving each other unleash divine edge; an empty cave without master — odd enters the middle; a woman standing alone again becomes double."
translations.idiomatic: The Confucius River-Luo prophecy says, "Two mouths building a halberd cannot be square; two metals carving each other unleash a divine edge; an empty cave without a master — the odd enters the middle; a woman standing alone again becomes double."

sentences.zh: 」二口建戈，「劉」字也。

translations.literal: " Two mouths building a halberd — the character for the Liu surname.
translations.idiomatic: " "Two mouths building a halberd" denotes the character for the Liu surname.

sentences.zh: 晉氏金行，劉姓又有金，故曰兩金相刻。

translations.literal: The Jin clan followed the Metal phase; the Liu surname also contains metal — hence "two metals carving each other."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin house followed the Metal phase, and the Liu surname also contains the metal element — hence "two metals carving each other."

sentences.zh: 空穴無主奇入中，為「寄」字。

translations.literal: Empty cave without master, odd enters the middle — the character for "to lodge."
translations.idiomatic: "An empty cave without a master, with the odd entering the middle" forms the character meaning "to lodge."

sentences.zh: 女子獨立又為雙，「奴」字。

translations.literal: Woman standing alone again becomes double — the character for "servant."
translations.idiomatic: "A woman standing alone that again becomes double" forms the character for "servant."

sentences.zh: 晉既禪宋，太史令駱達奏陳天文符讖曰：:去義熙元年，至元熙元年十月，太白星晝見經天凡七。

translations.literal: After Jin had abdicated to Song, Grand Astrologer Luo Da submitted a memorial reporting astronomical tokens and prophecies, saying: From the first year of Yixi to the tenth month of the first year of Yuanxi, Venus was seen in daytime traversing the heavens — seven times in all.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin had abdicated to Song, Grand Astrologer Luo Da submitted a memorial on heavenly signs and prophecies: From the first year of Yixi through the tenth month of the first year of Yuanxi, Venus appeared in daylight crossing the heavens seven times in all.

sentences.zh: 占曰：『天下革民更王，異姓興。

translations.literal: The divination reads: "When the realm is reformed the people change their king; a different surname rises.
translations.idiomatic: The divination reads, "When the realm is reformed the people change kings; a house of different surname rises.

sentences.zh: 』義熙元年至元熙元年十一月朔，日有蝕之凡四，皆蝕從上始，臣民失君之象也。

translations.literal: " From the first year of Yixi to the new moon of the eleventh month of the first year of Yuanxi, solar eclipses occurred four times in all — all beginning from the top; an image of ministers and people losing their lord.
translations.idiomatic: " From the first year of Yixi through the new moon of the eleventh month of the first year of Yuanxi there were four solar eclipses, all beginning from the top — a sign that subjects had lost their ruler.

sentences.zh: :義熙十一年五月三日，彗星出天市，其芒掃帝坐。

translations.literal: On the third day of the fifth month in the eleventh year of Yixi, a comet emerged from the Celestial Market; its rays swept the Imperial Seat.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the fifth month in the eleventh year of Yixi, a comet emerged from the Celestial Market, its tail sweeping the Imperial Seat.

sentences.zh: 天市在房、心之北，宋之分野。

translations.literal: The Celestial Market lies north of the Fang and Heart lodges — Song's sky division.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Market lies north of the Fang and Heart lodges — the celestial division of Song.

sentences.zh: 得彗柄者興，此除舊布新之徵。

translations.literal: He who obtains the comet's handle rises; this is a token of clearing out the old and spreading the new.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever obtains the comet's handle will rise — a sign of clearing out the old and ushering in the new.

sentences.zh: :義熙七年七月二十五日，五虹見于東方。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month in the seventh year of Yixi, five rainbows appeared in the east.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month in the seventh year of Yixi, five rainbows appeared in the east.

sentences.zh: 占曰：『五虹見，天子黜，聖人出。

translations.literal: The divination reads: "When five rainbows appear, the Son of Heaven is deposed; a sage emerges.
translations.idiomatic: The divination reads, "When five rainbows appear, the Son of Heaven is deposed and a sage emerges.

sentences.zh: 』:義熙七年八月十一日，新天子氣見東南。

translations.literal: " On the eleventh day of the eighth month in the seventh year of Yixi, the new emperor's qi appeared in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: " On the eleventh day of the eighth month in the seventh year of Yixi, the qi of a new emperor appeared in the southeast.

sentences.zh: :十二年，北定中原，崇進宋公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the north was pacified and the Central Plains secured; the Duke of Song was elevated in honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the north was pacified and the Central Plains secured, and the Duke of Song was elevated in rank.

sentences.zh: 歲星裴回房、心之間，大火，宋之分野。

translations.literal: The Year Star lingered between the Fang and Heart lodges — Great Fire — Song's sky division.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter lingered between the Fang and Heart lodges, at Antares — the celestial division of Song.

sentences.zh: 與武王克殷同，得歲星之分者應王也。

translations.literal: The same as when the Martial King conquered Yin — he who obtains the Year Star's division corresponds to kingship.
translations.idiomatic: As when the Martial King conquered Yin — he who holds Jupiter's division is destined for kingship.

sentences.zh: :十一年以來至元熙元年，月行失道，恒北入太微中。

translations.literal: From the eleventh year onward through the first year of Yuanxi, the moon's course deviated, constantly entering the Supreme Palace Enclosure from the north.
translations.idiomatic: From the eleventh year through the first year of Yuanxi, the moon's course went astray, repeatedly entering the Supreme Palace Enclosure from the north.

sentences.zh: 占：『月入太微廷，王入為主。

translations.literal: The divination: "When the moon enters the Supreme Palace court, a prince enters as master.
translations.idiomatic: The divination reads, "When the moon enters the court of the Supreme Palace Enclosure, a prince enters to become master.

sentences.zh: 』:十三年十月，鎮星入太微，積留七十餘日，到十四年八月十日，又入太微不去，到元熙元年，積二百餘日。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month of the thirteenth year the Stationary Star entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure and accumulated a stay of more than seventy days; reaching the tenth day of the eighth month of the fourteenth year it entered again and did not depart; by the first year of Yuanxi it had accumulated more than two hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth month of the thirteenth year Saturn entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure and remained for more than seventy days; by the tenth day of the eighth month of the fourteenth year it entered again and did not leave; by the first year of Yuanxi it had lingered there for more than two hundred days.

sentences.zh: 占：『鎮星守太微，亡君之戒。

translations.literal: The divination: "When the Stationary Star guards the Supreme Palace Enclosure — warning of a perished lord.
translations.idiomatic: The divination reads, "When Saturn guards the Supreme Palace Enclosure — a warning that the ruler will perish.

sentences.zh: 有立王，有徙王。

translations.literal: There is enthronement of a king; there is removal of a king.
translations.idiomatic: One sign foretells the enthronement of a king; another foretells a king's removal.

sentences.zh: 』:十四年五月十七日，茀星出北斗魁中。

translations.literal: " On the seventeenth day of the fifth month of the fourteenth year the Broom Star emerged from the boss of the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: " On the seventeenth day of the fifth month of the fourteenth year the Broom Star emerged from the boss of the Northern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 占曰：『星茀北斗中，聖人受命。

translations.literal: The divination reads: "When a bushy star appears in the Northern Dipper — a sage receives the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The divination reads, "When a bushy star appears in the Northern Dipper, a sage receives the mandate.

sentences.zh: 』:十四年七月二十九日，彗星出太微中，彗柄起上相星下，芒尾漸長至十餘丈，進掃北斗及紫微中。

translations.literal: " On the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month of the fourteenth year a comet emerged from the Supreme Palace Enclosure; the comet's handle rose below the Upper Minister Star, its ray and tail gradually lengthening to more than ten zhang, advancing to sweep the Northern Dipper and the center of the Purple Forbidden Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: " On the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month of the fourteenth year a comet emerged from the Supreme Palace Enclosure. Its handle rose below the Upper Minister Star, its tail gradually lengthening to more than ten zhang as it swept through the Northern Dipper and the heart of the Purple Forbidden Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 占曰：『彗星出太微，社稷亡，天下易政。

translations.literal: The divination reads: "When a comet emerges from the Supreme Palace Enclosure — the state altars perish, the realm's governance changes.
translations.idiomatic: The divination reads, "When a comet emerges from the Supreme Palace Enclosure, the state altars perish and governance of the realm changes hands.

sentences.zh: 入北斗，帝宮空。

translations.literal: Entering the Northern Dipper — the emperor's palace stands empty.
translations.idiomatic: If it enters the Northern Dipper, the emperor's palace stands empty.

sentences.zh: 』一占：『天下得召人。

translations.literal: " Another divination: "Under Heaven obtains a Summon-Person.
translations.idiomatic: " Another divination reads, "Under Heaven will obtain a Summon-Person.

sentences.zh: 』召人，聖主也。

translations.literal: " Summon-Person — a sage lord.
translations.idiomatic: " "Summon-Person" means a sage ruler.

sentences.zh: 一曰：『彗孛紫微，天下易主。

translations.literal: One version says: "When comet and broom star enter the Purple Forbidden Enclosure — the realm's master changes.
translations.idiomatic: One version reads, "When comet and broom star enter the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, the realm's master changes.

sentences.zh: 』:十四年十月一日，熒惑從入太微鉤己，至元年四月二十七日，從端門出積屍，留二百六日，繞鎮星。

translations.literal: " On the first day of the tenth month of the fourteenth year Mars followed in, entering the Supreme Palace Enclosure in hook-shaped retrograde; reaching the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month of the first year it exited from the End Gate through Accumulated Corpses, remaining two hundred six days, circling the Stationary Star.
translations.idiomatic: " On the first day of the tenth month of the fourteenth year Mars followed in, entering the Supreme Palace Enclosure in hook-shaped retrograde. By the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month of the first year it exited through the End Gate at Accumulated Corpses, remaining two hundred six days while circling Saturn.

sentences.zh: 熒惑與鎮星鉤己天廷，天下更紀。

translations.literal: Mars and the Stationary Star in hook-shaped retrograde in the celestial court — the realm changes its era.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars and Saturn form hook-shaped retrograde loops in the celestial court, the realm changes its era.

sentences.zh: :十四年十二月，歲、太白、辰裴回居斗、牛之間經旬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year, Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury lingered between the Dipper and Ox lodges for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year, Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury lingered between the Dipper and Ox lodges for some ten days.

sentences.zh: 斗、牛，曆數之起。

translations.literal: The Dipper and Ox — where the calendar's reckoning begins.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper and the Ox — the lodges where a dynasty's reckoning begins.

sentences.zh: 占曰：『三星合，是謂改立。

translations.literal: The divination reads: "When three stars unite — this is called changing the enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: The divination reads, "When three stars converge, it is called changing the enthronement.

sentences.zh: 』:元熙元年十二月二十四日，四黑龍登天。

translations.literal: " On the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month of the first year of Yuanxi, four black dragons ascended to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " On the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month of the first year of Yuanxi, four black dragons ascended into Heaven.

sentences.zh: 易傳曰：『冬龍見，天子亡社稷，大人應天命之符。

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Changes says: "When dragons appear in winter — the Son of Heaven loses the state altars; the great man responds to Heaven's mandate token.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Changes says, "When dragons appear in winter, the Son of Heaven loses the state altars and the great man responds to the token of Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 』:金雌詩云：『大火有心水抱之，悠悠百年是其時。

translations.literal: " The Golden Hen Poem says: "Great Fire has a heart; water embraces it — leisurely, a hundred years is its time.
translations.idiomatic: " The Golden Hen Poem says, "Great Fire has a heart and water embraces it — in the fullness of a hundred years, the time arrives.

sentences.zh: 』火，宋之分野。

translations.literal: " Fire — Song's sky division.
translations.idiomatic: " Fire is Song's celestial division.

sentences.zh: 水，宋之德也。

translations.literal: Water — Song's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Water is Song's dynastic virtue.

sentences.zh: :金雌詩又曰：『云出而兩漸欲舉，短如之何乃相岨，交哉亂也當何所，唯有隱巖殖禾黍，西南之朋困桓父。

translations.literal: The Golden Hen Poem also says: "Cloud emerges and two gradually wish to rise; short — how can they face the steep? Crossed — alas the chaos, where shall it go? Only the hidden cliff planting millet and panic grass; southwest companion traps Huan the father."
translations.idiomatic: The Golden Hen Poem also says, "Cloud emerges and two gradually wish to rise; shortened — how can they scale the steep? Chaos intersects — where shall it lead? Only at the hidden cliff, planting millet; the southwest companion ensnares the Huan father."

sentences.zh: 』兩云，「玄」字也。

translations.literal: " Two clouds — the character Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: " "Two clouds" forms the character Xuan.

sentences.zh: 短者，云胙短也。

translations.literal: The short one — the cloud's lower portion is short.
translations.idiomatic: "Short" refers to the shortened lower portion of the cloud character.

sentences.zh: 巖隱不見，唯應見谷，殖禾谷邊，則聖諱炳明也。

translations.literal: When the cliff is hidden and not seen, only the valley should appear; millet planted beside the valley — then the sage's taboo name shines clear.
translations.idiomatic: When the cliff is concealed from view and only the valley appears, with grain planted beside the valley — then the sage emperor's taboo name stands radiant and clear.

sentences.zh: 易曰：『西南得朋。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "In the southwest one obtains companions.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "In the southwest one obtains companions.

sentences.zh: 』故能困桓父也。

translations.literal: " Therefore one can trap Huan the father.
translations.idiomatic: " Hence one can ensnare Huan the Father.

sentences.zh: :劉向讖曰：『上五盡寄致太平，草付合成集羣英。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's prophecy says: "The upper five entirely lodge, bringing great peace; grass entrusted combined gathers the host of worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's prophecy says, "The upper five entirely lodge, bringing great peace; grass entrusted and combined gathers the host of worthies.

sentences.zh: 』前句則陛下小諱，後句則太子諱也。

translations.literal: " The former line is Your Majesty's childhood taboo name; the latter line is the Crown Prince's taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: " The first line encodes Your Majesty's childhood taboo name; the second line encodes the Crown Prince's taboo name.

sentences.zh: :十一年五月，西明門地陷，水涌出，毀門扉閾。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year the ground at the Western Bright Gate collapsed; water gushed forth, destroying the gate panels and threshold.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eleventh year the ground subsided at the Western Bright Gate; water burst forth and destroyed the gate panels and threshold.

sentences.zh: 西者，金鄉之門，為水所毀，此金德將衰，水德方興之象也。

translations.literal: The west is the gate of the Metal district; destroyed by water — this is an image of Metal Virtue about to decline and Water Virtue rising.
translations.idiomatic: The west is the gate of the Metal quarter; destroyed by water — a sign that Metal Virtue is waning and Water Virtue is rising.

sentences.zh: :太興中，民於井中得棧鐘，上有古文十八字，晉自宣帝至今，數滿十八傳。

translations.literal: During Taixing, a commoner obtained a stacked bell from a well; upon it were eighteen characters in ancient script — from Jin's Emperor Xuan to the present the count fills eighteen successions.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taixing era, a commoner found a layered bell in a well bearing eighteen characters in ancient script — from Jin's Emperor Xuan to the present the tally reaches eighteen transmissions.

sentences.zh: 義熙八年，太社生桑，尤著明者也。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi mulberry sprouted on the Grand Earth Altar — the most conspicuous sign of all.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yixi mulberry grew upon the Grand Earth Altar — the most conspicuous omen of all.

sentences.zh: 夫六，亢位也。

translations.literal: As for six — it is the Kang position.
translations.idiomatic: Six is the Kang position.

sentences.zh: 漢建安二十五年，一百九十六年而禪魏。

translations.literal: Han — twenty-fifth year of Jian'an; after one hundred ninety-six years the throne was yielded to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: From the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an, Han ruled one hundred ninety-six years before yielding the throne to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏自黃初至咸熙二年，四十六年而禪晉。

translations.literal: Wei — from Huangchu to the second year of Xianxi, forty-six years, then yielded the throne to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruled from Huangchu through the second year of Xianxi — forty-six years — before yielding the throne to Jin.

sentences.zh: 晉自泰始至今元熙二年，一百五十六年。

translations.literal: Jin — from Taishi to the present second year of Yuanxi, one hundred fifty-six years.
translations.idiomatic: Jin has ruled from Taishi to the present second year of Yuanxi — one hundred fifty-six years.

sentences.zh: 三代數窮，咸以六年。

translations.literal: The three dynasties when their numbers were exhausted — all ended in the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: When the three dynasties exhausted their allotted spans, each ended in a sixth year.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，景平三年四月，有五色雲見西方。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shao ascended the throne, in the fourth month of the third year of Jingping, five-colored clouds appeared in the west.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shao ascended the throne, in the fourth month of the third year of Jingping five-colored clouds appeared in the west.

sentences.zh: 時文帝為荊州刺史，鎮江陵，尋即大位。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wen was Governor of Jingzhou, garrisoned at Jiangling; soon he assumed the supreme position.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Wen was Governor of Jingzhou, holding Jiangling — and soon thereafter ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉中，謠言錢唐當出天子，乃於錢唐置戍軍以防之。

translations.literal: During Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, a rumor spread that Qiantang would produce a Son of Heaven; they therefore stationed garrison troops at Qiantang to guard against it.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wen's Yuanjia reign, rumor held that Qiantang would produce a Son of Heaven, so garrison troops were posted at Qiantang to guard against it.

sentences.zh: 其後孝武帝即大位於新亭寺之禪堂。

translations.literal: Afterwards Emperor Xiaowu assumed the supreme position in the abdication hall of Xinting Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Afterwards Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne in the abdication hall of Xinting Temple.

sentences.zh: 「禪」之與「錢」，音相近也。

translations.literal: "Abdication" and "money" — their sounds are close.
translations.idiomatic: The word for "abdication" and the word for "Qian" sound nearly alike.

sentences.zh: 太宗為徐州刺史，出鎮彭城，昭太后賜以大珠鹿盧劍，此劍是御服，占者以為嘉祥。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong as Governor of Xuzhou went out to garrison Pengcheng; Empress Dowager Zhao bestowed the Great Pearl Deer-Reed Sword — this sword was imperial regalia; diviners took it as an auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong served as Governor of Xuzhou and went out to garrison Pengcheng, Empress Dowager Zhao bestowed upon him the Great Pearl Deer-Reed Sword. This sword was imperial regalia, and diviners regarded it as an auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝永光初，又譌言湘州出天子，幼主欲南幸湘川以厭之，既而湘東王即尊位，是為明帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongguang under the Former Deposed Emperor, another false rumor spread that Xiangzhou would produce a Son of Heaven. The young emperor wished to tour south to the Xiang River to suppress it; soon the Prince of Xiangdong assumed the exalted position — this was Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongguang under the Former Deposed Emperor, another false rumor held that Xiangzhou would produce a Son of Heaven. The young emperor planned a southern tour to the Xiang River to counter it — but soon the Prince of Xiangdong ascended the throne as Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 史臣謹按，冀州道人法稱所云玉璧三十二枚，宋氏卜世之數者，蓋卜年之數也。

translations.literal: The historiographer respectfully observes: the thirty-two jade discs spoken of by the Taoist Fachēng of Jizhou — the number by which Song's fortune in the world is divined — is in fact the number for divining years.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer observes that the thirty-two jade discs described by the Taoist Fachēng of Jizhou — said to foretell the number of Song generations — in fact foretell the number of years.

sentences.zh: 謂卜世者，謬其言耳。

translations.literal: To call it divining generations — that distorts the words.
translations.idiomatic: To speak of divining generations is to misread the prophecy.

sentences.zh: 三十二者，二三十，則六十矣。

translations.literal: As for thirty-two — two times thirty makes sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-two means two thirties — sixty in all.

sentences.zh: 宋氏受命至於禪齊，凡六十年云。

translations.literal: From Song's receiving the mandate until yielding to Qi — sixty years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the hour Song received the mandate until its abdication to Qi, sixty years passed in all.
